en: (1.1.1.1.a) For food thee, for strength thee!
(1.1.1.1.b) You are the winds; you are the up-breaths. (1.1.1.1.c) May the god Savitṛ impel you toward the most excellent work.
(1.1.1.1ḍ) Swell, O inviolable ones, as the portion of the gods; full of vigor, full of milk, rich in offspring, free from disease, and free from affliction.
(1.1.1.1.e) Let not the thief nor the malevolent one have power over you. (1.1.1.1.f) May the weapon of Rudra avoid you.
(1.1.1.1.g) May you be many and firm with this lord of cattle.
(1.1.1.1ḥ) Protect the livestock of the sacrificer.
(1.1.2.1.a) You are the proclaimer of the sacrifice. (1.1.2.1.b) Burnt away is the Rakṣas; burnt away are the enemies.

(1.1.2.1.c) This prayer has gone forth toward the sacrificial grass, fashioned by Manu and adorned with the Svadhā-call. The sages bring it from the east, this sacrificial grass dear to the gods, for them to sit upon here.
(1.1.2.1ḍ) You are gathered around by the gods;
(1.1.2.1.e) you are grown by rain;
(1.1.2.1.f) O divine sacrificial grass, do not pierce me from behind, nor across.
(1.1.2.1.g) May I prosper in your joint; may I, as the cutter, not be harmed.
(1.1.2.1.i) O divine sacrificial grass, grow with a hundred shoots! May we grow with a thousand shoots! (1.1.2.2) May we grow forth!
(1.1.2.2.k) Protect me from contact with the earth. (1.1.2.2ḷ) I gather you together, well-prepared. (1.1.2.2ṃ) You are the girdle for Aditi; you are the binding cord for Indrāṇī.
(1.1.2.2ṇ) May Pūṣan tie your knot; may it not loosen for you.
(1.1.2.2.o) With the two arms of Indra, I lift you up; with the head of Bṛhaspati, I carry you. (1.1.2.2.p) Proceed along the wide atmosphere.
(1.1.2.2.q) You are that which goes to the gods.
(1.1.3.1.a) Purify yourselves for the divine rite, for the sacrifice to the gods.
(1.1.3.1.b) You are the cauldron of Mātariśvan.
(1.1.3.1.c) You are heaven; you are earth.
(1.1.3.1ḍ) You are the sustainer of all, by the highest power.
(1.1.3.1.e) Be firm; do not falter.
(1.1.3.1.f) You are the purifier of the Vasus, with a hundred streams; you are the purifier of the Vasus, with a thousand streams.
(1.1.3.1.g) The drop is offered, the spark is offered.
(1.1.3.1.h) To Agni, the great, the firmament; *svāhā* to Heaven and Earth.
(1.1.3.1.k) She is all-life, she is all-expansive, she is all-action.
(1.1.3.1ḷ) Be united, O you who possess the cosmic order, you who are wavy and most rich in sweetness, you who are delightful for the winning of wealth.
(1.1.3.1ṃ) With Soma I stretch you out; I give you as curd to Indra.
(1.1.3.1ṇ) O Viṣṇu, protect the oblation!
(1.1.4.1.a) May I be able for you two, for the work, for the gods. (1.1.4.1.b) For the service, thee!
(1.1.4.1.c) Burnt away is the Rakṣas; burnt away are the enemies.
(1.1.4.1ḍ) You are the yoke-pole.
(1.1.4.1.e) Strike down, O striker; strike down him who strikes us down; strike him down whom we strike down.
(1.1.4.1.f) You are the most bountiful, the most fulfilling, the most beloved, the best bearer, the most excellent invoker of the gods among the gods.
(1.1.4.1.g) You are the unswerving vessel for the oblation.
(1.1.4.1.h) Be firm; do not waver. (1.1.4.1.i) I gaze upon you with the eye of Mitra.
(1.1.4.1.k) Do not fear, do not tremble; may I not harm you. (1.1.4.2ḷ) Wide open for the wind!
(1.1.4.2ṃ) At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan, I offer you, acceptable to Agni, and to Agni-Soma.
(1.1.4.2ṇ) This belongs to the gods, and this is ours together.
(1.1.4.2.o) For prosperity, not for misfortune, do I take you.
(1.1.4.2.p) May I behold the light of Vaiśvānara, the sun.
(1.1.4.2.q) May the doors of heaven and earth be made firm. (1.1.4.2ṛ) Proceed along the wide mid-region.
(1.1.4.2ṣ) I set thee down in the lap of Aditi.
O Agni, protect the oblation.
(1.1.5.1.a) May the divine Savitṛ purify you with a flawless strainer, with the rays of the Vasu Sūrya.

(1.1.5.1.b) O divine Waters, flowing forward, moving at the head, lead this sacrifice forward; place the lord of the sacrifice at the head. (1.1.5.1.c) Indra chose you for the slaying of Vṛtra; you chose Indra for the slaying of Vṛtra.
(1.1.5.1ḍ) You are sprinkled.
(1.1.5.1.e) I sprinkle you, acceptable to Agni, and to Agni and Soma.
(1.1.5.1.f) Be purified for the divine rite, for the sacrifice to the gods.
Shaken off is the Rakṣas, shaken off are the enemies.
You are the skin of Aditi; may the earth recognize you.
You are the wooden pressing-plate; may the skin of Aditi recognize you.
(1.1.5.2.k) You are the body of Agni, the release of speech. (1.1.5.2ḷ) I take you for the enjoyment of the gods. (1.1.5.2ṃ) You are the stone, belonging to the tree.
(1.1.5.2ṇ) Perform this oblation for the gods with perfect skill.
(1.1.5.2.o) Speak forth nourishment; speak forth vigor. (1.1.5.2.p) Speak with splendor.
(1.1.5.2.q) May we conquer the compact mass;
(1.1.5.2ṛ) thou art increased by rain;
(1.1.5.2ṣ) may that which is increased by rain receive thee.
(1.1.5.2ṭ) Blown away is the Rakṣas; blown away are the enemies.
(1.1.5.2.u) You are the portion of the Rakṣases.
(1.1.5.2.v) May Vāyu separate you!
May the god Savitṛ, the golden-handed, receive you.
(1.1.6.1.a) Shaken off is the Rakṣas, shaken off are the enemies.
(1.1.6.1.b) You are the skin of Aditi; may the earth recognize you.
(1.1.6.1.c) You are the pillar of heaven; may the skin of Aditi recognize you.
(1.1.6.1ḍ) You are Dhiṣaṇā, belonging to the mountains; may the Supporter of Heaven recognize you.
(1.1.6.1.e) You are Dhiṣaṇā, daughter of the mountain; may the Mountain recognize you.
(1.1.6.1.f) At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan, I shave you.
(1.1.6.1.g) You are grain; satisfy the gods. (1.1.6.1.h) For out-breath you, for in-breath you, for diffused breath you. (1.1.6.1.i) May I extend long along the reach of life.
May the god Savitṛ, the golden-handed, receive you.
(1.1.7.1.a) You are bold; bestow the sacred word (*brahman*). (1.1.7.1.b) O Agni, drive away the raw-eating fire; expel the flesh-eating fire; bring hither the fire that sacrifices to the gods.
(1.1.7.1.c) The *rakṣas* is burnt up; the enemies are burnt up.

(1.1.7.1ḍ) You are the firm one; steady the earth! Steady life! Steady offspring! Bring his kinsmen together for this sacrificer! (1.1.7.1.e) You are the supporter; steady the atmosphere! Steady the out-breath! Steady the in-breath! Bring his kinsmen together for this sacrificer! (1.1.7.1.f) You are the upholder; steady the sky! Steady the eye! Steady the ear! Bring his kinsmen together for this sacrificer!
(1.1.7.2.g) You are the law; make firm the quarters, make firm the womb, make firm the offspring; gather around for this sacrificer his kinsmen.
(1.1.7.2.h) You are piled; gather around for him offspring, for him wealth, for this sacrificer his kinsmen.
(1.1.7.2.i) By the fervor of the Bhṛgus and the Aṅgirases, be heated!
(1.1.7.2.k) Those potsherds which the wise arrange upon the cauldron—may Indra and Vāyu release them according to the ordinance of Pūṣan.
(1.1.8.1.a) I mix together.
(1.1.8.1.b) The waters have united with the waters, the plants with their sap. (1.1.8.1.c) O wealthy ones, flow together with the moving ones; the honey-sweet ones, with the honey-sweet ones.
(1.1.8.1ḍ) You have been produced from the waters; be united with the waters. (1.1.8.1.e) I mix you for the sake of generation.
(1.1.8.1.f) For Agni, for Agni and Soma, I [take] you.
(1.1.8.1.g) You are the head of Makha; (1.1.8.1.h) you are the Gharma, the life of all.
(1.1.8.1.i) Spread wide! May the lord of the sacrifice spread wide for you.
(1.1.8.1.k) Take up the skin! (1.1.8.1ḷ) The Rakṣas is excluded; the enemies are excluded!
(1.1.8.1ṃ) May the god Savitṛ cook thee upon the highest vault of heaven.
(1.1.8.1ṇ) May Agni not burn up your body.
(1.1.8.1.o) O Agni, protect the oblation. (1.1.8.1.p) Be united with the sacred prayer (*brahman*).
Hail to oneness! Hail to twoness! Hail to threeness!
(1.1.9.1.a) I take hold.
(1.1.9.1.b) You are the right arm of Indra, thousand-edged and hundred-fold radiant.
(1.1.9.1.c) You are Vāyu, of sharp brilliance.
(1.1.9.1ḍ) O Earth, place of sacrifice for the gods, may I not harm the root of your plants.
(1.1.9.1.e) Araru is driven away from the earth.
(1.1.9.1.f) Go to the fold, the stall of the cattle.
(1.1.9.1.g) May the sky rain for you.
(1.1.9.1.h) Bind him, O God Savitṛ, in the farthest distance with a hundred fetters—he who hates us and whom we hate—do not release him from there.
(1.1.9.1.i) Araru is driven away from the earth, the place of sacrifice to the gods.
(1.1.9.1.k) Go to the fold, the place of cattle!
(1.1.9.2ḷ) May the sky rain for you!
(1.1.9.2ṃ) O divine Savitṛ, bind him who hates us and whom we hate with a hundred fetters in the farthest distance; do not release him from there!
(1.1.9.2ṇ) Araru, the non-sacrificer to the gods, is struck down from the earth.
(1.1.9.2.o) Go to the fold, to the stall of the cattle.
(1.1.9.2.p) May the sky rain for you.
(1.1.9.2.q) O God Savitṛ, bind him who hates us and whom we hate with a hundred fetters in the farthest distance; do not release him from there!
(1.1.9.3ṛ) Let not thy Araru leap up to heaven!
(1.1.9.3ṣ) May the Vasus encompass thee with the Gāyatrī metre; may the Rudras encompass thee with the Triṣṭubh metre; may the Ādityas encompass thee with the Jagatī metre.
(1.1.9.3ṭ) At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, the wise perform the rite.
(1.1.9.3.u) You are the cosmic order; you are the seat of cosmic order; you are the glory of cosmic order.
(1.1.9.3.v) You are the offering; you are the self-offering.
(1.1.9.3.w) You are wide and you are wealthy.

(1.1.9.3.x) Before the spreading of the cruel one, O mighty one, the earth, the giver of life, was lifted up; that which they established in the moon by means of funeral offerings (*svadhā*), the wise behold and sacrifice.
(1.1.10.1.a) Burnt away is the Rakṣas; burnt away are the enemies. (1.1.10.1.b) With the most brilliant splendor of Agni, I heat [thee] thoroughly.
(1.1.10.1.c) May I not wipe out the cattle-pen; I cleanse thee, the vigorous one, the subduer of rivals.
(1.1.10.1ḍ) May I not wipe away speech, breath, sight, hearing, offspring, or the womb. I cleanse you, the vigorous one, the subduer of rivals.
(1.1.10.1.e) Aspiring for goodwill, progeny, good fortune, and a healthy body, I gird myself to perform a good deed, remaining devoted to the service of Agni.
(1.1.10.1.f) We, possessing noble offspring and being excellent wives, have sat down near you, O Agni, who crushes rivals—unassailable ourselves, we approach you the unassailable one.
(1.1.10.2.g) I loosen this bond of Varuṇa which Savitṛ, the kindly-minded, has bound. In the womb of Dhātṛ, in the world of good deeds, I make it pleasant for me together with my husband.
(1.1.10.2.h) Be united again with life, with offspring, and with splendor, O Agni! May I, as a wife, be united with my husband; may my self be united with my body.
(1.1.10.2.i) You are the milk of the great ones, the sap of the plants. Of you, who are inexhaustible, I cut off the omentum.
(1.1.10.3.k) You are the milk of the great ones, the sap of the plants; I gaze upon you with an undeceived eye for the sake of good offspring.
(1.1.10.3ḷ) You are brilliance; go after brilliance! May Agni not take away your brilliance from you.
(1.1.10.3ṃ) You are the tongue of Agni, the well-being of the gods.
(1.1.10.3ṇ) For every station, for the gods, for every sacrificial formula, be present!
(1.1.10.3.o) You are the bright, you are the light, you are the splendor.
(1.1.10.3.p) May the god Savitṛ purify you with a flawless filter, with the rays of the Vasu Sūrya.

(1.1.10.3.q) I take you, the bright one, for the bright [vessel], for every station, for the gods, for every sacrificial formula. (1.1.10.3.ṛ) I take you, the light, for the light; I take you, the flame, for the flame, for every station, for the gods, for every sacrificial formula.
(1.1.11.1.a) You are black, dwelling in the cleft; for Agni, svāhā!
(1.1.11.1.b) You are the altar; for the sacrificial grass, svāhā!
(1.1.11.1.c) You are the sacrificial grass; for the offering-ladles, svāhā! (1.1.11.1ḍ) For heaven, for the intermediate space, for earth, svāhā!
(1.1.11.1.e) Svadhā to the fathers; become nourishment for those who sit upon the sacrificial grass. (1.1.11.1.f) Go to the earth with nourishment.
(1.1.11.1.g) You are the tuft of Viṣṇu.
(1.1.11.1) I spread thee, who art wool-soft, as a comfortable seat for the gods.
(1.1.11.1.i) Thou art Viśvāvasu, the Gandharva; from all that causes fear, thou art the enclosure of the sacrificer, the *iḍ*, the praised one.
(1.1.11.1.k) Thou art the right arm of Indra; thou art the enclosure of the sacrificer, the *iḍ*, the praised one.
(1.1.11.2ḷ) May Mitra and Varuṇa enclose you from the north with steadfast law, as the praised enclosing-stick of the sacrificer, O Iḍā.
(1.1.11.2ṃ) May Sūrya protect you from the east against any curse.
(1.1.11.2ṇ) O Sage, we kindle you, the one who enjoys the oblation, the radiant, the great Agni, at the sacrifice.
(1.1.11.2.o) You two are the supports of the people. (1.1.11.2.p) Sit in the seat of the Vasus, the Rudras, and the Ādityas.
(1.1.11.2.q) You are the *juhū*, the *upabhṛt*, and the *dhruvā*; you are *ghṛtācī* by name; sit in your dear seat with your dear name.

(1.1.11.2ṛ) These have sat down in the world of the well-performed deed; (1.1.11.2ṣ) protect them, O Viṣṇu! (1.1.11.2ṭ) Protect the sacrifice, protect the lord of the sacrifice, protect me, the leader of the sacrifice.
(1.1.12.1.a) You are the world; spread yourself out!
(1.1.12.1.b) O Agni, sacrificer, this is homage. (1.1.12.1.c) O Juhū ladle, come hither; Agni calls you for the sacrifice to the gods.
(1.1.12.1ḍ) O Upabhṛt, come hither; the god Savitṛ calls you for the sacrifice to the gods.
(1.1.12.1.e) O Agni and Viṣṇu, may I not step upon you both.
(1.1.12.1.f) Open wide; do not scorch me.
(1.1.12.1.g) O you two makers of the world, create a world for me! (1.1.12.1.h) You are the station of Viṣṇu.
(1.1.12.1.i) From here Indra performed his heroic deeds.
(1.1.12.1.k) Having been commenced, the sacrifice rises upward, touching the sky; (1.1.12.1ḷ) the unswerving sacrifice belongs to the lord of the sacrifice; (1.1.12.1ṃ) accompanied by Indra, Svāhā!
(1.1.12.1ṇ) Great is the light! (1.1.12.1.o) Protect me, O Agni, from evil conduct; establish me in good conduct!
(1.1.12.1.p) You are the head of Makha; may light be anointed with light.
With the impulse of strength, with the upward-grasping, Indra has seized me; then, by the downward-grasping, he has cast my rivals beneath me.
The gods have increased the sacred word, both the upward grasp and the downward grasp; then may Indra and Agni scatter my rivals in all directions.
(1.1.13.1.c) For the Vasus you, for the Rudras you, for the Ādityas you. (1.1.13.1ḍ) Licking what has been anointed, let the birds depart.
(1.1.13.1.e) May I not wipe away offspring or the womb.
(1.1.13.1.f) May the waters and the plants swell. (1.1.13.1.g) You are the spotted deer of the Maruts; (1.1.13.1ḥ) go to heaven! (1.1.13.2) From there, send down rain for us.
(1.1.13.2.i) O Agni, you are the protector of life; protect my life.
(1.1.13.2.k) O Agni, you are the protector of sight; protect my sight. (1.1.13.2.l) You are firm.

(1.1.13.2ṃ) O Agni, god, that enclosing-stick which you placed around yourself when you were being carried away by the Paṇis—that very one I bring back to you according to your pleasure, so that he may not be estranged from you. (1.1.13.2ṇ) Come together to the path of the sacrifice!

(1.1.13.2.o) You who possess the portions of the remnants, you great ones who stand upon the *prastara* grass and sit upon the *barhis*—all you gods, welcoming this speech, take your seats upon this *barhis* and rejoice!
(1.1.13.3.p) I set you two in the seat of Agni, whose house is secure. (1.1.13.3.q) O benevolent ones, for the sake of well-being, bestow well-being upon me.
(1.1.13.3ṛ) O you who bear the yoke, protect us at the yoke.

(1.1.13.3ṣ) O Agni, of unimpaired life-force, of cool body, protect me today from heaven; protect me from bondage; protect me from ill-sacrificed rites; protect me from bad food; protect me from evil conduct.
(1.1.13.3ṭ) Make our food free from poison; make our dwelling-place comfortable; Svāhā!
(1.1.13.3.u) O gods who know the way, having found the way, go forth upon the way.
O Lord of the mind, O God, place this sacrifice of ours among the gods; Svāhā! In speech, Svāhā! Place it in the wind!
(1.1.14.1.a) O Indra and Agni, I call upon you both; may you both rejoice together in the gift of wealth. You both are givers of food and riches; I invoke you both for the winning of booty.

(1.1.14.1.b) For I have heard that you two are more liberal givers than even a father-in-law or a brother-in-law; therefore, O Indra and Agni, as the Soma is being offered to you, I generate a new hymn of praise.
O Indra and Agni, you two shook down ninety forts belonging to the Dāsas, all at once by a single deed.

O Indra and Agni, slayers of Vṛtra, may you today graciously accept this pure hymn newly born. For I call upon both of you, who are easily invoked; you two are most swift to grant strength to the one who desires it.
O Pūṣan, Lord of the Path, we have yoked you for our prayer, as one yokes a chariot for the winning of booty.

With eloquence, I have approached the protector of every path, impelled by desire, with a hymn of praise. May he grant us riches preceded by splendor; may Pūṣan bring each of our prayers to fulfillment.

(1.1.14.2.g) Through the Lord of the Field, as if by a friend, may we conquer; may he, who nourishes cattle and horses, be gracious to us such as we are. (1.1.14.3) May he be merciful to us in this state.
O Lord of the Field, pour out for us a honeyed wave, as a cow yields her milk—sweet-dropping, well-purified like clarified butter. May the Lords of Cosmic Order show us mercy.
O Agni, lead us by a good path to prosperity, O God who knowest all ways; keep away from us the sin that leads astray, and we shall offer unto thee the most abundant speech of homage.

(1.1.14.3.k) We have come to the path of the gods so that we may carry out what we are able to do. May Agni, the wise one, perform the sacrifice; he is indeed the Hotṛ, he shall arrange the rites and the seasons.
(1.1.14.4ḷ) Whatever is most effective, that sing forth as a great hymn for Agni, O Vibhāvasu! Like a sovereign queen, from you wealth issues forth; from you, spoils of war arise.
O Agni, you who are ever new, carry us across all difficulties with your blessings; be a broad, vast, and wide fortress for us, and grant well-being and health to our children and descendants.
O Agni, you are the guardian of vows, a god among mortals; you are to be praised at the sacrifices.
O gods, whatever vows of yours we, being more ignorant, violate while you are wise—may Agni, the knower, satisfy all that for us with those seasonal rites by which he ordains the gods.
(1.2.1.1.a) May the waters moisten you for life, for long-lived vigor and splendor.
(1.2.1.1.b) O herb, protect him!
(1.2.1.1.c) O axe, do not harm him!
(1.2.1.1ḍ) O you who are renowned among the gods, I shave these [hairs].
(1.2.1.1.e) May I attain well-being in what lies beyond.
(1.2.1.1.f) May the waters, our mothers, purify us; may those purified by ghee cleanse us with ghee. May they carry away all impurity from us; I emerge from them pure and sanctified.
(1.2.1.1.g) You are the body of Soma; protect my body. (1.2.1.1.h) You are the milk of the great ones; you are the bestower of splendor; bestow splendor upon me.
(1.2.1.2.i) You are the pupil of Vṛtra’s eye; you are the protector of sight; protect my sight.
(1.2.1.2.k) May the Lord of Thought purify you; may the Lord of Speech purify you; may the god Savitṛ purify you with an unbroken filter, with the rays of the sun, the Vasu.

(1.2.1.2ḷ) O Lord of the Filter, by means of your filter, may I be able to accomplish that for which I purify myself. (1.2.1.2ṃ) O gods, we approach you at the sacrifice, you whose laws are true; since we, O gods worthy of worship, call upon you at the invocation.
(1.2.1.2ṇ) Indra and Agni, Heaven and Earth, the Waters, and the Plants;
(1.2.1.2.o) you are the overlord of consecrations; protect me while I am here.

(1.2.2.1.a) To Ākūti, to Prayuj, to Agni, Svāhā! To Medhā, to Manas, to Agni, Svāhā! To Dīkṣā, to Tapas, to Agni, Svāhā! To Sarasvatī, to Pūṣan, to Agni, Svāhā! (1.2.2.1.b) O divine waters, vast, bringing welfare to all; O Heaven and Earth, the wide mid-air; may Bṛhaspati increase our oblation with Svāhā! (1.2.2.1.c) Let every mortal choose the friendship of the god who leads; let everyone seek wealth, and let him choose glory so that he may prosper—Svāhā!
(1.2.2.1ḍ) You two are the artistic forms (*śilpa*) of the *Ṛc* and the *Sāman*; I take hold of you both. Do you two protect me until the conclusion of this sacrifice.

(1.2.2.2.e) O God Varuṇa, sharpen this prayer of one who strives, and sharpen his will (*kratu*) and skill (*dakṣa*). May we cross over all difficulties; may we ascend the ship that provides a good crossing.
(1.2.2.2.f) You are strength, belonging to Aṅgiras, soft as wool. Grant me strength; protect me; do not harm me.
(1.2.2.2.g) You are Viṣṇu’s protection; you are the protection of the sacrificer; grant me protection.
(1.2.2.2.h) Protect me from the gaze of the stars.
(1.2.2.2.i) You are the womb of Indra; do not harm me.
For the sake of cultivation, for a good harvest; for you, the plants with good fruit;
may the divine tree, well-established, protect me upright until the end.
Svāhā! I take up the sacrifice with my mind; svāhā! from heaven and earth; svāhā! from the wide mid-air; svāhā! I grasp the sacrifice from the wind.
We meditate upon the divine intellect for our well-being and for our aid—that which bestows splendor, which carries the sacrifice, and may it lead us safely across to our desire.
(1.2.3.1.b) Those gods who are born of the mind, yoked by the mind, highly skillful, and whose father is Skill—may they protect us, may they favor us; homage to them! To them, Svāhā!
(1.2.3.1.c) O Agni, you be well awake; may we be well gladdened. Guard us for our well-being; give us back to wakefulness.
(1.2.3.1ḍ) O Agni, you are the guardian of vows, a god among mortals; you are to be praised at the sacrifices. (1.2.3.2)
(1.2.3.2.e) All the gods have turned toward me: Pūṣan with his gain, Soma with his bounty, and the god Savitṛ, the giver of wealth among riches.
(1.2.3.2.f) Grant this much, O Soma; bring more!
(1.2.3.2.g) May I, bestowing, not fail through my gift; may I not fail through my life-span.

(1.2.3.2) "Thou art the moon; be for my enjoyment! Thou art clothing; be for my enjoyment! Thou art the dawn; be for my enjoyment! Thou art a horse; be for my enjoyment! (1.2.3.3) "Thou art a goat; be for my enjoyment! Thou art a ram; be for my enjoyment!
(1.2.3.3.i) "For Vāyu thee! For Varuṇa thee! For Nirṛti thee! For Rudra thee!
(1.2.3.3.k) "O divine waters, O Son of the Waters, that wave of yours which is fit for oblation, powerful, and most intoxicating—that I shall not step upon."
(1.2.3.3ḷ) May I follow the unbroken thread of the earth.
(1.2.3.3ṃ) Go forth from good toward better. (1.2.3.3ṇ) Let Bṛhaspati be your forerunner; now descend to the choice place on the earth. Drive the enemies far away, O you who possess all heroes!

(1.2.3.3.o) We have come to this place of sacrifice on earth which all the gods of old delighted in; crossing over by means of the Ṛg, Sāman, and Yajus verses, may we rejoice in the increase of wealth and in nourishment.
(1.2.4.1.a) This is your bright body, O *śukra*, this is your splendor; unite with it, go to radiance.
(1.2.4.1.b) You are swift, held by the mind, beloved by Viṣṇu. (1.2.4.1.c) In the impulse of you, whose impulse is true, may I obtain the restraint of speech; *svāhā*.
(1.2.4.1ḍ) You are the bright; you are the immortal; you are the oblation for the All-Gods.
(1.2.4.1.e) I have mounted the eye of the Sun, the pupil of the eye of Agni, when you go forth with the dappled steeds, shining, wise with inspired knowledge.

(1.2.4.1.f) You are consciousness; you are thought; you are wisdom; you are the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*); you are worthy of sacrifice; you are the ruling power (*kṣatriyā*); you are Aditi, whose heads are on both sides.
(1.2.4.2.g) Be favorable to us from the front and favorable to us from behind.
(1.2.4.2.h) May Mitra bind you by the foot.
(1.2.4.2.i) May Pūṣan protect the paths.
(1.2.4.2.k) To Indra, the overseer.
(1.2.4.2ḷ) May your mother give her consent, may your father, may your brother born of the same womb, and may your friend of the same herd give their consent.
(1.2.4.2ṃ) O Goddess, go to the God; [bring] Soma for Indra.
May Rudra turn you back by the path of Mitra; return safely with Soma as your companion, together with wealth.
(1.2.5.1.a) You are Vasvī; you are Rudrā; you are Aditi; you are Ādityā; you are Śukrā; you are Candrā.
(1.2.5.1.b) May Bṛhaspati cause you to rejoice in happiness; may Rudra with the Vasus take heed of you.
(1.2.5.1.c) I sprinkle you upon the head of the earth, on the place of sacrifice to the gods, at the station of Iḍā, rich in ghee—svāhā!
(1.2.5.1ḍ) The *rakṣas* is encircled; the enemies are encircled. Here do I cut off the necks of the *rakṣas*.
(1.2.5.1.e) He who hates us and whom we hate—here do I cut off his necks. (1.2.5.2.f) May there be wealth for us, wealth for you, and wealth for him.
(1.2.5.2.g) O Goddess, look together with the goddess Urvaśī!
(1.2.5.2.h) Endowed with Tvaṣṭṛ, may I consort with thee; possessing good seed, may I deposit seed and obtain a hero in thy sight.
(1.2.5.2.i) May I not be separated from the increase of wealth.

(1.2.6.1.a) Let your stalk be joined with the stalk, joint with the joint; may your fragrance favor our desire; may the unshakable juice be for intoxication. You are the domestic attendant; the bright cup is yours.

(1.2.6.1.b) Toward that god Savitṛ, the wise in thought, within the two bowls, I sing praise—him whose impulse is true, the bestower of jewels, the beloved one of the mind. Whose lofty splendor has shone forth at his impelling; the golden-handed one of good wisdom has measured out the light with his form.
For the sake of offspring, for the sake of out-breath, for the sake of diffused breath—do you breathe after the offspring; may the offspring breathe after you.

(1.2.7.1.a) I purchase Soma for you—rich in vigor, rich in milk, rich in strength, overcoming the adversary. With the bright I purchase the bright; with the radiant the radiant; with the immortal the immortal. Yours is the cow.
(1.2.7.1.b) For us are the radiant ones.
(1.2.7.1.c) You are the body of austerity, the color of Prajāpati. Of you, who thrive with a thousandfold nourishment, I purchase [Soma] with the last animal.
(1.2.7.1ḍ) May your kinship be with us; may your riches rest upon me. (1.2.7.1.e) Light for us, and darkness for the seller of Soma. (1.2.7.1.f) Come to us like Mitra, bestowing good friendship.
(1.2.7.1.g) Enter the right thigh of Indra, desiring him who desires you, being pleasant to him who is pleasant to you.
(1.2.7.1.h) O Svāna, Bhrāja, Aṅghāri, Bambhāri, Hasta, Suhasta, Kṛśānu—these are your Soma-purchasers; guard them, let them not deceive you.
(1.2.8.1.a) Upward with life-force, well-endowed with life-force, with the sap of the plants, upward with the vigor of Parjanya, we have risen following the immortals.
(1.2.8.1.b) Proceed along the wide mid-air.
(1.2.8.1.c) You are the seat of Aditi.
(1.2.8.1ḍ) Sit upon the seat of Aditi!

(1.2.8.1.e) The Bull propped up the sky, he measured out the mid-region, and he established the breadth of the earth; as sovereign lord, he took his seat over all worlds—all these are the sacred ordinances of Varuṇa.

(1.2.8.1.f) He has spread the atmosphere across the forests; he has placed speed in horses, milk in cows, and mental power in hearts. (1.2.8.2) Varuṇa established Agni among the people, Sūrya in heaven, and Soma upon the mountain.
(1.2.8.2.g) His rays bear up that god Jātavedas, Sūrya, so that everyone may behold him.
(1.2.8.2: Come hither, O two oxen, bearers of the yoke, tearless, not slayers of heroes, impellers of prayer.
(1.2.8.2.i) Thou art the support of Varuṇa.
(1.2.8.2.k) Thou art the release of Varuṇa’s support.
The noose of Varuṇa has been cast off.

(1.2.9.1.a) Move forward, O Lord of the World, toward all your stations! Let not those who lie in ambush find you; let not highwaymen find you; let not the malevolent wolves find you; let not the Gandharva Viśvāvasu seize you!
(1.2.9.1.b) Becoming a hawk, fly away to the house of our sacrificer! You are consecrated by the gods; you are the bringer of well-being for the sacrificer.
(1.2.9.1.c) We have entered upon the path that leads to well-being and is free from danger, by which one avoids all enemies and finds wealth.
Homage to the eye of Mitra and Varuṇa; pay worship to that great god, to that *ṛta*. Proclaim praise to Sūrya, the far-seeing, the banner born of the gods, the son of Heaven.
(1.2.9.1.e) You are the support of Varuṇa.
(1.2.9.1.f) You are the release of Varuṇa’s support. (1.2.9.1.g) The noose of Varuṇa is loosened.

(1.2.10.1.a) You are the guest-offering for Agni; for Viṣṇu, you! You are the guest-offering for Soma; for Viṣṇu, you! You are the guest-offering for the guest; for Viṣṇu, you! For Agni, the giver of increase of wealth, for Viṣṇu, you! For Śyena, the bearer of Soma, for Viṣṇu, you!

(1.2.10.1.b) Whatever abodes of yours they worship with oblation—may all those encompass this sacrifice! Increasing the household, furthering us, rich in heroes, not slaying our men—O Soma, enter the dwellings!
(1.2.10.1.c) "Thou art the seat of Aditi; sit on the seat of Aditi. (1.2.10.2ḍ) "Thou art Varuṇa, whose vow is firm; thou art of Varuṇa.
(1.2.10.2.e) "Through the friendship of the gods, may we not be severed from the works of the gods."
(1.2.10.2.f) I take thee for the one who falls upon; I take thee for the one who falls all around; I take thee for Tanūnapāt; I take thee for Śākvara; I take thee for the mightiest in power.
(1.2.10.2.g) Thou art unassailed, thou art unassailable, the vigor of the gods, a protector against imprecation, beyond reproach.
(1.2.10.2) May the Lord of Consecration favor my consecration; may the Lord of Penance favor my penance. May I straightway attain truth; establish me in prosperity.
(1.2.11.1.a) May each stalk of yours, O divine Soma, swell for Indra, the winner of the single prize; may Indra swell for you, and may you swell for Indra.
(1.2.11.1.b) Cause your friends to swell with gain and wisdom; O divine Soma, may I attain well-being at your pressing.
(1.2.11.1.c) Desiring riches, I send forth [this prayer] for fortune; to the speakers of Truth, to Ṛta—homage to Heaven, homage to Earth!

(1.2.11.1ḍ) O Agni, Lord of Vows, you are the lord of vows among all vows. That body of mine which is here, let it be in you; that body of yours which is here, let it be in me. O Lord of Vows, may the vows of us two who observe the vow be fulfilled together.
(1.2.11.2.e) O Agni, with that body of yours which belongs to Rudra, protect us; to that body of yours, Svāhā!
(1.2.11.2.f) O Agni, that body of yours which dwells in iron, which dwells in silver, which dwells in gold—the most excellent, dwelling in the deep abyss.
I have struck down the fierce word; I have struck down the dazzling word. Svāhā!
(1.2.12.1.a) You are my path to wealth; you are my path to refreshment. Protect me when I am in distress; protect me when I am in agitation.
(1.2.12.1.b) May Agni find the name Nabhas.
(1.2.12.1.c) O Agni Aṅgiras, you who are on this earth, come with life and with the name! With that name of yours which is invincible and worthy of sacrifice, I establish you.
O Agni Aṅgiras, you who are on the second and third earth—come hither with life for the sake of this name! With that name of yours which is unassailable and worthy of sacrifice, I establish you.
You are a lioness; you are a buffalo-cow.
Spread yourself wide; may the lord of the sacrifice spread wide for you.
(1.2.12.2.g) You are firm. (1.2.12.2.h) Be purified for the gods; be adorned for the gods.

(1.2.12.2.i) May Indraghoṣa protect you from the east with the Vasus; may Manojavā protect you from the south with the Pitṛs; may Pracetas protect you from the west with the Rudras; may Viśvakarman protect you from the north with the Ādityas.

(1.2.12.2.k) You are a lioness, overcoming rivals; *svāhā*! You are a lioness, bestowing good progeny; *svāhā*! You are a lioness, bestowing abundance of wealth; *svāhā*! You are a lioness, bestowing the Ādityas; *svāhā*! You are a lioness; bring the gods hither for the god-loving sacrificer; *svāhā*! (1.2.12.3ḷ) For the beings, you! (1.2.12.3ṃ) You are the life of all; make firm the earth! You are dwelling in stability; make firm the intermediate space! You are dwelling in the unshakable; make firm the sky!
(1.2.12.3ṇ) You are the ash of Agni; you are the soil of Agni.

(1.2.13.1.a) The inspired priests of the great, inspired, wise one yoke their minds and yoke their thoughts. He alone, the knower of ways, ordains the priestly functions. Great is the praise of the god Savitṛ.
(1.2.13.1.b) O God, speak auspiciously in our dwellings.
(1.2.13.1.c) O you two who are heard by the gods, announce it among the gods.
(1.2.13.1ḍ) May a hero be born to us, one capable of action, upon whom we all may depend, who shall be the controller of many.
(1.2.13.1.e) Viṣṇu strode across this [universe]; in three places he planted his step. His [step] is gathered in the dust.

(1.2.13.2.f) O ye two [worlds], be full of nourishment, rich in milch-cows, providing good pasture for Manu, and glorious! Viṣṇu propped apart these two worlds; he has supported the earth on all sides with his rays.
(1.2.13.2.g) Moving forward, prepare the sacrifice; lead the rite upward; do not falter. Rest here upon the summit of the earth.

(1.2.13.2ḥ) O Viṣṇu, from heaven or from earth, or O Viṣṇu, from the great [realm] or from the intermediate space, fill your hands with many riches and bestow them! (1.2.13.3) From the south and from your own [place].
(1.2.13.3.i) Now I shall proclaim the heroic deeds of Viṣṇu, who measured out the earthly realms, who propped up the highest dwelling place, stroding three times across the wide expanse.
(1.2.13.3.k) You are the forehead of Viṣṇu; you are the back of Viṣṇu.
(1.2.13.3ḷ) You two are the corners of Viṣṇu’s mouth.
(1.2.13.3ṃ) You are the needle of Viṣṇu; (1.2.13.3ṇ) you are the firm station of Viṣṇu;
(1.2.13.3.o) you belong to Viṣṇu; for Viṣṇu, you!

(1.2.14.1.a) Display your power like a wide-spreading net; go forth like a mighty king with his host, like a bull with its herd. Rushing along your swift path, you are an archer; pierce the demons with your most scorching shafts.

(1.2.14.1.b) Your whirling flames fly swiftly; following them, touch [the enemy] boldly, O fiercely glowing one! O Agni, with your tongue of fire, cast forth your heats like winged insects; unrestrained, scatter your firebrands in every direction.

(1.2.14.1.c) Dispatch thy spies; be thou the swiftest one. Be thou an undeceivable guardian of this people, O Agni—[warding off] him who plots evil against us from afar, and him who is near. Let no affliction sent by thee prevail over us.

(1.2.14.2ḍ) Rise up, O Agni; stretch yourself out against [the foe]; burn down our enemies, O you of the sharp weapon! Whosoever has practiced hostility toward us, O kindled one, him you shall burn down like dry brushwood.
(1.2.14.2.e) Stand upright; pierce [them] from above us. Make manifest thy divine powers, O Agni! Slacken the firm [bonds] of those impelled by demons; crush the enemies, whether kin or stranger.
He knows your goodwill, O youngest one, who has opened a path for such a prayer; he has shone upon all his fair days, his riches, and the splendors of the noble, opening wide the doors for him.

(1.2.14.3.g) O Agni, let him be fortunate and a liberal giver who, throughout his own life, desires to satisfy you with constant oblations and hymns within his home; for him, every sacrifice shall result in auspicious days.

(1.2.14.3) I praise your benevolence; let my cry reach you from afar. May this song of mine resound for you like a beloved wife. (1.2.14.4) O you who possess noble horses and fine chariots, may we adorn you. May you maintain sovereign powers for us day after day.

May many a person here approach you of their own accord, O illuminator of the darkness, as you shine day after day. May we, sporting and well-disposed, attend upon you, while we stand amidst the splendors of the people.

(1.2.14.4.k) O Agni, whoever approaches you with good horses and fine gold on a chariot laden with wealth—he you become his protector, his friend, he who has taken pleasure in showing you hospitality in due order.

(1.2.14.4ḷ) I shatter the great [fortresses] with kinship and with words; that has come down to me from my father Gotama. O most youthful Hotṛ, of good will, master of the house, take heed of this our speech! (1.2.14.5) I shatter the great [fortresses]. That [speech] has followed me from my father Gotama. O most youthful Hotṛ, of good will, master of the house, take heed of this our speech!
(1.2.14.5) Born not from sleep, swift, most gracious, unwearied, free from predators, and most tireless—may those guardians, sitting together in harmony, O Agni, protect us, O wise one.

(1.2.14.5ṇ) O Agni, those guardians of yours who, seeing him blind, protected the son of Mamatā from misfortune—they, the all-knowing one, protected those doers of good; for the enemies, though seeking to harm, did not succeed in harming them. (1.2.14.6) They did not deceive.

(1.2.14.6.o) Through you we are possessed of wealth; aided by you, may we obtain spoils under your guidance. Accomplish both our prayers, O upholder of truth; act immediately, O one who is never put to shame.

(1.2.14.6.p) With this fuel, O Agni, may we worship you; accept the hymn being recited. Burn the malicious Rākṣasas; protect us from malice, from reproach, and from blame, O you who are great as Mitra.
I sprinkle the foe-slaying, vigorous one; I approach for protection the firm foundation, Mitra. Sharpened by our rites and kindled, may Agni protect us from harm by day and by night.
Agni shines forth with lofty light; he makes all things manifest by his greatness. He overcomes the godless, malevolent wiles; he sharpens his two horns to gore the Rakṣasa.
And let the roars of Agni rise to heaven, with sharp weapons to slay the Rakṣasa; for even in his exhilaration, his splendors shatter [the foe], and the godless obstructors cannot hold him back.
(1.3.1.1.a) At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan, I take thee up. Thou art a spade; thou art a woman.
(1.3.1.1.b) Encircled is the Rakṣas; encircled are the enemies. Here I cut off the neck of the Rakṣas.
(1.3.1.1.c) He who hates us and whom we hate—here I cut off his neck.
(1.3.1.1ḍ) For heaven thee, for the atmosphere thee, for the earth thee.
(1.3.1.1.e) May the world, the seat of the fathers, be purified. (1.3.1.1.f) Thou art barley; bar from us our hatred; bar away our enemies.
(1.3.1.2.g) You are the seat of the fathers. (1.3.1.2.h) Support the sky, fill the intermediate space, and make firm the earth.
(1.3.1.2.i) May Dyutāna Māruta set you up with the steadfast law of Mitra and Varuṇa.
(1.3.1.2.k) I carry you around as the winner of spiritual power, the winner of sovereign power, the winner of good progeny, and the winner of the increase of wealth.
(1.3.1.2ḷ) Strengthen spiritual power; strengthen sovereign power; strengthen progeny; strengthen the increase of wealth.
(1.3.1.2ṃ) O Heaven and Earth, fill yourselves with clarified butter.
(1.3.1.2ṇ) You are the seat of Indra, the shade for all people.
(1.3.1.2.o) May these songs encompass you on every side, O lover of song; may they be increases for the one whose life has increased, and may they be welcome delights.
(1.3.1.2.p) You are the needle of Indra; you are the firm foundation of Indra.
(1.3.1.2.q) You belong to Indra.
(1.3.1.2ṛ) For Indra, you!
(1.3.2.1.a) I dig these pits belonging to Viṣṇu, which slay the Rakṣas and destroy the secret spells.
(1.3.2.1.b) Here I cast up that secret spell which an equal or an unequal has buried against us.
(1.3.2.1.c) Here I cast him down lower, he who, whether an equal or an unequal, acts as an enemy toward us.
(1.3.2.1ḍ) By the Gāyatrī metre, the spell is suppressed.
(1.3.2.1.e) Whatever is auspicious here, let that be ours together.

(1.3.2.1.f) Thou art the Virāj, the slayer of rivals; thou art the Samrāj, the slayer of enemies; thou art the Svarāj, the slayer of the malicious; thou art the Viśvārāj, the destroyer of all destructive powers.

(1.3.2.2.g) I sprinkle you, the slayers of demons, the destroyers of secret spells, belonging to Viṣṇu. (1.3.2.2.h) I pour down you, the slayers of demons, the destroyers of secret spells, belonging to Viṣṇu. (1.3.2.2.i) You are barley; bar away from us hatred, bar away our enemies.
(1.3.2.2.k) I strew down those belonging to Viṣṇu, which are slayers of demons and destroyers of secret spells.

(1.3.2.2ḷ) I offer oblations to those belonging to Viṣṇu, which are slayers of demons and destroyers of secret spells. (1.3.2.2ṃ) I place down the two [bricks] belonging to Viṣṇu, which are slayers of demons and destroyers of secret spells.
(1.3.2.2ṇ) I spread around the two Rakṣas-slayers, the two Valaga-slayers, belonging to Viṣṇu. (1.3.2.2.o) I strew around the two Rakṣas-slayers, the two Valaga-slayers, belonging to Viṣṇu.
(1.3.2.2.p) The two Rakṣas-slayers, the two Valaga-slayers, belonging to Viṣṇu.
(1.3.2.2.q) You are great, O great pressing-stone; utter a great voice for Indra!
(1.3.3.1.a) You are the pervasive one, the carrier away. (1.3.3.1.b) You are the bearer, the carrier of the oblation. (1.3.3.1.c) You are the strengthening one, the wise one.
(1.3.3.1ḍ) Thou art Tutha, the all-knowing.
(1.3.3.1.e) Thou art Uśij, the seer.
(1.3.3.1.f) Thou art Aṅghāri, thou art Bambhāri.
(1.3.3.1.g) You are the seeker of aid, the one who honors;
(1.3.3.1.h) you are the purifier, the Mārjālīya;
(1.3.3.1.i) you are the sovereign, the Kṛśānu.
(1.3.3.1.k) You are the one to be honored in assembly, O Pavamāna; (1.3.3.1ḷ) you are the swift mover, possessed of the mist; (1.3.3.1ṃ) you are the unsullied one, the preparer of the oblation.
(1.3.3.1ṇ) You are the one whose abode is the cosmic order (*ṛta*), the light of heaven.
(1.3.3.1.o) You are the light of sacred knowledge (*brahman*), the abode of heaven. (1.3.3.1.p) You are the Unborn One, the Single-footed.
(1.3.3.1.q) You are the serpent of the deep.
(1.3.3.1ṛ) With your fierce aspect, O Agni, protect me; carry me across; do not harm me.
(1.3.4.1.a) O Soma, you are the wide-extender of protection against the hostilities that pierce our bodies and those wrought by others;

Svāhā! (1.3.4.1.b) May the swift one, enjoying the clarified butter, partake of it; Svāhā! (1.3.4.1.c) May this Agni create wide space for us; may he go before us, shattering the adversaries. May he, exulting, conquer the enemies; may he win the prize in the struggle for booty.

(1.3.4.1ḍ) O Viṣṇu, stride out widely; make wide space for our dwelling. Drink the clarified butter, O you whose source is clarified butter; further and further extend the life of the lord of the sacrifice.
(1.3.4.1.e) Soma goes forth, the finder of the way. (1.3.4.2) He goes to the appointed place of the gods, to sit upon the womb of *ṛta*.
(1.3.4.2.f) You are the seat of Aditi; (1.3.4.2.g) sit upon the seat of Aditi.

(1.3.4.2: This, O God Savitṛ, is your Soma; guard it, let it not deceive you. (1.3.4.2.i: O Soma, as a god you have approached the gods; here I, a man, [approach] men, together with offspring, together with the increase of wealth.
(1.3.4.2.k: Homage to the gods! Svadhā to the ancestors!
(1.3.4.2ḷ) Here, from the noose of Varuṇa, I have looked out toward the light of heaven, the Vaiśvānara light.
(1.3.4.3ṃ) O Agni, Lord of Vows, you are the lord of vows among all vows.
(1.3.4.3ṇ) That body of mine which was in you, let it be here in me; that body of yours which was in me, let it be there in you.
O Lord of Vows, according to our respective roles, may the vows of us two who observe the vow be fulfilled.
(1.3.5.1.a) I have passed beyond some; I have not approached others.
(1.3.5.1.b) I have found you on this side through those who are further, and through those who are yet further still.
(1.3.5.1.c) I take pleasure in you, the one belonging to Viṣṇu, for the sacrifice to the gods.
(1.3.5.1ḍ) May the god Savitṛ anoint you with honey.
(1.3.5.1.e) O herb, protect him!
(1.3.5.1.f) O axe, do not harm him!
(1.3.5.1.g) Do not scratch the sky with your top; do not harm the mid-air with your middle; be united with the earth.
(1.3.5.1.h) O Lord of the Forest, grow forth with a hundred shoots; may we grow forth with a thousand shoots.
(1.3.5.1.i) You whom this whetted axe has brought forward for great good fortune—may you be uncut, possessing wealth and heroic sons.
(1.3.6.1.a) For the earth thee, for the intermediate space thee, for the sky thee.
(1.3.6.1.b) May the world, the seat of the fathers, be purified. (1.3.6.1.c) Thou art barley; bar from us hatred, bar away enemies.

(1.3.6.1ḍ) You are the seat of the ancestors. (1.3.6.1.e) You are easy of access; you are the leader of leaders, O Vanaspati; he shall stand upon you—be mindful of him. (1.3.6.1.f) May the divine Savitṛ anoint you with honey.
(1.3.6.1.g) For you, from the plants with goodly fruit.

(1.3.6.1.h) Prop up the sky, fill the mid-air, and make firm the earth with your base. (1.3.6.1.i) We desire to go to those, your abodes, where the many-horned, tireless cows dwell; there, indeed, shines down that highest step of the wide-striding Viṣṇu, the abundant one.
Behold the deeds of Viṣṇu, through which he has made his vows manifest; he is the close-allied friend of Indra.
The wise ever behold that highest step of Viṣṇu, like an eye stretched across the sky.
(1.3.6.2m) I enclose you, who win the *brahman*, who win the *kṣatra*, who win good progeny, and who win the increase of wealth.

(1.3.6.2n) Strengthen the *brahman*; strengthen the *kṣatra*; strengthen progeny; strengthen the increase of wealth. (1.3.6.2.o) You are the one girt about; may the divine subjects surround you; may the increase of wealth surround this sacrificer, as do human beings.
I conceal you on the ridge of the intermediate space.
(1.3.7.1.a) For the sake of nourishment, thee!
(1.3.7.1.b) Thou art the one who comes near.
(1.3.7.1.c) The divine hosts have approached the gods—the bearers, the eager ones.
O Bṛhaspati, bestow riches;
may the oblations be sweet to you. O divine Tvaṣṭṛ, delight in wealth.
(1.3.7.1.g) O wealthy ones, rejoice!
(1.3.7.1.h) You are the birthplace of Agni. (1.3.7.1.i) You two are the bulls.
(1.3.7.1.k) You are Urvaśī; you are Āyu; you are Purūravas.
(1.3.7.1ḷ) Anointed with clarified butter, may you two bestow virility.
(1.3.7.1ṃ) Be born after the Gāyatrī metre; be born after the Triṣṭubh and Jagatī metres.
Be of one mind for us, of one dwelling, and free from blemish;
do not harm the sacrifice nor the lord of the sacrifice, O Jātavedas; be auspicious to us today.

Fire moves within fire, having entered it; he is the son of the seers, this sovereign ruler. Having consecrated with the sacred word (*brahman*), I offer to you with *svāhā*; may I not wrongly perform the portion of the gods.
(1.3.8.1.a) I take hold. (1.3.8.1.b) O divine oblation, I seize you with the noose of *ṛta*. (1.3.8.1.c) Overpower the men!
(1.3.8.1ḍ) I sprinkle you with water and herbs. (1.3.8.1.e) You are the drinker of waters.
(1.3.8.1.f) O divine waters, season this well-prepared oblation, which is already seasoned by the gods.
(1.3.8.1.g) May your breath unite with the wind; may your limbs unite with those worthy of sacrifice; may the lord of the sacrifice unite with his blessing.
(1.3.8.1.h) Anointed with clarified butter, do you two protect the animal. (1.3.8.1.i) O wealthy ones, enter the lord of the sacrifice with what is dear to him.

(1.3.8.1.k) O breast, the intermediate space; in harmony with the god Vāta, sacrifice by yourself for this oblation; be united with his body; in the most excellent sacrifice, establish the lord of the sacrifice in a more excellent state.
(1.3.8.2ḷ) Protect him from contact with the earth. (1.3.8.2ṃ) Homage to you, O expansion!
(1.3.8.2ṇ) Go forward, unassailable, along the stream of clarified butter, together with offspring, together with the increase of wealth.
(1.3.8.2.o) O divine waters, you who seek purity, pure yourselves, carry the gods; being pure, may we be served by you as those who serve. May we be your servers.
(1.3.9.1.a) May your speech swell; may your breath swell; may your eye swell; may your ear swell.

(1.3.9.1.b) Whatever pain has entered your vital breaths, whatever [pain] your eye, whatever your ear, whatever is harsh in you, whatever is settled [within], may that swell for you; may that be purified for you by this.
(1.3.9.1.c) May your navel swell; may your anus swell.

(1.3.9.1ḍ) Pure in their conduct, (1.3.9.1.e) peace unto the waters! (1.3.9.2) Peace unto the plants, peace unto the earth, peace unto the two worlds (day and night)! (1.3.9.2.f) O plant, protect him!
(1.3.9.2.g) O axe, do not harm him!
(1.3.9.2.h) You are the portion of the Rakṣases. (1.3.9.2.i) Here I lead this Rakṣas into the lowest darkness.
(1.3.9.2.k) "Whoever hates us and whomsoever we hate—him I lead into this lowest darkness.
(1.3.9.2ḷ) "For strength, thee!
(1.3.9.2ṃ) "O Heaven and Earth, clothe yourselves with clarified butter!"
(1.3.9.2ṇ) May there be unbroken wealth accompanied by heroic sons.
(1.3.9.2.o) Proceed along the wide mid-air.
(1.3.9.2.p) O Vāyu, partake of the drops.
Svāhā! Go to the Maruts of the upward-moving cloud.
(1.3.10.1.a) May your mind be united with [my] mind; may your breath be united with [my] breath.
(1.3.10.1.b) An offering rich in ghee, pleasing to the gods—*svāhā*!
(1.3.10.1.c) May Indra’s out-breath settle in every limb; may Indra’s in-breath manifest in every limb.

O divine Tvaṣṭṛ, let your abundant abundance come together, since you, though diverse in form, become uniform in appearance. May your friends rejoice after you as you go among the gods for protection; may your mother and father rejoice after you.
(1.3.10.1.e) You are glory.
(1.3.10.1.f) May Agni mix you.
(1.3.10.1.g) The waters have flowed together.
(1.3.10.1) For the gliding of Vāta, for the speed of Pūṣan, for the growth of the waters and the plants—(1.3.10.2.i) O drinkers of ghee, drink the ghee; O drinkers of fat, drink the fat!
(1.3.10.2.k) You are the oblation of the intermediate space.
Svāhā! To you for the intermediate space. Svāhā! To the quarters, the intermediate quarters, the primary quarters, the secondary quarters, and the upward quarters; svāhā! To the quarters.

(1.3.10.2.o) Homage to the quarters! (1.3.11.1.a) Go to the ocean, svāhā! Go to the intermediate space, svāhā! Go to the god Savitṛ, svāhā! Go to day and night, svāhā! Go to Mitra and Varuṇa, svāhā! Go to Soma, svāhā! Go to the sacrifice, svāhā! Go to the meters, svāhā! Go to heaven and earth, svāhā! Go to the celestial waters, svāhā! Go to Agni Vaiśvānara, svāhā! (1.3.11.1.b) For the waters, for the plants, thee!
(1.3.11.1.c) Grant me mind and heart.
(1.3.11.1ḍ) May I attain my body, my skin, my son, and my grandson. (1.3.11.1.e) You are heat; burn him who hates us and whom we hate.
(1.3.11.1.f) O King Varuṇa, from every bond release us here; from whatever oath we have sworn by the waters, by the cows, or by Varuṇa himself, from that, O Varuṇa, release us.
(1.3.12.1.a) Rich in oblations are these waters; rich in oblations is the divine sacrifice; rich in oblations he seeks to win over; rich in oblations let the sun be.
(1.3.12.1.b) I set you down in the seat of Agni, whose house is secure; for the sake of bliss, O you who bring bliss, place me in bliss.
(1.3.12.1.c) You are the portion of Indra and Agni; you are the portion of Mitra and Varuṇa; you are the portion of all the gods.
(1.3.12.1ḍ) Be watchful at the sacrifice.
(1.3.13.1.a) For the heart thee, for the mind thee, for the sky thee, for the sun thee!
(1.3.13.1.b) Make this sacrifice ascend; bestow the priestly offices upon the gods in heaven! (1.3.13.1.c) O King Soma, come hither; descend!
Do not fear; do not tremble.
May I not harm you. Descend upon the progeny; may the progeny descend upon you.
(1.3.13.1.g) May Agni hear my call with his fuel; may the Waters and the divine Dhiṣaṇās hear; O pressing-stones, you who are wise, hear now the sacrifice! May the god Savitṛ hear my call.

(1.3.13.2ḥ) O divine waters, O son of the waters, that wave of yours which is fit for oblation, powerful, and most intoxicating—place that bright [wave] among the gods for those who drink the bright [Soma], for whom you are the portion; *svāhā*! (1.3.13.2.i) You are the plougher; drive away the enemy of the waters. (1.3.13.2.k) For the sake of the ocean’s abundance, I lift you up.
O Agni, the mortal whom you protect in battles and whom you urge on in the contests for booty—he shall be the master of eternal nourishments.

(1.3.14.1.a) You, O Agni, are Rudra, the Asura of the great heaven; you are the host of the Maruts; you rule over nourishment. You travel with the ruddy winds, bringing peace to the home; as Pūṣan, you yourself protect those who serve you.

(1.3.14.1.b) Bring hither for your protection Agni, the king of the sacrifice, the Rudra, the Hotṛ-priest who sacrifices truly between the two worlds—he who is of golden form, before the unperceived thunderbolt strikes.

Agni, the Hotṛ, the most skilled in sacrifice, has sat down in the fragrant lap of his mother, in her place; he is the youthful sage, dwelling among many, the observer of Truth, the supporter of the peoples, kindled in their midst.

He has made our divine assembly auspicious; grant us protection. We have found the secret tongue of the sacrifice. He has come with life, clothed in fragrance; he has made our invocation of the gods auspicious today.
Agni has cried out like the thundering sky, licking the earth, anointing the plants; as soon as he was born, once kindled, he looked abroad; he shines with his splendor between the two worlds.

(1.3.14.2.f) In thee, O many-faced Hotṛ, the worshipful ones have placed all treasures at evening and at dawn; like the earth, O sacrificer, thou hast encompassed all beings; they have bestowed all blessings upon thee, the purifier.
(1.3.14.3.g) To you, O best of Angirases, all these well-settled people have turned separately, O Agni, out of desire.

May we attain that desire of yours through your power, O Agni; may we attain wealth, O Lord of Wealth, together with heroic sons. May we, seeking strength, attain booty; may we attain your undecaying and ageless splendor.
O youngest Agni, descendant of Bharata, bring us the most excellent, radiant, and much-desired wealth, O Vasu.

He, the whitening one, the thundering, dwelling in the luminous realm, most youthful with his unaging, roaring [flames]—Agni, the purifier, who is most manifold, goes along devouring many broad things.
Bestowing life upon you from every side, may this Agni, the most excellent, bring back your breath; I drive away consumption from you.

(1.3.14.4) O Agni, giver of life, enjoying the oblation, be one whose face is ghee and whose source is ghee! Having drunk the ghee and the sweet, pleasant [milk] of the cow, protect this man as a father protects his son. (1.3.14.5) Protect him!
To you, O Jātavedas, who are observant of all people and who take pleasure in our offerings, O Agni, I generate this excellent hymn of praise.
Agni was first born from heaven; a second time, Jātavedas was born from us. A third time, he of manly mind was born in the waters. The pious man, kindling him, praises this eternal one.
O Agni, pure, purifying, and worthy of praise, you shine forth mightily when you are offered oblations of clarified butter.

Visible like a golden ornament, he has shone forth widely; shining for the sake of glory with an irrepressible life-force, Agni became immortal through his vital powers, since Dyaus, rich in seed, begat him.

When the brilliance reached the lord of men for the sake of nourishment, the pure seed was poured down from heaven in the encounter; Agni brought forth and perfected the blameless, youthful host, well-disposed and wise.

With a more brilliant mind, O Agni, protect us; grant us aid, O giver of good offspring, you who bestow gifts. May we be present at the abundance of your most heroic wealth, and may we be the singers of your excellent praises, O Vasu.
O Agni, by thy overwhelming power, bring hither wealth that conquers all; for he who, by his mouth, shall overcome all peoples in the contests for booty.
O Agni, bring us that wealth which conquers armies, for you are the true and wondrous giver of booty consisting of cattle.
To Agni, the ordainer, whose food is the bull and the cow, who bears Soma upon his back—to him we shall pay worship with hymns of praise.

For you, O Son, are a speaker; Agni, by his very birth, has made for himself food while seated at the meal. As such, O winner of strength, bestow strength upon us; like a king, dwell among us in a place free from enemies.
O Agni, [grant] lifespans! Purify yourself; bring to us strength and nourishment, and drive misfortune far away.
O Agni, you who are skillful in action, purify yourself for us; bestowing upon me splendor, heroic vigor, nourishment, and wealth.
O Agni, purifier, with your radiant and delightful tongue, O god, bring the gods here and worship them.
O purifying, radiant Agni, bring the gods here to us, to our sacrifice and our oblation.
Agni, whose vows are most pure, is pure as a sage, pure as a seer; pure, he shines when offered oblations.
Upward, O Agni, your pure, bright, and radiant flames rise; your lights are your rays of splendor.

(1.4.1.1.a) I take up the pressing-stone; it is the performer of the sacrifice for the gods. Make this sacrifice deep; with your highest rim, [press] the Soma for Indra—well-pressed, honeyed, rich in milk, and winning the rain.

(1.4.1.1.b) For Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, you! For Indra, the overcomer of Vṛtra, you! For Indra, the slayer of the arrogant foe, you! For Indra accompanied by the Ādityas, you! For Indra accompanied by all the gods, you!

(1.4.1.1.c) You are strengthening, overcomers of Vṛtra, delighting in bounty, wives of immortality. O goddesses, bestow this sacrifice upon the gods; being invited, drink of the Soma! Being invited, let Soma drink of yours!

(1.4.1.2ḍ) O Soma, whatever light is yours in heaven, whatever on earth, and whatever in the broad mid-air—with that, create wide wealth for this sacrificer; speak in favor of the giver! (1.4.1.2.e) O two bowls (*dhiṣaṇe*), though you are firm, be made firm; bestow strength, bestow strength upon me! May I not harm you; may you not harm me.
(1.4.1.2.f) From the east, from the west, from the north, from the south—let those quarters run toward you; O Mother, cry out!
(1.4.1.2.g) O Soma, that invincible and watchful name of yours, for that, O Soma, to Soma, svāhā!

(1.4.2.1.a) Flow pure for the Lord of Speech, O vigorous one; as a bull, purified by the hands with the two shoots of the bull, you are a god, the purifier of the gods; for those whose portion you are, for them I take you.
(1.4.2.1.b) You are self-fashioned; make our nourishments sweet; for all the powers of Indra, celestial and terrestrial, [I take you].
(1.4.2.1.c) May the mind fashion you.
(1.4.2.1ḍ) Follow along the wide mid-region;
(1.4.2.1.e) Svāhā! To the Sun, thee, O thou of noble birth; (1.4.2.1.f) To the gods who drink the rays of light, thee!
(1.4.2.1.g) This is your womb; for breath, you!

(1.4.3.1.a) You are taken with a support. (1.4.3.1.b) O Maghavan, interpose yourself; protect the Soma; grant us wealth; bestow nourishments; I place you between heaven and earth, within the wide intermediate space; in harmony with the gods, both lower and higher, O Maghavan, rejoice in the Antaryāma cup.
(1.4.3.1.c) You are made ready by yourself; make our nourishments sweet; for all your powers, celestial and terrestrial.
(1.4.3.1ḍ) May the mind attend you!
(1.4.3.1.e) Proceed along the wide mid-air!
(1.4.3.1.f) Svāhā! To the sun, thee, O thou of noble birth!
(1.4.3.1.g) For the gods who drink the rays of light, you!
(1.4.3.1.h) This is your womb; for the out-breath, you!
O Vāyu, drinker of the pure, come to us; a thousand are your teams, O possessor of all boons. To you this intoxicating juice is offered, of which, O God, you have the first draught.
(1.4.4.1.b) You are taken with a support; for Vāyu, you! (1.4.4.1.c) Indra and Vāyu, these [Soma juices] have been pressed. Come hither with refreshments, for the drops long for you both.
(1.4.4.1ḍ) You are taken with a support; for Indra and Vāyu, you! This is your place of origin; for you two who are in harmony, you!
(1.4.5.1.a) O Mitra and Varuṇa, increasers of cosmic order, this Soma has been pressed for you; hear my invocation here.
(1.4.5.1.b) You are taken with a support; for Mitra and Varuṇa you are; this is your womb; for the two who live by the Cosmic Order (*ṛta*), you are.
O Aśvins, with that whip of yours which is honeyed and full of pleasant truth, sprinkle the sacrifice.
(1.4.6.1.b) You are taken with a support; for the Aśvins you! This is your womb; for the two Mādhvīs you!
(1.4.7.1.a) O Aśvins, you who are yoked at dawn, unyoke yourselves; come hither to drink this Soma.
(1.4.7.1.b) You are taken with a support; for the Aśvins you! This is your womb; for the Aśvins you!

(1.4.8.1.a) This Vena, enveloped in light, impels the offspring of Pṛśni within the expanse of the mid-world; at the meeting of the waters and the sun, the sages lick him with their hymns as if he were an infant.
(1.4.8.1.b) You are taken with a support; for Śaṇḍa you! This is your womb; protect manly vigor!

(1.4.9.1.a) As of old, as before, as always, as now—[we invoke] him who sits upon the sacrificial grass, the most excellent, the finder of heaven, the one who yields for us a strengthening fortress through our song; he who is swift, the conqueror, in whom you grow great.
(1.4.9.1.b) You are taken with a support; for Marka you! This is your womb; protect the offspring.
(1.4.10.1.a) You gods who are eleven in heaven, who are eleven upon the earth, who sit in the waters as eleven by your greatness—O gods, may you graciously accept this sacrifice.

(1.4.10.1.b) You are taken with a support; you are the Āgrayaṇa, the excellent Āgrayaṇa. Quicken the sacrifice, quicken the lord of the sacrifice; protect the pressings! May Viṣṇu protect you; protect the people with your power! This is your womb; for all the gods, I take you.
(1.4.11.1.a) The thirty and three Rudras, moving in troops and causing pain, attend to heaven and earth; may all these eleven who dwell in the waters enjoy the pressed Soma for the libation.

(1.4.11.1.b) You are taken with a support; you are the Āgrayaṇa, the good Āgrayaṇa. Quicken the sacrifice, quicken the lord of the sacrifice; protect the pressings! May Viṣṇu protect you; protect the people with your power! This is your womb: for all the gods, you!

(1.4.12.1.a) You are taken with a support; for Indra, the mighty, the vigorous, the seeker of hymns, I take you. That which is your great vigor, O Indra—for that I take you. For Viṣṇu, I take you. This is your womb; for Indra, the seeker of hymns, I take you.
The gods generated from their mouth the head of heaven, the messenger of earth, Agni Vaiśvānara born for the sake of cosmic order—the sage, the sovereign, the guest of men—as a vessel.

(1.4.13.1.b) You are taken with a support; I take you for Agni Vaiśvānara. You are firm, a firm dwelling, the firmest of the firm, the most immovable of the immovable. This is your womb; I take you for Agni Vaiśvānara.
Madhu and Mādhava, Śukra and Śuci, Nabhas and Nabhasya, Iṣa and Ūrja, Sahas and Sahasya, Tapas and Tapasya.
You are taken with a support;
you are Saṃsarpa.
For the sake of Aṃhaspati, I take you.
O Indra and Agni, come to the pressed juice with our songs; drink of this desirable cloud, impelled by our prayer.
(1.4.15.1.b) You are taken with a support; for Indra and Agni you are; this is your womb; for Indra and Agni you are.
O protectors, sustainers of the people, all you gods, come hither; you who accept the offering, come to the pressed juice of the donor.
(1.4.16.1.b) You are taken with a support; for all the gods you are taken. This is your womb; for all the gods you are taken.
We invoke here for our new protection that Indra, the bull accompanied by the Maruts, who has grown mighty, the heavenly ruler who is without a rival, the all-conquering bestower of victory.
(1.4.17.1.b) You are taken with a support; for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, you! This is your womb; for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, you!

(1.4.18.1.a) O Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, drink the Soma here, just as you drank of the pressed juice at Śāryāta’s sacrifice. Under your guidance and in your protection, O Hero, the sages who perform excellent sacrifices seek to win your favor.
(1.4.18.1.b) You are taken with a support; for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, you! This is your resting place; for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, you!

Accompanied by the Maruts, O Indra, bull-like hero, drink the Soma for the battle, according to your custom, for exhilaration. Pour the wave of honeyed juice into your belly; you have been the king of the pressed juices from time immemorial.
(1.4.19.1.b) You are taken with a support; for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, you! This is your womb; for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, you!
Great is Indra, who by his might is like Parjanya rich in rain; he has grown strong through the hymns of Vatsa.
(1.4.20.1.b) You are taken with a support; for Mahendra you! This is your womb; for Mahendra you!

Great is Indra, manly, filling the peoples; moreover, doubly vast and undiminished in his powers, he has grown for the sake of heroic deeds directed toward us. Broad and wide, he has been made well-fashioned by the makers.
(1.4.21.1.b) You are taken with a support; for Mahendra you! This is your womb; for Mahendra you!
Never art thou barren, O Indra; never dost thou fail the donor. More and more, O Maghavan, thy bounty as a god is poured forth.

(1.4.22.1.b) You are taken with a support; for the Ādityas, you! (1.4.22.1.c) Never indeed do you neglect; you protect both generations. O fourth Āditya, your power is the libation; immortality has taken its place in heaven.
The sacrifice goes forth toward the favor of the gods; O Ādityas, be gracious! May your benevolence turn hitherward, which is the best finder of wide space even from distress.
O Vivasvat Āditya, this is your draught of Soma; rejoice with it, be satisfied with it, and may we, as those who satisfy you, be satisfied by you. With that divine rain, I mix you.

(1.4.23.1.a) O Savitṛ, grant us what is desirable today, and what is desirable tomorrow, and what is desirable day by day. For, O God, through this prayer, may we be partakers of the desirable, of an abundant dwelling.
(1.4.23.1.b) You are taken with a support; for the god Savitṛ, you!
O Savitṛ, with your undeceivable and auspicious guardians, protect our household today; O golden-tongued one, guard us for new prosperity, so that no malevolent person may have power over us.
(1.4.24.1.b) You are taken with a support; I take you for the god Savitṛ.
(1.4.25.1.a) I invoke Savitṛ, the golden-handed, for aid; he, the god, knows the place.
(1.4.25.1.b) You are taken with a support; I take you for the god Savitṛ.
(1.4.26.1.a) You are a good protector, well-established.
(1.4.26.1.b) A great reverence to the bull!
(1.4.26.1.c) This is your womb; for all the gods, you!
(1.4.27.1.a) O Indu, from thee, the son of Bṛhaspati, who art possessed of Indra-power, I take the draught for the wives.
(1.4.27.1.b) O Agni, accompanied by the wives, in harmony with the god Tvaṣṭṛ, drink the Soma; Svāhā!

(1.4.28.1.a) You are the tawny one, the yoker of the tawny steeds, the rider of the tawny horses, the bearer of the thunderbolt, the lover of Pṛśni. O divine Soma, for you whose sacrificial formula has been offered, whose hymn has been chanted, and whose recitation has been performed, I take this cup accompanied by the tawny steeds.
(1.4.28.1.b) You two are the tawny ones; here are the parched grains for the tawny steeds, together with the Soma.
(1.4.28.1.c) To Indra, Svāhā!
(1.4.29.1.a) O Agni, you purify our lifespans; bring to us strength and nourishment. Drive far away misfortune.
(1.4.29.1.b) You are taken with a support; I take you for Agni the radiant. This is your womb; I take you for Agni the radiant.
Rising up with vigor, having drunk, you shook your jaws, O Indra, after drinking the Soma pressed in the ladle.
(1.4.30.1.b) You are taken with a support; for Indra, the powerful, you are taken. This is your resting place; for Indra, the powerful, you are taken.
(1.4.31.1.a) You are the one who carries us across, visible to all, the maker of light, O Sūrya; you illuminate the entire radiant realm.
(1.4.31.1.b) You are taken with a support; for the radiant Sūrya, you! This is your womb; for the radiant Sūrya, you!
(1.4.32.1.a) Swell up, O most intoxicating Soma, with all your aids; be for us the most extensive one.
(1.4.33.1.a) Gone are those mortals who saw the Dawn shining long ago; now she has become visible to us. And they come who shall see her in future days.
(1.4.34.1.a) I settle you, the luminous one. (1.4.34.1.b) I settle you, the light-maker. (1.4.34.1.c) I settle you, the knower of light.
(1.4.34.1ḍ) I settle thee, the radiant one;
(1.4.34.1.e) I settle thee, the blazing one;
(1.4.34.1.f) I settle thee, who art making a rustling sound.
(1.4.34.1.g) I settle you, the blazing one; (1.4.34.1.h) I settle you, the shining one;
(1.4.34.1.i) I settle you, the imperishable one.
(1.4.34.1.k) I settle you, whose light is great. (1.4.34.1ḷ) I settle you, who are awakening. (1.4.34.1ṃ) I settle you, who are watchful.

Hail to exertion! Hail to effort! Hail to fatigue! Hail to exhaustion! Hail to rising! Hail to wandering! Hail to purity! Hail to grief! Hail to burning! Hail to the scorcher! Hail to the murder of a Brahmin! Hail to everything! Hail!

(1.4.36.1.a) With the mind, [I appease] Saṃtāna-Bhava; with the liver, Rudra; with the thin membrane, Paśupati; with the thick heart, Agni; with the heart, Rudra; with the blood, Śarva; with the two kidneys, Mahādeva; with the inner ribs, Auṣiṣṭhahan; with the two *śiṅgīnikośya* organs, [I appease the gods].
(1.4.37.1.a) Ascend the chariot, O slayer of Vṛtra; your two bay steeds have been yoked by our sacred prayer (*brahman*). May the pressing-stone, with its sound, turn your mind toward us.
(1.4.37.1.b) You are taken with a support; for Indra, for the Ṣoḍaśin, you! This is your womb; for Indra, for the Ṣoḍaśin, you!
(1.4.38.1.a) The two bay steeds carry Indra, whose power is unassailable, toward the praises of the seers and the sacrifice of men.
(1.4.38.1.b) You are taken with a support; I take you for Indra, for the *ṣoḍaśin*. This is your resting place; I take you for Indra, for the *ṣoḍaśin*.
(1.4.39.1.a) Soma has been pressed for you, O Indra; come, O most powerful and bold one! Let Indra-power fill you, as the sun fills the mid-air with its rays.
(1.4.39.1.b) You are taken with a support; for Indra, for you, the sixteenfold one. This is your womb; for Indra, for you, the sixteenfold one.
(1.4.40.1.a) The earth, which lies spread out for all, has placed thee upon her lap; be pleasant and easy to sit upon for him, and grant him wide-spreading protection.
(1.4.40.1.b) You are taken with a support; for Indra, for the Ṣoḍaśin, you! This is your womb; for Indra, for the Ṣoḍaśin, you!
May the great Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, the sixteenfold one, grant us protection; may the bounteous lord bestow well-being upon us and slay the evil one who hates us.
(1.4.41.1.b) You are taken with a support; for Indra, for the Ṣoḍaśin, you! This is your womb; for Indra, for the Ṣoḍaśin, you!

(1.4.42.1.a) May Indra, well-pleased and accompanied by his troop of Maruts, drink the Soma, O wise hero, slayer of Vṛtra! Slay our enemies, drive away those who oppose us, and then grant us security from every side.
(1.4.42.1.b) You are taken with a support; for Indra, for the Ṣoḍaśin, you! This is your womb; for Indra, for the Ṣoḍaśin, you!
(1.4.43.1.a) His rays bear him aloft, the god Jātavedas, Sūrya, so that everyone may behold him.
The brilliant face of the gods has risen, the eye of Mitra, Varuṇa, and Agni. Sūrya has filled the heaven, the earth, and the mid-air; he is the soul of all that moves and stands still.
O Agni, lead us by a good path to wealth, O God who knowest all ways; drive away from us the sin that leads astray; we shall offer unto thee the most abundant speech of homage.
(1.4.43.1ḍ) Go to heaven; fly to the light with your form!
(1.4.43.1.e) With my own form I approach your form, with my own vitality your vitality.
(1.4.43.2.f) May Tutha, the all-knowing, distribute you upon the highest firmament.
(1.4.43.2.g) This gift of yours, O Agni, comes, distilling Soma.
(1.4.43.2.h) Lead it along the path of Mitra.
(1.4.43.2.i) Go forth by the path of *ṛta*, O you who possess brilliant sacrificial fees, leading us to prosperity by the path of the sacrifice.
(1.4.43.2.k) Today may I succeed with a Brāhmaṇa—a seer, of seer-lineage, having a father and a grandfather, and one who gives a gift of gold.
(1.4.43.2ḷ) Behold the light of heaven; behold the mid-air. (1.4.43.2ṃ) Strive together with those in the assembly hall.

(1.4.43.2ṇ) O you who have been given by us, go among the gods; full of sweetness, enter the giver. Without abandoning us, proceed by the path traveled by the gods and sit in the world of the doers of good deeds. (1.4.43.2.o) May that be prepared for us.
May Dhātṛ, Rāti, and Savitṛ enjoy this; may Prajāpati, the lord of treasures, and Agni; and Tvaṣṭṛ and Viṣṇu, bestowing offspring, grant wealth to the sacrificer.

O Indra, unite us with a favorable mind, with cattle, with wise patrons, O Maghavan, and with well-being; unite us with the sacred prayer (*brahman*) created by the gods, and with the benevolent goodwill of the gods worthy of sacrifice.
(1.4.44.1.c) We have united with splendor, with milk, with our bodies, and with a gracious mind. May Tvaṣṭṛ grant us wide space here. (1.4.44.2) May he smooth over whatever in our bodies is injured.

Since today, at this proceeding sacrifice, we have chosen you here, O Agni, as the Hotṛ—having sacrificed successfully and having performed the service successfully, come as one who knows, approaching the sacrifice with full awareness.
(1.4.44.2.e) "Welcome, O gods, we have prepared a seat for you who have come to this libation with favor. Having eaten and having drunk, all of you, O Vasus, bestow riches upon us."
O divine Agni, send forth those gods whom you have brought hither according to their desire; bearing and carrying the oblations, ascend to heaven along with the Vasu Gharma.
(1.4.44.3.g) O sacrifice, go to the sacrifice; go to the lord of the sacrifice; go to your own womb; svāhā!
(1.4.44.3ḥ) This is your sacrifice, O lord of the sacrifice, accompanied by the *sūktavāka* and rich in heroes; svāhā!
(1.4.44.3.i) O gods who know the way, having found the way, proceed upon the way.
O Lord of the mind, O God, place this sacrifice of ours among the gods; Svāhā! In speech, Svāhā! Place it in the wind!
(1.4.45.1.a) For King Varuṇa has made wide for Sūrya a path to follow; he has made feet to be set down where there was no place to stand, and he is the remover even of that which pierces the heart.

(1.4.45.1.b) A hundred are your physicians, O King, a thousand; let your benevolence be wide and deep. Drive away hatred and destruction far off; release us from whatever sin we have committed. (1.4.45.1.c) Varuṇa’s noose has been stepped upon.

(1.4.45.1.d) Agni’s face has entered the waters. The Son of the Waters, protecting his divine power, dwells in every house. (1.4.45.2) Offer the fuel-stick, O Agni! Let your tongue rise up toward the clarified butter.

(1.4.45.2.e) In the ocean is your heart, within the waters; may the plants and the waters enter into you. O Lord of the Sacrifice, with oblations we shall serve you at the *sūktavāka* and the *namovāka* of the sacrifice. (1.4.45.2.f) O *Avabhṛtha*, you who sink down, you who move downward, you who sink down! With the gods, you have expiated the sin committed against the gods; with mortals, you have expiated the sin committed against mortals. O God, protect us from wide-ranging harm. (1.4.45.2.g) May the waters and the plants be friendly to us; may they be unfriendly to him who hates us and whom we hate.

(1.4.45.3) O divine waters, this is your embryo; we have made it well-pleasing and well-sustained for you. Declare us as doers of good deeds among the gods. (1.4.45.3.i) Released is the noose of Varuṇa; cast off is the noose of Varuṇa. (1.4.45.3.k) You are fuel; may we prosper. You are kindling; you are splendor; bestow splendor upon me.
I have moved along the waters; we have been united with their essence. O Agni, I have come full of milk; endow me with splendor.
(1.4.46.1.a) O Jātavedas, I, a mortal, calling upon you, the immortal, with a humble heart, beseech you: bestow glory upon us; may I attain immortality through my offspring, O Agni.
O Agni Jātavedas, for that well-doer for whom you create a pleasant world, he shall attain, as his well-being, wealth consisting of horses, sons, heroes, and cattle.
In you, O son of strength, those who desire your favor have found fulfillment; nothing, O Indra, surpasses you.

At every hymn, O Soma, the pressed juices have exhilarated Indra; at every chant, the libations have gladdened Maghavan, when, like sons beseeching their father, they call upon him for aid with one accord and common resolve.
O Agni Jātavedas, you shine forth with sap and splendor, the slayer of Rākṣasas and the driver away of disease.
I have moved along the waters; we have been united with their essence. O Agni, rich in milk, I have come; endow me with splendor.
O Agni, you are indeed the Vasu, the lord of treasures, and rich in light; may we abide in your favor.

(1.4.46.2) O Agni, King of the sacrifice, I gladden you, the lord of riches among all treasures. (1.4.46.3) Through you, may we who strive for booty win the prize; may we overcome the hostile attacks of mortals.
(1.4.46.3.i) O Agni, the inspired singers magnify you, the best winner of booty, who are well-praised; as such, grant us great heroic strength.
(1.4.46.3.k) May this Agni create wide space for us; may he go before us, shattering our adversaries. May he, exulting, conquer the enemies; may he win the prize in the struggle for booty.
By Agni is Agni kindled—the sage, the master of the house, the youth, the bearer of oblations, whose mouth is the sacrificial ladle.
For you, O Agni, are kindled by fire; as a sage by a sage, as one who exists by one who exists, as a friend by a friend.
(1.4.46.3ṇ) Upward, O Agni, [rise] thy pure [flames]; (1.4.46.3.o) [extend] with thy light.

(1.5.1.1) The gods and the Asuras were engaged in conflict. When the gods were about to achieve victory, they deposited their desirable wealth in Agni, thinking, "This shall be ours if they should conquer us.
Agni desired that wealth for himself; he departed with it.
(1.5.1.1) Having conquered, the gods followed after it, desiring to recover it; they sought to seize it by force.
