Be born indeed at the beginning of days, O conqueror, placed among the well-placed, the ruddy one in the woods; bestowing seven treasures in every house, Agni, the most excellent sacrificer, has sat down as the Hotṛ priest.
(4.1.4.1.a) May Vāyu Mātariśvan restore for you, who lie supine, the heart that was injured. To him who moves by the breath of the gods, O Goddess, let there be *vaṣaṭ* to him and to you!
(4.1.4.1.b) Well-born together with light, you have taken your seat as a refuge and a protection, a heaven. O Agni, rich in radiance, clothe yourself in a garment of every form.
(4.1.4.1.c) Rise up, O you who perform the sacrifice well; come to us with divine grace, so that we may behold you with your great splendor, O Agni, shining brightly with excellent praises.
Stand up erect for our protection like the god Savitṛ; standing erect as the winner of booty when we, with ointments, call upon you together with the officiating priests.

(4.1.4.2.e) Once born, you are the embryo of heaven and earth, O Agni, lovely and distributed among the plants; as a brilliant infant, anointed against the darkness, you have gone forth from your mothers, crying aloud.
(4.1.4.2.f) Be firm, O you of strong limbs; be swift, O steed; be broad, you who carry the soil of Agni, so that you may sit comfortably.
(4.1.4.2.g) Be auspicious! (4.1.4.3) O Aṅgiras, be gracious toward the human offspring; do not burn against heaven and earth, nor the intermediate space, nor the trees.
(4.1.4.3) Let the vigorous steed go forward, neighing loudly, the braying donkey, flying along; bearing the Agni Purīṣya, may he not fall before his full span of life.
(4.1.4.3.i) The donkey, braying loudly, is well-yoked to your chariot, O two bulls; may he, swift as a messenger, carry you from here to Agni Purīṣya.
(4.1.4.3.k) Bearing the bull Agni, the bull, the offspring of the waters, the son of the ocean—O Agni, come hither for the feast! Right is truth.
(4.1.4.4ḷ) O plants, receive this Agni, the auspicious one, as he approaches you here. Dispelling all ignorance and hostilities, may he, settling down, strike away our evil thought.
(4.1.4.4ṃ) O plants, rejoice in him—ye who bear flowers and possess goodly fruit! This germ of yours, born in due season, has taken his seat in the ancient dwelling-place.

Flaring up with your broad radiance, drive away our enemies, the Rākṣasas, and diseases. May I abide in the protection of the great Agni, who grants excellent refuge, under the guidance of him who is easily invoked.
(4.1.5.1.b) O Waters, you are indeed the sources of bliss; grant us strength for great joy and for the sake of vision.
Whatever most auspicious essence you possess, grant us a share of it today, as longing mothers do for their children.
(4.1.5.1ḍ) Therefore, we come gladly to you, for whose dwelling you quicken us; O Waters, give us life.
(4.1.5.1.e) Mitra! (4.1.5.2) Having united the earth and the ground together with light, [I honor] Agni Vaiśvānara, the well-born Jātavedas, the all-pervading one.
(4.1.5.2.f) I unite you for health and for offspring. May all the gods belonging to all men unite you with the Ānuṣṭubh metre, in the manner of Aṅgiras.
(4.1.5.2.g) Having gathered together the earth, the Rudras kindled the great light; their unceasing, bright radiance shines among the gods.

(4.1.5.2) Having made with his two hands the soft clay, which has been mixed by the Vasus, the Rudras, and the wise ones, and is fit for the ritual work—may Sinīvālī fashion it. (4.1.5.3) That [clay].
(4.1.5.3.i) Sinīvālī, with beautiful braids, beautiful rings, and beautiful ornaments—may she, O Aditi, place the great fire-pan into your hands.
(4.1.5.3.k) May Aditi fashion the fire-pan with her power, her two arms, and her wisdom; as a mother bears her son in her lap, may she bear Agni within her womb.
(4.1.5.3ḷ) You are the head of Makha;
(4.1.5.3ṃ) you two are the two feet of the sacrifice.

(4.1.5.3) May the Vasus fashion you with the Gāyatrī metre, after the manner of Aṅgiras; you are the earth. May the Rudras fashion you with the Triṣṭubh metre, after the manner of Aṅgiras; you are the intermediate space. (4.1.5.4) May the Ādityas fashion you with the Jagatī metre, after the manner of Aṅgiras; you are the sky. May all the gods, belonging to all men, fashion you with the Anuṣṭubh metre, after the manner of Aṅgiras; you are the quarters. You are firm; bestow upon me offspring, increase of wealth, lordship over cattle, heroic vigor, and kinsmen for the sacrificer. (4.1.5.4.o) You are the girdle of Aditi.

(4.1.5.4.p) May Aditi grasp your cavity with the *pāṅkta* metre, in the manner of Aṅgiras. (4.1.5.4.q) Having fashioned that great earthen pan as a womb for Agni, Aditi delivered it over to her sons, saying, "Let him cook [the oblation] within it."

(4.1.6.1.a) May the Vasus fumigate thee with the Gāyatrī metre, in the manner of Aṅgiras; may the Rudras fumigate thee with the Triṣṭubh metre, in the manner of Aṅgiras; may the Ādityas fumigate thee with the Jagatī metre, in the manner of Aṅgiras; may the All-Gods, belonging to all men, fumigate thee with the Anuṣṭubh metre, in the manner of Aṅgiras; may Indra fumigate thee, in the manner of Aṅgiras; may Viṣṇu fumigate thee, in the manner of Aṅgiras; may Varuṇa fumigate thee, in the manner of Aṅgiras.
(4.1.6.1.b) May the goddess Aditi, accompanied by all the gods, dig a pit for you in the lap of the earth, in the manner of Aṅgiras.
(4.1.6.1.c) May the wives of the gods, the goddesses accompanied by all the gods, place you, O two wooden troughs, in the lap of the earth, in the manner of Aṅgiras.

(4.1.6.2ḍ) May the divine Dhiṣaṇās, accompanied by all the gods, kindle thee, O Ukha, in the lap of the earth, in the manner of Aṅgiras. May the divine Gnas, accompanied by all the gods, cook thee, O Ukha, in the lap of the earth, in the manner of Aṅgiras. May the divine Varūtris, the female progenitors, accompanied by all the gods, bake thee, O Ukha, in the lap of the earth, in the manner of Aṅgiras.
(4.1.6.2.e) O Mitra, bake this Ukha; let it not break.
(4.1.6.2.f) I entrust this to thee so that it may not be destroyed.

(4.1.6.2.g) By his greatness, Mitra has become coextensive with this heaven; and by his glory, he has overspread the earth. (4.1.6.3) Mitra has become coextensive with this heaven by his greatness; and by his glory, [he has overspread] the earth.
The glorious renown of the god Mitra, the sustainer of the people, which wins booty and possesses most brilliant fame.
(4.1.6.3.i) May the god Savitṛ, with beautiful hands, beautiful fingers, and beautiful arms, dig you up with his power.
(4.1.6.3.k) O Earth, sinking down, fill the regions and the quarters. Arise, become vast; stand upright, you who are steadfast.

(4.1.6.3ḷ) May the Vasus fashion you with the Gāyatrī metre, in the manner of Aṅgiras; may the Rudras fashion you with the Triṣṭubh metre, in the manner of Aṅgiras; may the Ādityas fashion you with the Jagatī metre, in the manner of Aṅgiras; may the All-Gods, belonging to all men, fashion you with the Anuṣṭubh metre, in the manner of Aṅgiras.
(4.1.7.1.a) O Agni, may the seasons, the years, the seers, and all that is true, strengthen you together. Shine forth with the celestial light; illuminate all the quarters of the earth.
(4.1.7.1.b) "Be kindled, O Agni, and awaken this man; arise for great good fortune! May no one sit near you, O Agni, in vain; may your *brahmans* be glorious, and not others."

(4.1.7.1.c) O Agni, these Brahmins choose you; be auspicious to us, O Agni, in our dwelling. As a slayer of rivals and a conqueror of those who plot against us, watch over our own home, never failing.

Right here, O Agni, bestow upon us wealth; let not the destroyers who were established before us humble thee. O Agni, may sovereignty be easy for thee to govern; may thy worshipper increase, unsubdued.

(4.1.7.2.e) O Agni, with sovereign power (*kṣatra*), grasp well-being for yourself; O Agni, strive for friendship in the bond of alliance. Be one who stands in the midst of your kinsmen; O Agni, worthy of invocation among kings, shine here!

(4.1.7.2.f) Overcome the attackers, overcome the plotters; overcome the thoughtless and overcome the enemy, O Agni! For you, O Agni, overcome all difficulties; therefore, grant us wealth together with heroic sons. For you, O Agni, overcome all difficulties; therefore, grant us wealth together with heroic sons. (4.1.7.3) Overcome the attackers, overcome the plotters; overcome the thoughtless and overcome the enemy, O Agni! For you, O Agni, overcome all difficulties; therefore, grant us wealth together with heroic sons. (4.1.7.3) Overcome the attackers, overcome the plotters; overcome the thoughtless and overcome the enemy, O Agni! For you, O Agni, overcome all difficulties; therefore, grant us wealth together with heroic sons. (4.1.7.3) Overcome the attackers, overcome the plotters; overcome the thoughtless and overcome the enemy, O Agni! For you, O Agni, overcome all difficulties; therefore, grant us wealth together with heroic sons. (4.1.7.3) Overcome the attackers, overcome the plotters; overcome the thoughtless and overcome the enemy, O Agni! For you, O Agni, overcome all difficulties; therefore, grant us wealth

Unassailable, Jātavedas, unconquered, the far-shining Agni, sustainer of dominion, shine here! Driving away all human fears from every quarter, protect us today with your auspicious powers for our prosperity.
O Bṛhaspati, O Savitṛ, awaken him; sharpen him further, even though he is already sharpened. Make him grow for great good fortune. May all the gods rejoice after him.

When you released [him] from the curse of Yama, O Bṛhaspati, so that he would not go to the world beyond; the Aśvins and the two physicians of the gods, O Agni, drove death away from him with their powers.
Beholding the higher light beyond the darkness, we have gone from among the gods to Sūrya, the god, the supreme light.
(4.1.8.1.a) His fuel-sticks rise upward, and the bright flames of Agni rise upward—the most radiant [flames] of the Son who has a beautiful countenance.
Tanūnapāt, the Asura, the all-knowing, the god among gods, anoints the paths with honey and ghee.
(4.1.8.1.c) O Agni, being gratified, you approach the sacrifice with honey; Narāśaṃsa is the god who performs good deeds, the impeller, the possessor of all boons.
(4.1.8.1ḍ) To this Agni comes the priest with power and clarity, praising him with reverence as the bearer of oblations when the ladles are extended in the sacrifices.
May he worship the majesty of this Agni; may he [enjoy] the offerings among the delightful songs—he who is the most wise Vasu and the greatest bestower of wealth.
(4.1.8.2.f) All the divine doors follow his ordinances; they belong to Agni, wide-extending, ruling according to their nature.
(4.1.8.2.g) May those two divine maidens, Dawn and Night, like [sisters] in their own womb, protect this sacrifice and our ritual service.
(4.1.8.2) O two divine Hotṛ-priests, elevate our sacrifice; praise the tongue of Agni, and make our oblation well-sacrificed.
(4.1.8.2.i) May the three goddesses—*Iḍā*, *Sarasvatī*, and the great *Bhāratī*—sit upon this sacred grass (*barhis*) while being praised.
May Tvaṣṭṛ release for us that wonderful seed, rich in food and full of heroic sons, an increase of wealth, and our very kinship.
O Lord of the Forest, being gracious, release [the victim] yourself among the gods; let Agni, the immolator, prepare the oblation.
(4.1.8.3ṃ) O Agni Jātavedas, perform the *svāhā* offering for Indra; may all the gods graciously accept this oblation.
In the beginning, Hiraṇyagarbha arose; once born, he was the sole lord of all that exists. He supported the earth and this heaven. To which god shall we offer worship with our oblation?
(4.1.8.4.o) He who by his greatness became the sole king of the breathing and blinking world; he who rules over these bipeds and quadrupeds—to what god shall we offer worship with our oblation?

He who bestows self and bestows strength, whose command all the worlds obey, and whose command even the gods obey; he whose shadow is immortality and whose [other side] is death—to what god shall we offer worship with our oblation?

(4.1.8.4.q) Of whom these Himālayas are by his greatness, and of whom they say the ocean is together with the Rasā; of whom these quarters are, and whose two arms they are—to what god shall we offer worship with our oblations?
To whom both the worlds, supported by his aid and trembling in their minds, looked up—over whom the risen sun moves forth—to what god shall we offer worship with our oblation?

By whom the formidable heaven and the earth were made firm, by whom the sun was established, and by whom the celestial vault; he who is the measurer of the mid-region within the space—unto what god shall we offer worship with our oblation?
When the great waters went forth, carrying all skill and generating Agni, from them there emerged the one life-force (*asus*) of the gods. To which god shall we offer worship with our oblation?
(4.1.8.6.u) He who by his greatness beheld the waters as they held creative power and brought forth Agni—he who was the one God above all gods—to what god shall we offer worship with our oblation?

(4.1.9.1.a) To intention, to Agni the impeller, *svāhā*! To mind, to wisdom, to Agni the impeller, *svāhā*! To thought, to what is discerned, to Agni the impeller, *svāhā*! To the restraint of speech, to Agni the impeller, *svāhā*! To Prajāpati, to Manu, *svāhā*! To Agni Vaiśvānara, *svāhā*!
(4.1.9.1.b) Every mortal should choose the friendship of the All-God, the Leader; everyone seeks wealth from him. Let one choose his splendor for prosperity, *svāhā*!
(4.1.9.1.c) Do not be afraid; do not be harmed! Be firm, be steadfast, O Mother! Be bold and act like a hero! (4.1.9.2) For you two shall perform this work together with Agni.
(4.1.9.2ḍ) Be firm, O Goddess Earth; for our well-being, you are a divine artifice fashioned by the *svadhā*-offering. May this oblation be pleasing to the gods; rise up uninjured at this sacrifice.
(4.1.9.2.e) O Mitra, heat this fire-pan; may it not break.
(4.1.9.2.f) I entrust this to you so that it may not be shattered.
(4.1.9.2.g) He who feeds on wood, whose libation is clarified butter, the ancient, excellent Hotṛ-priest, the wonderful son of strength.
(4.1.9.2) From the distant realm beyond, come hither toward those who are nearer! Protect those where I am. (4.1.9.3) Come hither toward those who are nearer! Protect those where I am.
From the furthest distance, O Lord of the Red Steeds, come hither; as the one who dwells in the soil, beloved by many, O Agni, do thou overcome our adversaries.
(4.1.9.3.k) Sit down in the lap of this mother, O Agni, you who know all ways. Do not burn her with your flame, nor scorch her with your heat; shine forth within her with pure light.
(4.1.9.3ḷ) O Agni, within your own seat, the fire-pan, with your radiance—burning it with your heat, O Jātavedas, be auspicious!
(4.1.9.3ṃ) Having become auspicious for me, O Agni, sit down as one who is auspicious; having made all the quarters auspicious, you have settled here in your own womb.
O Agni, whatever logs we place before you, let that be for you as clarified butter; accept it, O youngest one.
Whatever the ant eats, whatever the woodlouse crawls over—let all that be ghee for you; enjoy it, O youngest one!

Night after night, bringing unceasing offerings, we present nourishment to him as fodder for a standing horse; rejoicing in the increase of wealth and in food, O Agni, may we, your neighbors, not come to harm.

Upon the navel of the earth, we invoke Agni as he is kindled, for the increase of great wealth—the one who gladdens with delight, the one of lofty hymns, the worshipful, the victor, Agni, the subduer in battles.
The armies that are attacking, piercing, and fierce in their multitudes—those who are thieves and those who are robbers—all these I place within your mouth, O Agni.
With your two fangs, O Bhagavan, devour the night-prowlers; with your teeth, the thieves; and with your jaws, the robbers—devour them all so that they are well-chewed.
(4.1.10.2.g) Those who among the people are malicious, thieves, and robbers in the forest; those who in the thickets are intent on evil—these I place within your two jaws.
Whoever acts with hostility toward us, and whatever person hates us, whoever reviles us and seeks to harm us—reduce all of them to ashes!
Sharpened is my sacred formulation (*brahman*), sharpened is my heroism and strength; sharpened is the victorious sovereignty (*kṣatra*) of him for whom I am the domestic priest.
(4.1.10.3.k) I have raised up their arms; I have raised up their luster, I have raised up their strength. With my sacred word (*brahman*), I destroy the enemies; I lead my own people upward.
(4.1.10.4ḷ) Shining like gold, he has gleamed far and wide; his life is invincible, radiant for the sake of glory. Agni became immortal through his vital powers, when the prolific Heaven begat him.

The Seer puts on all forms; he has brought forth what is auspicious for the two-footed and the four-footed. Savitar, the most excellent, has looked out upon the firmament; he shines following the departure of the Dawn.

Night and Dawn, of one mind yet different forms, moving together, suckle the single infant. Like a golden ornament between heaven and earth, he shines forth; the gods, the givers of wealth, have sustained Agni.

(4.1.10.5.o) You are the fair-winged Garuḍa; the Trivṛt is your head, the Gāyatra your eye, the Stoma your soul, the Vāmadevya Sāman your body, the Bṛhat and Rathantara your wings, the Yajñāyajñīya your tail, the meters your limbs, the Dhiṣṇiya hearths your hooves, and the Yajus formulas your name.
(4.1.10.5.p) You are the fair-winged Garuḍa; go to the sky, fly to the light of heaven!
O Agni, whatever sacrifice or rite you encompass on every side, that indeed goes to the gods.
O Soma, with those bliss-bestowing aids of yours that exist for the donor, with those be our protector.
(4.1.11.1.c) Agni is the head.
(4.1.11.1ḍ) Of the world.
(4.1.11.1.e) O Soma, you for us.
(4.1.11.1.f) Those abodes of yours...
(4.1.11.1.g) We meditate upon that excellent splendor of the divine Savitṛ; may he impel our thoughts.

(4.1.11.1) Whatever we have done through lack of mindfulness toward the divine folk, with feeble skill and through human frailty; (4.1.11.2) O Savitṛ, among both gods and men, do you here impel us to be sinless.
Impelling the true words, awakening kind thoughts, Sarasvatī has established the sacrifice.

The daughter of the lightning, Sarasvatī, of wondrous life, the wife of heroes, bestows inspired thought. May she, in harmony with the divine dames, grant to the singer an unassailable refuge and flawless protection.
May Pūṣan follow after our cows; may Pūṣan protect our horses; may Pūṣan win booty for us.

(4.1.11.2) One part of you is bright, the other part is worthy of sacrifice; (4.1.11.3) like the sky, you possess two days of different forms. For you, O self-dependent one, protect all wondrous powers; O Pūṣan, may your bounty here be auspicious.

(4.1.11.3ṇ) They grew strong by their own power through their greatness; they ascended to the firmament and made for themselves a wide dwelling. When Viṣṇu ran toward the bull that distills exhilaration, they sat down like birds upon the beloved sacrificial grass.

(4.1.11.3.o) Offer forth a brilliant hymn to the singing, swift Marut host, who is strong by its own might—to those who overcome all powers with their own power! O Agni, the earth trembles before these fierce warriors.
(4.1.11.4.p) All the gods.
(4.1.11.4.q) All the gods.
(4.1.11.4ṛ) May Heaven and Earth today present this successful sacrifice, which reaches unto heaven, among the gods.
(4.1.11.4ṣ) Bring forward the two first-born parents with newest songs in the seat of Order. O Heaven and Earth, come to us with the divine host; great is your protection.
(4.1.11.4ṭ) Kindling the immortal Agni with a hymn of praise, awaken him so that he may place our oblations among the gods.
He, the immortal bearer of oblations, the eager messenger, well-disposed, Agni, brings [the gods] together through our prayer.
May they be auspicious for us in every contest.

(4.2.1.1.a) You are the stride of Viṣṇu, the slayer of the arrogant; ascend the Gāyatrī metre; stride forth along the earth; excluded is he whom we hate. You are the stride of Viṣṇu, the slayer of the accursed; ascend the Triṣṭubh metre; stride forth along the intermediate space; excluded is he whom we hate. You are the stride of Viṣṇu, the slayer of the hostile; ascend the Jagatī metre; stride forth along the sky; excluded is he whom we hate. You are the stride of Viṣṇu. (4.2.1.2) You are the stride.
The slayer of those who act as enemies, ascend the *anuṣṭubh* metre; stride out through the quarters; excluded is he whom we hate.

(4.2.1.2.b) Agni has roared like the thundering sky, licking the earth, anointing the plants. As soon as he was born, being kindled, he looked abroad; he shines with his splendor between the two worlds, heaven and earth.
(4.2.1.2.c) O Agni, you who turn back toward us, turn toward us with life-span, with splendor, with gain, with wisdom, with progeny, and with wealth!
O Agni Aṅgiras, may there be a hundred turnings for you, and a thousand turnings for you. By the increase of that prosperity, restore to us what we have lost; restore to us our wealth.
(4.2.1.3.e) Return again with vigor, O Agni, return with food and long life; protect us again from every side.
(4.2.1.3.f) Return with wealth, O Agni; overflow with a stream that nourishes all, from every side.
(4.2.1.3.g) O Varuṇa, loosen the highest bond from us, the lowest, and the middle one; then, O Āditya, being sinless in your service, may we belong to Aditi.
I have brought you hither; you have come within. Stand firm, immovable. Let all the people desire you; establish the kingdom upon this [throne].

(4.2.1.4.i) At the head of the dawns, the great one has stood upright; having emerged from darkness, he has come with light. Agni, the fair-limbed one, with his brilliant luster, having been born, has filled all dwellings.
(4.2.1.4.k) Sit down in the lap of this mother, O Agni, you who know all ways. Do not scorch her with your flame, nor consume her with your heat; shine forth within her with pure light.
(4.2.1.5ḷ) O Agni, within the fire-pan in your own seat, glowing with light—scorching it with your heat, O Jātavedas, be auspicious to us.
(4.2.1.5ṃ) Having become auspicious for me, O Agni, sit down as one who is auspicious; having made all the quarters auspicious, settle here in your own womb.

The swan dwelling in the pure, the Vasu dwelling in the mid-air, the priest dwelling at the altar, the guest dwelling in the house; dwelling among men, dwelling in the best places, dwelling in the sky, born of the waters, born of the kine, born of Truth, born of the mountains—the Great Truth.

(4.2.2.1.a) Agni was first born from heaven; for a second time, Jātavedas was born from us. A third time, he of manly mind was born in the waters. The pious man, kindling him, praises this eternal one.

(4.2.2.1.b) We know your three forms, O Agni, in three ways; we know your dwelling distributed in many places. We know your supreme name that is hidden in secret; we know that fountain from which you have come.

(4.2.2.1.c) The manly-minded one kindled you within the waters, in the ocean; O Agni, the beholder of men kindled you in the udder of heaven. The mighty ones urged you on, as you stood in the third realm, in the womb of Cosmic Order (*ṛta*).

Agni has roared like the thundering sky, licking the earth and anointing the plants. As soon as he was born, being kindled, he looked abroad; with his radiance, he shines between the two worlds, heaven and earth.
The eager, purifying, wise steward, the immortal Agni, has been established among mortals. Bearing aloft his ruddy smoke, he rises up; with his bright flame, he strives to reach the sky.
The banner of the universe, the germ of the world, being born, filled the two worlds; he split even the firm mountain as he went forth, when the five peoples sacrificed to Agni.

(4.2.2.3.g) The exalted source of glories, the supporter of riches, the impeller of great bulls, the guardian of Soma—the Son of the Vasu and of Might, the King in the waters—shines forth, kindled at the forefront of the dawns.

(4.2.2.3) O Agni, you of auspicious luster, whoever today prepares for you a cake rich in ghee, O God—lead him further toward greater prosperity, and toward the glory allotted by the gods, O youngest one.

(4.2.2.3.i) Partake of that, O Agni, in glorious deeds; partake at every hymn being recited. May he be dear to Sūrya, dear to Agni; may he excel through what has been born and through what is yet to be born.
(4.2.2.4.k) O Agni, day after day, the sacrificers have placed all desirable treasures within you. Seeking wealth through you, the yearning ones have opened the cow-stall.

Visible like a golden ornament, he has shone forth widely; resplendent for the sake of glory, he has attained an invincible lifespan. Agni became immortal through his vital powers when the prolific Heaven begat him.
(4.2.3.1.a) O Lord of Food, grant us food that is free from disease and full of vigor. Further the giver; bestow strength upon our bipeds and our quadrupeds.
(4.2.3.1.b) May all the gods lift you up, O Agni, with their thoughts. Be most auspicious to us, fair of face, rich in light.
(4.2.3.1.c) O Agni, go forward, radiant with light, with your auspicious flames; shining with great beams, do not harm our offspring with your body.
(4.2.3.1ḍ) Worship Agni with fuel; awaken the guest with clarified butter. Offer the oblations into him.
(4.2.3.2.e) This Agni of Bharata is heard afar, as he shines forth with great light like the sun; he who has stood firm against the Pūru in battles, the divine guest, has shone for us auspiciously.
(4.2.3.2.f) O divine waters, receive this ash; place it in a pleasant and fragrant world. Let wives with noble husbands bow down before it; bear it well, as a mother bears her son.
(4.2.3.2.g) O Agni, your seat is in the waters; (4.2.3.3) you grow along with the plants; being in the womb, you are born again.
(4.2.3.3) You are the embryo of the plants, the embryo of the forest trees; you are the embryo of all that exists, O Agni, you are the embryo of the waters.
(4.2.3.3.i) Having propitiated the womb with ashes, and having united with the waters and the earth, O Agni, you have sat down again, radiant, together with your mothers.
(4.2.3.3.k) Having settled again upon your seat, O Agni, you lie upon the waters and the earth, most auspicious within her, as if in the lap of a mother.
(4.2.3.3ḷ) Return again with vigor! (4.2.3.4) Return again, O Agni, with food and long life; protect us again from every side.
(4.2.3.4ṃ) Return with wealth, O Agni; swell with a stream that nourishes all, from every side.

(4.2.3.4ṇ) May the Ādityas, the Rudras, and the Vasus kindle you again; may the Brahmins, O leader of wealth, [kindle you] again with sacrifices. May you cause your bodies to grow with clarified butter; may the desires of the sacrificer come true.

(4.2.3.4.o) O youngest one, master of self-power, take note of this speech of ours, most bountiful and well-offered! One person reviles, another praises; I, your worshipper, laud your very body, O Agni.
May he, the wise sage, the bounteous lord, the giver of wealth, the master of riches, drive away from us all enmities.

Depart, go away, and creep away from here—those who are here, both the ancient ones and those who are recent. Yama has given this dwelling-place on earth; the fathers have prepared this world for him.
(4.2.4.1.b) You are the ash of Agni; you are the soil of Agni. (4.2.4.1.c) You are consciousness, the sustainer of desires; may your sustaining of my desires be with me.

(4.2.4.1.d) Those bodies of yours which are dear, and those hearts of yours which are dear—may your self be united [with us]. (4.2.4.2) May I be united with [you], and may my bodies be united with [you].
(4.2.4.2.e) This is that Agni in whom Indra, longing for him, has placed the pressed Soma within his belly; having won thousandfold booty like a swift steed, you are praised, O Jātavedas.

(4.2.4.2.f) O Agni, you go toward the flood of heaven; you have called upon the gods who are worthy of worship. [We call] those waters which are beyond the luminous realm of the sun, and those which stand below it.

(4.2.4.2.g) O Agni, that splendor of yours which is in heaven, on earth, and in the plants—(4.2.4.3) or in the waters, O worshipful one—by which you have spread across the wide mid-air: may that light of yours be brilliant, surging, and beholding men.
(4.2.4.3) May the fires of the soil, in harmony with those of the slopes, graciously accept the offered oblation and grant great, disease-free nourishments.

(4.2.4.3.i) O Agni, bestow upon the one who invokes you the *iḍā*-offering, the many-wondrous gain of cattle, most constant for all time. May there be to us a son, a spreading progeny; O Agni, may that benevolence of yours be with us.
(4.2.4.3.k) This is your seasonal womb, from which, once born, you shone forth; knowing it, O Agni, ascend it, and then increase our wealth. (4.2.4.4)
(4.2.4.4ḷ) You are consciousness; by that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras.
(4.2.4.4ṃ) You are the surrounding layer; by that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras.
(4.2.4.4ṇ) Fill the world, fill the gap, and then sit down, you who are auspicious. Indra, Agni, and Bṛhaspati have seated you in this womb.
(4.2.4.4.o) These dappled cows, yielding milk for the preparation, mix the Soma for him; they are the subjects at the birth of the gods, in the three luminous realms of heaven.

Come together! Be united; be well-disposed and radiant, being of one mind. Dwelling together for the sake of food and vigor, I have brought your minds into harmony, your vows into harmony, and your thoughts into harmony.
(4.2.5.1.b) O Agni of the soil, be our protector; bestow nourishment and vigor upon the sacrificer.
(4.2.5.1.c) O Agni, you who dwell in the soil, you are possessed of wealth and prosperity; having made all directions auspicious, sit here upon your own birthplace.
(4.2.5.1ḍ) Be you two of one mind and one dwelling for us! (4.2.5.2) Be you two stainless! Do not harm the sacrifice, nor the lord of the sacrifice, O Jātavedas; be auspicious to us today!

As a mother her son, the earth—the fire-pan—has borne Agni, the filler of the soil, in his own womb. May Prajāpati Viśvakarman, being in harmony with all the gods and the seasons, release him from it.
That brilliant light which was born for him beyond this atmospheric realm—may that carry us across our enemies, O Agni Vaiśvānara; Svāhā!
(4.2.5.2.g) Homage be to you, O Nirṛti of every form! (4.2.5.3) Untie this iron bond! In agreement with Yama and Yamī, cause this man to ascend to the highest heaven.

(4.2.5.3) That bond which the goddess Nirṛti fastened upon your necks, so that it could not be loosened—that bond of yours I now unfasten from the midst of your life. Thus, being released, live on as a living man and eat your food.

(4.2.5.3.i) Into that cruel mouth of yours, I offer this [oblation] for the release from these bonds. People know you as "Earth," but I know you from every side as Nirṛti. (4.2.5.4) Thus do I encompass you on all sides.

Seek out the one who does not press the soma and does not sacrifice; follow the track of the thief and the robber. Seek someone other than us—this is your portion. O Goddess Nirṛti, let there be homage to you!
(4.2.5.4ḷ) Praising the goddess Nirṛti, I subdue her with my words as a father does his son. She who knows the head of every being as it is born, the wise one, beholds it in every head.
The dweller, the gatherer of riches, he beholds all forms with his powers; like the god Savitṛ whose laws are true, he stands like Indra at the meeting-place of the paths.
(4.2.5.5ṇ) "Fasten the straps together; prepare the water-buckets! Let us pour into the water-hold that is full of water, a never-failing reservoir for all time."
I pour out the water from the well that has its mouth fashioned, its buckets well-fastened, and its pouring easy; it is full of water, inexhaustible.
(4.2.5.5.p) The sages yoke the ploughs; they stretch out the yokes separately, the wise ones, seeking favor among the gods.

(4.2.5.5.q) Yoke the ploughs, stretch out the yokes; sow the seed here in the prepared womb. May our song and our prompt obedience be shared together; may the ripened grain come closer to us than the sickle.
The plough, sharp-pointed, very auspicious, with a well-fashioned handle—this indeed furrows the earth for cattle, sheep, and a fat, swelling crop; it is like a chariot-bearer carrying its load.

May our ploughshares cleave the earth auspiciously; may the ploughmen go happily toward their draft-animals. May Parjanya [bestow] auspiciousness with honey and milk; O Śunāsīras, bestow auspiciousness upon us!
(4.2.5.6ṭ) O yielder of desires, milk forth desire for Mitra and Varuṇa, for Indra and Agni, for Pūṣan, for the plants, and for all creatures.
(4.2.5.6.u) Anointed with ghee and honey, approved by all the gods and the Maruts, full of vigor and swelling with milk—O Furrow, turn toward us with your milk!
(4.2.6.1.a) Of those herbs that were born for the gods three ages ago, I celebrate the hundred and seven abodes of the brown ones.
(4.2.6.1.b) A hundred, O Mothers, are your abodes, and a thousand are your growths; therefore, you who possess a hundred powers, make this [child] of mine free from disease.
(4.2.6.1.c) The plants—those that bear flowers, those that bring forth fruit, those that are fruitful, and those that are fruitless—are like victorious mares; they are the ones who carry us across.
(4.2.6.1ḍ) "O plants," so I address you, O goddesses, my mothers; driving away misfortunes, drive away evil from here. (4.2.6.2) Driving [it] away.
(4.2.6.2.e) On the *aśvattha* tree is your seat; on the *parṇa* leaf is your dwelling made. You shall indeed be sharers of cattle, if you win back the man.
When I, seeking strength, place these herbs in my hand, the self of the wasting disease perishes, as if before one who seizes the living.
When the plants come together like kings in an assembly, he is called the wise physician, the slayer of demons and the driver away of disease.
(4.2.6.2) "Niṣkṛti" is the name of your mother; thus you are the Saṃkṛtis. You are the winged streams. (4.2.6.3) Whatever is diseased, you heal it.
(4.2.6.3.i) Let one among you protect the other; let each assist the next. May all those plants, being in full agreement, favor this speech of mine.
(4.2.6.3.k) The swelling powers of the plants surge forth like cows from the cow-pen, seeking to win wealth for you, O man.
They have stepped over all obstacles as a thief passes through a pen; the plants have shaken off whatever blemish was upon their bodies.
(4.2.6.3) Those which have occupied your self, those which have entered you joint by joint—let them drive away your consumption, like a fierce one who sits in the midst. (4.2.6.4)
(4.2.6.4ṇ) Fly away, O consumption, together with the hawk, with the blue jay; vanish together with the rush of the wind, together with the whirlwind!
(4.2.6.4.o) Rich in horses, rich in Soma, strengthening, and full of vigor—I have gathered all these plants for this man’s safety.
Those that bear fruit and those that are fruitless, those that are flowerless and those that are flowering—impelled by Bṛhaspati, may they release us from distress.

(4.2.6.4.q) Those plants whose king is Soma, which have entered into the earth—of these you are the best; impel us toward life. (4.2.6.5) Those plants whose king is Soma, which have entered into the earth—of these you are the best; impel us toward life.
As they descended from heaven, the plants spoke: "The living man whom we shall reach, that person shall not come to harm."
Those who hear this and those who have gone far away—all of you, having gathered here, bestow healing medicine upon him.
(4.2.6.5ṭ) May he who digs you not be harmed, nor he for whom I dig you. May our bipeds and quadrupeds all be free from disease.
The plants converse together with Soma the king: "O King, we shall carry across that man for whom the Brahmin performs [this rite]."

May he not harm us, who is the progenitor of the earth, or he who, possessing true law, generated heaven, and who generated the great, shining waters—to which god shall we offer worship with our oblation?
Turn toward us, O Earth, together with the sacrifice and the milk; may Agni, impelled, glide over your omentum.
O Agni, that which is yours—the bright, the radiant, the purified, and the worthy of sacrifice—that we bring to the gods.

(4.2.7.1ḍ) Food and strength I take from here, from the abode of Cosmic Order, from the womb of immortality. May it enter into our cattle and our plants! I leave behind exhaustion, lack of nourishment, and disease.
(4.2.7.2.e) O Agni, yours is glory and vital strength; great and radiant are your flames, O Vibhāvasu. O Bṛhadbhānu, through your power you bestow praiseworthy booty upon the donor, O Sage.

(4.2.7.2.f) O Agni, ruling over all, spread yourself out with living beings; bestow upon us riches, O Immortal One! You shine forth with a form worthy to be seen; you grant us wealth that wins the prize.

(4.2.7.2.g) O Son of Strength, Jātavedas, rejoice in our excellent praises! (4.2.7.3) Being well-disposed through our prayers, in you the many-seeded ones, who possess wondrous aids and noble births, have gathered their nourishments.

(4.2.7.3) With purifying luster, with bright luster, with undiminished luster, you rise up with your radiance. Moving between your two parents like a son, you protect them; you fill both the worlds, heaven and earth.

(4.2.7.3.i) For the sake of favor, men have placed before them Agni, the observer of Truth, the mighty one, the lord of all people; you, the divine one with ears that hear, most far-reaching, the human generations honor with their song.

(4.2.7.3.k) You bestow wealth—the fulfiller of the sacrifice, the wise one, who rules for great bounty, the gift of the Bhr̥gus, the eager one, possessing the insight of a seer, the winner of spoils. (4.2.7.4) [Bestow] wealth!
(4.2.7.4ḷ) You are piled, you are piled around; being piled upwards, take your place! With that deity, in the manner of Aṅgiras, sit firm.
(4.2.7.4ṃ) Swell up; let virility come to you from every side, O Soma; be present at the gathering of the prize.

(4.2.7.4ṇ) May thy milks come together, and let thy strengths and thy bull-like powers that overcome the enemy gather. Swelling for the sake of immortality, O Soma, bestow upon us the highest glories in heaven.

He has overcome all hostile armies; this Agni has declared, and Soma has likewise declared it. Bṛhaspati and Savitṛ have told me this: Puṣan shall establish me in the world of the well-performed deed.

When you first neighed at birth, rising from the ocean or from the primordial waters—that birth of yours was like the wings of a falcon or the forelegs of a deer; O steed, that birth of yours is worthy of praise.

(4.2.8.1.c) You are the back of the waters, the womb of Agni, swelling all around the ocean; increasing in greatness, (4.2.8.2) extend the lotus-leaf of heaven according to its measure and by its color.
(4.2.8.2ḍ) Brahma, being born, first from the east, Vena revealed from the radiant horizon. He disclosed its lowest and highest stations, the womb of both the existent and the non-existent.

In the beginning, the Golden Embryo (Hiraṇyagarbha) came into being; once born, he was the sole Lord of all that exists. He supported this earth and yonder sky. To which god shall we offer worship with our oblation?

(4.2.8.2.f) The drop has fallen upon the earth, (4.2.8.3) upon this heaven, and upon this womb as well as that which was before; following the third womb as it moves about, I offer the drop according to the seven priestly offices.
(4.2.8.3.g) Homage be to the serpents, whichever ones are upon the earth; those who are in the intermediate space and those who are in heaven—to those serpents, homage!
(4.2.8.3) To those who are there in the bright realm of heaven, or those who are in the rays of the sun, and those whose seat is established in the waters—to those serpents, homage!
Homage to those serpents who belong to the sorcerers, or who dwell among the trees, or who lie in holes.
(4.2.9.1.a) You are firm, a supporting base, spread out by Viśvakarman, well-fashioned. Let not the ocean destroy you, nor the Suparṇa; being unshakable, make the earth firm.

(4.2.9.1.b) May Prajāpati settle you upon the back of the earth—expansive, wide-reaching. You are extension; you are the earth; you are the world; you are the ground; you are Aditi, the all-sustaining, the upholder of the entire universe. Support the earth; make firm the earth; do not harm the earth! For the sake of every out-breath, diffused breath, and up-breath, for the sake of stability and for movement. (4.2.9.2) May Agni protect you with great well-being, with a most peaceful shelter. By that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras.
(4.2.9.2.c) Growing forth from joint to joint, from knot to knot, even so, O *dūrvā* grass, spread out for us with a thousandfold and a hundredfold!
(4.2.9.2ḍ) O divine brick, you who spread yourself with a hundred and sprout forth with a thousand—to you we shall offer worship with an oblation.

(4.2.9.2.e) You are the invincible, the subduer; subdue the enemies, subdue those who act as enemies. (4.2.9.2.f) Subdue the hostile armies, subdue those who attack; you possess thousandfold power—(4.2.9.3) as such, quicken me!
(4.2.9.3.g) Honeyed are the winds for the one who follows the cosmic order; honey do the rivers flow. May the plants be sweet for us.
(4.2.9.3) May the night be honey-sweet, and may the dawn be honey-sweet; may the earthly realm be full of honey, and may our Father Heaven be honey-sweet for us.
May the Lord of the Forest be full of sweetness for us; may the Sun be full of sweetness; may the cows be sweet for us.
(4.2.9.3.k) May the great Heaven and Earth sprinkle this sacrifice for us; may they fill us with nourishments.
(4.2.9.3) That supreme abode of Viṣṇu, (4.2.9.4) the wise ever behold, like an eye stretched across the sky.
(4.2.9.4ṃ) You are firm, O Earth; overcome those who attack us. Woven together with the gods, you have come through immortality.
O Agni, those splendors of yours which, when the sun has risen, spread across the sky with its rays—by means of all of them, grant splendor to this person for us.
(4.2.9.4.o) O gods, those splendors of yours that are in the sun, those splendors that are in the cows and in the horses—with all of them, O Indra and Agni, bestow splendor upon us, O Bṛhaspati.

(4.2.9.4.p) The Virāj has established the light; the Samrāj has established the light; the Svarāj has established the light. (4.2.9.5.q) O Agni, yoke indeed those horses of yours, O god, which are excellent; the swift ones carry [you] well.
(4.2.9.5ṛ) Harness, O Agni, like a charioteer, the steeds who best invoke the gods; sit down as the ancient Hotṛ-priest.
The drop has fallen upon the earth and across the sky, following this womb and that which was before; I offer the drop as it moves along the third womb, according to the seven priestly offices.
(4.2.9.6ṭ) This has become the vigor of the entire world and of Agni Vaiśvānara. Agni is radiant with light; he is a golden disk, glorious with splendor.

(4.2.9.6.u) For the Ṛc, for the Ruc, thee! (4.2.9.6.v) Together they flow, like rivers, the milky streams, purified within by the heart and the mind; I gaze upon the streams of clarified butter; in their midst stands the golden reed.
Upon it sits the fair-winged bird, the honey-maker, nest-building, distributing honey to the deities. Upon its bank sit seven bay horses, milking the self-sustaining stream of nectar.
Anointing the Āditya-embryo with milk, the thousandfold counterpart of all forms—encompass it with your heat; do not strike it, but grant it a life of a hundred years as you are being piled.
(4.2.10.1.b) Do not harm this two-footed animal, O thousand-eyed one, while the sacrifice is being piled. I assign to you the wild antelope; building up your own bodies with that, sit down.

(4.2.10.1.c) The speed of the wind, the navel of Varuṇa, the horse born in the midst of the flood—do not harm the infant of the rivers, the tawny one awakened by the stones, O Agni, in the highest heaven! (4.2.10.2) In the highest firmament!
(4.2.10.2ḍ) Do not harm this one-hoofed animal among cattle, the neighing steed amidst the prize-winning races. I assign to you the wild ox; building up your bodies with that, settle down.

(4.2.10.2.e) With prostrations, I praise in the first thought Agni—the unceasing, ruddy, and restless drop. May you, fashioning yourself according to the joints and the seasons, not harm the cow, Aditi, the radiant one.

(4.2.10.2.f) This ocean, a fountain with a hundred streams, spreading out in the midst of the world—Aditi, who yields clarified butter for the sake of mankind—O Agni, do not harm her in the highest heaven! I assign to you the wild gavaya; building up your bodies with it, sit down.

(4.2.10.3.g) O Agni, do not harm the protective guardian of Tvaṣṭṛ, the navel of Varuṇa, the ewe born from beyond the realm of space, the great and thousandfold creative power (*māyā*) of the Asura, in the highest heaven.

(4.2.10.3) This woolly skin of Varuṇa, the magic power of animals, biped and quadruped—the first birthplace of Tvaṣṭṛ’s progeny—O Agni, do not harm it in the highest heaven! Following the wild camel, (4.2.10.4) I assign it to you; building up your bodies with that, sit down.
(4.2.10.4.i) That Agni who was born from the heat of Agni, from the glow of the earth or from the sky, by whom Viśvakarman pervaded all creatures—may thy wrath, O Agni, spare him.

(4.2.10.4.k) For the goat was born from the womb of Agni; she indeed beheld the progenitor in the beginning. By her, the worthy ones attained the ascent; by her, the gods attained divinity in the beginning. I assign to you the wild *śarabha*; piling [the fire] with it, settle down within your bodies.
O Indra and Agni, you adorn the luminous realms of heaven during the contests for booty; that heroic deed of yours is renowned far and wide.
He pierces Vṛtra and wins booty—he who honors Indra and Agni, the two victorious ones, who rule over abundant wealth, most powerful through their might, and striving for victory.

(4.2.11.1.c) You two surpass all people in the calls of battle; you surpass both the earth and the sky in greatness; you surpass the rivers and the mountains in majesty; O Indra and Agni, you surpass all other beings.
O Maruts, he in whose dwelling you drink [the soma] from heaven, O you of great luster—he is the person most well-protected.
O Maruts, you who are borne by sacrifices, listen to the sacrifice or to the hymns of the inspired singer; hear our invocation!

(4.2.11.2.f) For the sake of glory, they have mingled themselves with splendors; they, with their rays and their singers, are easy to invoke. Armed with axes and impetuous, yet fearless, they have found the beloved domain of the Marut host.
(4.2.11.2.g) Away with your anger;
(4.2.11.2.h) up [the knot] that is highest.
(4.2.11.2.i) With what aid will the wonderful one come to us, he who is ever-increasing as our friend? With what most powerful host?

(4.2.11.3.k) Who today yokes to the pole the oxen of the Truth—those who are vigorous, impetuous, and difficult to provoke; who have arrows in their mouths, dwell in the heart, and are sources of bliss? Only he who fulfills their service shall live.
(4.2.11.3ḷ) O Agni, lead us.
(4.2.11.3ṃ) To the gods. (4.2.11.3ṇ) May they be auspicious to us.
(4.2.11.3.o) In every contest for booty; (4.2.11.3.p) O Agni, your seat is in the waters; you penetrate the plants, and being in their womb, you are born again.
(4.2.11.3.q) O Soma, you are a bull, full of splendor; O God, you are a bull whose ordinances are bull-like. As a bull, you uphold the sacred laws.
(4.2.11.3ṛ) This [prayer] of mine, O Varuṇa; (4.2.11.3ṣ) for that I entreat you;
(4.2.11.3ṭ) you, O Agni, [are] for us.
As such, O Agni, be thou for us.
(4.3.1.1.a) I settle you in the movement of the waters; I settle you in the rising of the waters; I settle you in the heat of the waters; I settle you in the light of the waters;

I settle you in the course of the waters. (4.3.1.1.b) Sit in the ocean as your seat; sit in the sea as your seat; sit in the flood as your seat; sit in the abode of the waters; sit in the gathering-place of the waters. (4.3.1.1.c) I settle you in the seat of the waters; I settle you in the common dwelling of the waters; I settle you in the soil of the waters; I settle you in the womb of the waters; I settle you in the domain of the waters.
The Gāyatrī metre, the Triṣṭubh metre, the Jagatī metre, the Anuṣṭubh metre, and the Paṅkti metre.

(4.3.2.1.a) This one here is Purobhū; his breath is Bhauvāyana; the spring is Prāṇāyana; the Gāyatrī belongs to the spring; from the Gāyatrī comes the Gāyatra [Sāman]; from the Gāyatra comes the Upāṃśu [cup]; from the Upāṃśu comes the Trivṛt [Stoma]; from the Trivṛt comes the Rathantara [Sāman]; from the Rathantara comes the seer Vasiṣṭha. With thee, taken by Prajāpati, I take hold of the breath for the sake of offspring.

(4.3.2.1.b) This southern [cup] is Viśvakarman; his mind belongs to Viśvakarman; the summer season belongs to the mind; the *triṣṭubh* meter belongs to the summer; from the *triṣṭubh* comes the *aiḍa* chant; from the *aiḍa* comes the *antaryāma* cup; from the *antaryāma* comes the fifteenfold stoma; from the fifteenfold comes the *bṛhat* sāman; from the *bṛhat* comes the seer Bharadvāja. With thee, taken by Prajāpati, I take the mind for the sake of offspring. (4.3.2.2) I take the mind for the sake of offspring.

(4.3.2.2.c) This [breath] behind is the all-pervading; its [offspring] is the sight, the all-pervading; the rainy season is the offspring of sight; the *jagatī* meter is the offspring of the rainy season; from the *jagatī* comes the *ṛkṣama* chant; from the *ṛkṣama* comes the *śukra* cup; from the *śukra* comes the seventeenfold stoma; from the seventeenfold comes the *vairūpa* chant; from the *vairūpa* comes the seer Viśvāmitra. With thee, taken by Prajāpati, I take sight for my offspring.

(4.3.2.2ḍ) This [is from] the *uttara* [stotra] of the *suva*; its ear is the *sauva*; the *śarad* [season] is the *śrautri*; the *anuṣṭubh* [meter] is the *śāradya*; from the *anuṣṭubh* comes the *svāra* [sāman]; from the *svāra* comes the *manthin* [cup]; from the *manthin* comes the twenty-one-fold [stoma]; from the twenty-one-fold comes the *vairāja* [sāman]; from the *vairāja* comes Jamadagni the seer. With thee, taken by Prajāpati—(4.3.2.3)—I take the ear for the sake of offspring.

(4.3.2.3.e) This is the upper mind; speech is its mother. Winter is the [season] belonging to speech; the *paṅkti* meter belongs to winter. From the *paṅkti* comes the *nidhanavat* [stotra]; from the *nidhanavat* comes the *āgrayaṇa* cup. From the *āgrayaṇa* come the twenty-sevenfold and thirty-threefold [stomas]. From the twenty-sevenfold and thirty-threefold come the *śākvara* and *raivata* [sāmans]. From the *śākvara* and *raivata* comes Viśvakarman the seer. With thee, taken by Prajāpati, I take up speech for the sake of all creatures.

(4.3.3.1.a) The eastern quarter of the quarters; spring of the seasons; Agni the deity; the Brahman as wealth; the *trivṛt* hymn-form; it has fifteen paths; the three-year-old steer is the age; the Kṛta is among the throws of the dice; the east wind is the wind; Sānaga is the seer. (4.3.3.1.b) The southern quarter of the quarters; summer of the seasons; Indra the deity; the *kṣatra* as wealth; the *pañcadaśa* hymn-form; it has seventeen paths; the two-year-old bull is the age; the Tretā is among the throws of the dice; the south wind is the wind; Sanātana is the seer.

(4.3.3.1.c) The western direction; the rainy season of the seasons; the Viśve Devas as the deity; wealth; the seventeenfold hymn-form (*stoma*); it has twenty-one turnings; the two-year-old steer is the age; the Dvāpara is among the throws of the dice; the wind from behind is the wind; Ahabhūna is the seer. (4.3.3.2d) The northern direction; the autumn of the seasons; Mitra and Varuṇa as the deities; prosperity as the wealth; the twenty-onefold hymn-form; it has twenty-seven turnings; the four-year-old draught-ox is the age; the leaper is among the throws of the dice; the wind from the north is the wind; Pratna is the seer.

(4.3.3.2.e) The upward direction; the winter and cool seasons of the seasons; Bṛhaspati the deity; splendor the wealth; the twenty-sevenfold hymn-form; it is also the thirty-threefold path; the draft-ox the age; the overcomer of enemies; the wind blowing in all directions; the wind; the eagle the seer. (4.3.3.2.f) Fathers, grandfathers, those beyond and those below—may they protect us, may they favor us in this sacred word (*brahman*), in this dominion (*kṣatra*), in this blessing, in this priestly office, in this rite, and in this invocation of the gods.

(4.3.4.1.a) Firmly established, of firm origin, you are firm; sit upon a firm seat, O Sādhya. Let the Aśvins, the two Adhvaryu priests, establish you here as the first banner of the fire-pan in the east.

(4.3.4.1.b) Sit here upon your own skill, O Father of Skill; among the gods, upon the vast earth, bestowing gifts. Enter into this well-prepared seat with your body; be as a father is to his son, most gracious. May the Aśvins, the two Adhvaryu priests, establish you here.

(4.3.4.1.c) Nest-like, earthy, bestowing vital strength, increase for us abundant wealth with many heroic sons! (4.3.4.2) Driving away ignorance and ill-will, granting the lord of the sacrifice a share in the nourishment of riches, bestow upon the sacrificer the prosperity of heaven; may the two Aśvins, the Adhvaryus, settle you here.

(4.3.4.2ḍ) You are the soil of Agni, the path leading to the gods; may all the gods acclaim you. Seated here upon the back of the *stoma*, rich in ghee, grant us wealth accompanied by progeny; may the two Aśvins, acting as *adhvaryu* priests, settle you here.

(4.3.4.2.e) You are the head of heaven, the navel of the earth, the support of the quarters, the sovereign lady of all beings. (4.3.4.3) You are the wave, the drop of the waters; Viśvakarman is your seer. O Aśvins, as the two Adhvaryu priests, may you establish me here.

(4.3.4.3.f) In harmony with the seasons, in harmony with the divisions, in harmony with the Vasus, in harmony with the Rudras, in harmony with the Ādityas, in harmony with all the gods, in harmony with the gods, in harmony with the gods who provide vital strength—for Agni Vaiśvānara, may the two Aśvins, the Adhvaryus, establish you here. (4.3.4.3.g) Guard my out-breath; guard my in-breath; guard my diffused breath. Let your eye shine forth widely; make my hearing resonant. (4.3.4.3.h) Make the waters swell; quicken the plants. Protect the bipeds; protect the quadrupeds. Send down rain from heaven.
(4.3.5.1) Tryavi is the age, Triṣṭubh the metre;
(4.3.5.1) Dityavāḍ is the age, Virāj the metre;
(4.3.5.1) Pañcāvi is the age, Gāyatrī the metre.
The three-year-old steer is the age; the *uṣṇih* is the metre. The four-year-old steer is the age; the *anuṣṭubh* is the metre. The five-year-old steer is the age; the *bṛhatī* is the metre.
(4.3.5.1) The bull is the vigor; the *satobṛhatī* is the meter. (4.3.5.1) The bull is the vigor; the *kakubh* is the meter. (4.3.5.1) The cow is the vigor; the *jagatī* is the meter.
(4.3.5.1) The ox is the age; the *paṅkti* is the metre. (4.3.5.1) The ram is the age; the *vivala* is the metre. (4.3.5.1) The bull is the age; the *viśāla* is the metre.
The man is the age; *tandra* is the metre. The tiger is the age; *anādhṛṣṭa* is the metre. The lion is the age; *chadis* is the metre.
Viṣṭambha is the age, Adhipati the metre; Kṣatra is the age, Mayada the metre;
Viśvakarman is the age, Parameṣṭhin the metre.
(4.3.5.1) Mūrdhan, Vayaḥ, Prajāpati, and Chandas.
(4.3.6.1.a) O Indra and Agni, do you two make firm the unswerving brick; let it push apart heaven and earth and the intermediate space with its back.

(4.3.6.1.b) May Viśvakarman settle you upon the back of the mid-region—broad, expansive, radiant, and full of light—you who shine upon the sky, upon the earth, and across the wide mid-region. Support the mid-region; make firm the mid-region; do not harm the mid-region! For the sake of all out-breathing, in-breathing, diffused breathing, and upward breathing, for stability and for movement, may Vāyu protect you with great well-being and most peaceful shelter. By that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras!

(4.3.6.2.c) You are the Queen, the eastern quarter; you are the Virāj, the southern quarter; you are the Sovereign, the western quarter; you are the Self-Ruling, the northern quarter; you are the Overlord, the great quarter. (4.3.6.2ḍ) Protect my life-span; protect my out-breath; protect my in-breath; protect my diffused breath; protect my sight; protect my hearing; quicken my mind; swell my speech; protect my self; bestow light upon me.

(4.3.7.1.a) Mā-chandas, Prama-chandas, Pratima-chandas, Aśrīviś-chandas, Praṅkti-chandas, Uṣṇihā-chandas, Bṛhatī-chandas, Anuṣṭubh-chandas, Virāj-chandas, Gāyatrī-chandas, Triṣṭubh-chandas, Jagatī-chandas; Earth-chandas, Atmosphere-chandas, Sky-chandas, Years-chandas, Nakṣatras-chandas, Mind-chandas, Speech-chandas, Agriculture-chandas, Gold-chandas, Cow-chandas, Goat-chandas, Horse-chandas.

(4.3.7.1) Agni is the deity; (4.3.7.2) Vāta is the deity, Sūrya is the deity, Candramas is the deity, the Vasus are the deity, the Rudras are the deity, the Ādityas are the deity, the Viśve Devas are the deity, the Maruts are the deity, Bṛhaspati is the deity, Indra is the deity, Varuṇa is the deity. (4.3.7.2.b) You are the head, the sovereign; you are firm, the supporter; you are the restrainer, the controller. For food you, for strength you, for cultivation you, for security you. You are the restrainer, the sovereign; you are firm, the sustainer; you are the upholder, the bearer. For long life you, for splendor you, for vigor you, for power you.
(4.3.8.1) The Trivṛt is the swift;
(4.3.8.1) the Pañcadaśa is the radiant;
(4.3.8.1) the Saptadaśa is the void.
(4.3.8.1) *Pratūrti* consists of eighteen;
(4.3.8.1) *Tapas* consists of nineteen;
(4.3.8.1) *Abhivarta* consists of twenty.
The twenty-first is the Supporter;
the twenty-second is Splendor;
the twenty-third is the Gatherer.
The womb is the twenty-fourfold;
the embryos are the twenty-fivefold; vital force is the twenty-sevenfold.
The thirty-onefold is the creative power;
the thirty-threefold is the foundation;
the thirty-fourfold is the summit of the sun.
The *nāka* is the thirty-sixfold;
the *vivarta* is the forty-eightfold;
the *dhartra* is the four-stoma.
(4.3.9.1.a) You are the portion of Agni; the overlordship of Dīkṣā; the Brahman is protected; the Trivṛt Stoma.
(4.3.9.1.b) You are the portion of Indra; the overlordship of Viṣṇu; the Kṣatra is protected; the Pañcadaśa Stoma.
(4.3.9.1.c) You are the portion of the Nṛcakṣases; the overlordship of Dhātṛ; the progeny is protected; the Saptadaśa Stoma.

(4.3.9.1ḍ) You are the portion of Mitra; you are under the overlordship of Varuṇa. The rain of heaven and the winds have been won; the twenty-one-fold hymn-form (*stoma*) is [won]. (4.3.9.1.e) You are the portion of Aditi; you are under the overlordship of Pūṣan. Vital power (*ojas*) has been won; the twenty-seven-fold hymn-form is [won]. (4.3.9.1.f) You are the portion of the Vasus; you are under the overlordship of the Rudras. Quadrupeds have been won; the twenty-four-fold hymn-form is [won].

(4.3.9.2.g) You are the portion of the Ādityas; the overlordship of the Maruts; the embryos are protected; the twenty-fivefold hymn-form (*stoma*). (4.3.9.2.h) You are the portion of the god Savitṛ; the overlordship of Bṛhaspati; the convergent quarters are protected; the fourfold hymn-form (*stoma*). (4.3.9.2.i) You are the portion of the Yavas; the overlordship of the Ayavas; offspring are protected; the forty-fourfold hymn-form (*stoma*).
(4.3.9.2.k) You are the portion of the Ṛbhus; the overlordship of the Viśve Devas; the world that has come into being, the resting place, the protected; the thirty-threefold Stoma.
(4.3.10.1) They praised with one [verse]; creatures were produced; Prajāpati was the overlord.
(4.3.10.1) They praised with three; the Brahman was created; Brahmaṇaspati was the overlord. (4.3.10.1) They praised with five; beings were created; the Lord of Beings was the overlord.
They praised with seven; the Seven Seers were created; Dhātṛ was the overlord. They praised with nine; the Fathers were created; Aditi was the sovereign lady.
They praised with eleven; the Seasons were created; the Season was the overlord.
(4.3.10.1) They praised with thirteen; the months were created; the Year was the overlord.
(4.3.10.2) They praised with fifteen; the ruling power (*kṣatra*) was created; Indra was the overlord. (4.3.10.2) They praised with seventeen; the cattle were created; Bṛhaspati was the overlord.
They praised with nineteen; the Śūdra and the Ārya were created; Day and Night were the presiding lords.
They praised with twenty-one; one-hoofed animals were created; Varuṇa was the presiding lord. They praised with twenty-three; small animals were created; Pūṣan was the presiding lord.
(4.3.10.2) They praised with twenty-five; wild animals were created; Vāyu was the overlord.

(4.3.10.2) They praised with twenty-seven; heaven and earth went asunder; the Vasus, Rudras, and Ādityas followed after them; theirs was the overlordship. (4.3.10.3) They praised with twenty-nine; the lords of the forest were created; Soma was the overlord.
They praised with thirty-one; creatures were created, and they held sovereignty over both the Yāvas and the Ayāvas.
They praised with thirty-three; the beings became tranquil, and Prajāpati Parameṣṭhin was the sovereign lord.
(4.3.11.1.a) This is indeed she who first shone forth; having entered within her, she moves. The bride has given birth, the mother of nine sons; three majesties attend her.

(4.3.11.1.b) Adorned with meters, the two Dawns, shimmering brightly, moving together toward their common womb; having Sūrya as their husband, they move abroad, wise, creating a banner, ageless, and possessing abundant seed.
(4.3.11.1.c) Three have followed the path of *ṛta*; three heats have followed with light. One protects offspring, one protects vigor; (4.3.11.2) one protects the vow of those who seek the gods.

The fourth [part] of the sacrifice became the Catuṣṭoma; the seers become its two wings. Harnessing the Gāyatrī, Triṣṭubh, Jagatī, Anuṣṭubh, the Bṛhat, and the Arka, they brought this light of heaven hither.

With five [fingers], Dhātṛ has fashioned this world which he produced as five times five sisters; from them go forth by their impulse five [seasons], clothed in various forms and possessing distinct powers.
(4.3.11.2.f) Thirty sisters approach the appointed place, assuming a common banner. (4.3.11.3) The wise, knowing the seasons, extend them; the radiant ones move around the center of the meters.
The radiant goddess Night releases the garment of the sky; she observes the ordinances of the Sun. The variously formed creatures, being born, look out from within her, the Mother’s lap.
(4.3.11.3) The Ekāṣṭakā, performing penance, gave birth to a child, the greatness Indra; with him the gods overcame the Dasyus, and he became the slayer of the Asuras through his powers.

(4.3.11.3.i) "They say the truth when they say, 'They have made me, who was not a younger sister, a younger sister; seek after this. May I be so. (4.3.11.4) "As you are in his favor, let no other of you surpass me."

The All-Knowing One has come into my good thought; he has reached a firm foundation and found a footing. May I be in his good thought just as you are; do not cast me away from one of your others to another.
Five dawns follow five milkings; the seasons follow the cow of five names. The five directions are fashioned by the fifteenfold [stoma], all sharing one summit toward a single world.
The first dawns as the embryo of Cosmic Order; one bears the majesty of the waters. One moves among the appointed places of the sun; one belongs to the heat, and Savitṛ impels the other.
She who first shone forth became the milch-cow of Yama; as such, rich in milk, may she yield for us in each succeeding year.

Bright and bull-like, with the light of heaven, she has come; multiform and dappled, she has fire as her banner. Performing a common task with skillful workmanship, bearing age yet yourself undecaying, O Dawn, you have arrived.

(4.3.11.5.p) This first one has arrived as the mistress of the seasons, the leader of days, the mother of creatures. Being one, you shine forth in many ways at dawn; undecaying yourself, you cause everything else to decay.
O Agni, drive away our born enemies; O Jātavedas, repel those yet unborn. Shine for us with a gracious mind, without anger; may I abide in your triple-layered, protective shelter.
(4.3.12.1.b) Drive away our rivals who have already been born; O Jātavedas, drive back those yet unborn! Speak for us with a well-disposed mind; may we be victorious—drive away our rivals!
(4.3.12.1.c) The forty-fourfold hymn-form is splendor, the wealth. (4.3.12.1ḍ) The sixteenfold hymn-form is vigor, the wealth.
(4.3.12.1.e) You are the soil of the earth. (4.3.12.2) Your name is *apsas*.

The *eva* metre, the *varivas* metre, the *śambhū* metre, the *paribhū* metre, the *āc* metre, the *manas* metre, the *vyacas* metre, the *sindhu* metre, the *samudra* metre, the *salila* metre, the *saṃyas* metre, the *viyas* metre, the *bṛhat* metre, the *rathantara* metre, the *nikāya* metre, the *vivadha* metre, the *giras* metre, the *bhrajas* metre, the *ṣaṣṭubh* metre, the *anuṣṭubh* metre, the *kakubh* metre, the *trikakubh* metre, and the *kāvya* metre.

The *chandaḥ* is *aṅkuṣa*, the *chandaḥ* is *padapaṅkti*, the *chandaḥ* is *akṣarapaṅkti*, the *chandaḥ* is *viṣṭārapaṅkti*, the *chandaḥ* is *kṣuro bhṛjvān*, the *chandaḥ* is *prachat*, the *chandaḥ* is *pakṣa*, the *chandaḥ* is *evaḥ*, the *chandaḥ* is *varivaḥ*, the *chandaḥ* is *vayaḥ*, the *chandaḥ* is *vayaskṛt*, the *chandaḥ* is *viśālam*, the *chandaḥ* is *viṣpardhāḥ*, the *chandaḥ* is *chandiraḥ*, the *chandaḥ* is *dūrohaṇam*, the *chandaḥ* is *tandram*, the *chandaḥ* is *aṅkāṅkam*.
May Agni, kindled, bright, and invoked with oblations, slay the Vṛtras through our inspired praise, seeking wealth.
(4.3.13.1.b) O Soma, you are the lord of the virtuous; you are the king and the slayer of Vṛtra; you are the auspicious power of will.

(4.3.13.1.c) Auspicious is your appearance, O Agni of beautiful countenance; lovely is the sight of you, though you are formidable and manifold. For your brilliance they do not obstruct with darkness, nor do the defilers bring blemish upon your body.

(4.3.13.1ḍ) O Agni, possessor of power, auspicious is your countenance; it shines forth near the sun. (4.3.13.2) Brilliant to behold, it is seen even by night; unblemished in its form, food is visible within its appearance.

With a victorious army, most gracious to us, a sacrificer of the gods, most skilled in sacrifice, for our well-being—O Agni, an undeceived guardian and our protector from afar, shine forth with splendor and wealth!
(4.3.13.2.f) O Agni, bestow upon us well-being from heaven and earth for the sake of sacrifice, O God; grant us that wondrous wealth, O Son of Heaven, which is praised as excellent.

(4.3.13.2.g) Just as you, O Hotṛ of Manu, perform the sacrifice with offerings among the host of gods, O Son of Strength; even so, O Agni, desiring [them], sacrifice today to the desiring gods, bringing us together with those who are like-minded.
I praise Agni, the domestic priest, the god, the officiating priest of the sacrifice, the invoker, the bestower of most abundant treasures.
(4.3.13.3.i) O Soma, you are a bull, resplendent; O God, you are a bull whose ordinances are those of a bull. As a bull, you uphold the sacred laws.
O Sāṃtapanas, O Maruts, may you graciously accept this oblation; [we call] upon your assistance, O destroyers of enemies.

O Vasus, O Maruts, whatever mortal of evil intent should seek to slay us while we are engaged in our sacred truths—may he be caught in the snare of his own malice; strike him down with your most scorching heat!

The Maruts, who abide for a year, who possess beautiful songs, whose dwellings are wide, and who move in troops among men—may they release us from the snares of distress; they are the purifying ones, exhilarating and intoxicating.

Satisfy the longing gods, O youngest one; knowing the seasons, O Lord of Seasons, sacrifice here. With those who are the divine officiants, O Agni, you are the most excellent sacrificer among all invokers.

(4.3.13.4.o) O Agni, O Purifier, Hotṛ of the people’s sacrifice, today you have shone forth; for you, O Radiant One, are the sacrificer. Sacrifice according to the Truth, since you have spread yourself out with greatness; O Most Youthful One, carry those oblations which are yours today.
Through Agni, may one obtain wealth and nourishment day by day—wealth that is glorious and most rich in heroic sons.
O Soma, be a good friend to us—you who increase the dwelling, drive away disease, find wealth, and augment prosperity.
(4.3.13.5ṛ) O Maruts, you who dwell in the household, come hither; do not stay away from us, releasing us from distress.
For through many autumns we have offered oblations, O Maruts, with the greatness of the peoples.
(4.3.13.6ṭ) Your deep-seated splendors arise; O you who are worthy of sacrifice, extend your names. O Maruts, take pleasure in this thousandfold domestic portion, this offering of the householder.
To him, the very skillful one, the young woman approaches with the oblation at evening and at dawn—the ladle dripping with ghee; to him, Aramati, seeking wealth, approaches of her own accord.

(4.3.13.6.v) O Agni, bear these most desirable oblations to the assembly of the gods; may they accept our fragrant offerings. (4.3.13.6.w) Sing forth, O Kaṇvas, to the sportive host of the Maruts, the unassailable, who shine upon their chariots!
