Like coursers, the Maruts are swift-moving; like youths visible at a sacrifice, they have adorned themselves. Established in their mansions, they are brilliant like children; like playful calves, they are sucklers of milk.

At their racings, the earth trembles as if unsteady during their journeys when they harness themselves for glory. They, the playful, the roaring, with glittering spears—the shakers—themselves proclaim their own greatness.
When you have gathered on your secret haunts like birds on their flight, O Maruts, by what path? The vessels drip upon your chariots; pour out the ghee, honey-colored, for the singer.
With invocations, they ever call upon Agni, Agni, the lord of the people, the bearer of oblations, the one dear to many.
For him indeed all people constantly praise with the ladle dripping with ghee—the god Agni, so that he may carry the oblations.
(4.3.13.8.cc) O Indra and Agni, [you who are] the luminous realms of heaven;
(4.3.13.8ḍd) you struck Vṛtra down;
(4.3.13.8.ee) Indra for you from every side.
(4.3.13.8.ff) Indra, [the] men;
(4.3.13.8.gg) O Viśvakarman, increasing by means of the oblation;
(4.3.13.8ḥh) O Viśvakarman, through the strengthening of the oblation.

(4.4.1.1.a) You are the ray; for habitation, you; quicken habitation. You are the departure; for dharma, you; quicken dharma. You are the following-attainment; for heaven, you; quicken heaven. You are the junction; for the intermediate space, you; quicken the intermediate space. You are the support; for the earth, you; quicken the earth. You are the pillar; for rain, you; quicken rain. You are the precursor; for the day, you; quicken the day.

(4.4.1.1.b) You are the after-blowing; for the night, you; quicken the night! You are the eager one (uśij); (4.4.1.2) for the Vasus, you; quicken the Vasus! You are the thread; for progeny, you; quicken progeny! You are the conqueror of armies; for cattle, you; quicken cattle!

(4.4.1.2.c) Rich art thou; for the plants, thee! Quicken the plants! Thou art the conqueror; for the yoked chariot, thee! Quicken Indra! Thou art the overlord; for the out-breath, thee! (4.4.1.3) Quicken the out-breath! Thou art the restrainer; for the in-breath, thee! Quicken the in-breath! Thou art the glider; for the eye, thee! Quicken the eye! Thou art the bestower of vigor; for the ear, thee! Quicken the ear! Thou art the threefold;

(4.4.1.3ḍ) thou art the forward-turning; thou art the backward-turning; thou art the all-encompassing; thou art the upward-turning; thou art the downward-turning; thou art the forward-growing; thou art the downward-growing; thou art the upward-growing; thou art the following-growing.
(4.4.1.3.e) You are Vasuku; you are Veṣaśrī; you are Vasyaṣṭi.

(4.4.2.1.a) You are the Queen, the eastern quarter; the Vasus are your gods as overlords; Agni is the warder-off of missiles. May the threefold hymn-form take its place for you upon the earth; may the *ājya* litany, unshakable, support you; may the *rathantara* chant provide stability.

(4.4.2.1.b) You are the Virāj, the southern quarter; the Rudras are your gods as overlords; Indra is the warder-off of missiles. May the fifteenfold hymn-form take its place for you upon the earth; may the *prauga* litany, unshakable, support you; may the *bṛhat* chant provide stability.

(4.4.2.1.c) You are the sovereign; you are the eastern quarter. The Ādityas are your overlords; Soma is the warder-off of missiles. May the seventeenfold hymn-form (stoma) support you upon the earth; may the Marutvatīya hymn (uktha) prop you without wavering for the sake of stability; may the Vairūpa chant establish you. (4.4.2.2ḍ) You are the self-ruling one; you are the northern quarter. The Viśvedevas are your overlords; Varuṇa is the warder-off of missiles. May the twenty-onefold hymn-form (stoma) support you upon the earth; may the Niṣkevalya hymn (uktha) prop you without wavering for the sake of stability; may the Vairāja chant establish you.

(4.4.2.2.e) You are the sovereign, the lofty quarter; the Maruts are your divine overlords. (4.4.2.3) Bṛhaspati is the warder-off of missiles. May the Triṇava and Trayastriṁśa Stomas support you on earth. May the Vaiśvadeva and Āgnimāruta Ukthas, being unshakable, sustain you. May the Śākvara and Raivata Sāmans provide stability for your firm foundation.

(4.4.2.3.f) For the intermediate space! May the Ṛṣis, first-born among the gods, extend you with the measure and breadth of heaven. May this Vidhartṛ and the Adhipati—may they all, being in full accord, establish you and the sacrificer upon the back of the firmament, in the world of heaven.

(4.4.3.1.a) This one in front is Harikeśa, whose rays are the sun; his *grāmaṇīs* are Rathagṛtsa and Rathaujas, and his *apsarases* are Puñjikasthalā and Kṛtasthalā; the *yātudhānas* are his weapon (*heti*), and the *rakṣases* are his missile (*praheti*). (4.4.3.1.b) This one on the right is Viśvakarman; his *grāmaṇīs* are Rathasvana and Rathecitra, and his *apsarases* are Menakā and Sahajanyā; biting animals are his weapon, and man-made slaughter is his missile.

(4.4.3.1.c) This one from the west is Viśvavyacas; his two *grāmaṇīs* of the army are Ratheprota and Asamaratha, and his two *apsarases* are Pramlocantī and Anumlocantī; the serpents are his weapon (*heti*), and the tigers are his missile (*praheti*). (4.4.3.2ḍ) This one from the north is Saṃyadvasu; his two *grāmaṇīs* of the army are Senajit and Suṣeṇa, and his two *apsarases* are Viśvācī and Ghṛtācī; the waters are his weapon, and the wind is his missile.

(4.4.3.2.e) This one above is Arvāgvasu; his *grāmaṇīs* are Tārkṣya and Ariṣṭanemi, and his *apsarases* are Urvaśī and Pūrvacitti; his missile is lightning, and his weapon is the thunderclap. (4.4.3.2.f) Homage to them! May they be gracious to us. Whomsoever we hate, and whoever hates us—him I place within your jaws.
(4.4.3.3.g) I set you down in the seat of Āyu, in the shade of the well; homage to the ocean, homage to the eye of the ocean.

(4.4.3.3) May Parameṣṭhin settle you upon the back of heaven—expansive, wide, all-pervading, abundant, and encompassing. Support the sky; make the sky firm; do not harm the sky! For the sake of universal out-breathing, in-breathing, diffused breathing, and up-breathing; for stability and movement. May Sūrya protect you with great well-being, with a most peaceful shelter. By that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras.
(4.4.3.3.i) Like a neighing horse eager for pasture, when you have emerged from the great enclosure, then the wind blows along your flame; and so, your path becomes black.
Agni is the head of heaven, the summit, the lord of this earth; he quickens the seeds of the waters.
(4.4.4.1.b) From the lotus, O Agni, Atharvan churned you forth from the head of the entire universe, he the invoker.
(4.4.4.1.c) This Agni is the lord of thousandfold and hundredfold booty; he is the sage, the head of riches.

(4.4.4.1ḍ) You are the leader of the sacrifice and of the world; where you accompany [the gods] with your auspicious teams of horses, you place your head in heaven, O showerer of light, and you have made your tongue, O Agni, the bearer of the oblation.
Agni has been awakened by the fuel of the people, facing the Dawn as she approaches like a milch-cow. Like young birds rising up toward a branch, his rays stream forth toward the firmament.

(4.4.4.2.f) We have spoken a reverent word to the sage worthy of sacrifice, to the bull, the potent one. Gaviṣṭhira, with homage, has fixed his far-reaching hymn upon Agni, like a golden ornament in the sky.

(4.4.4.2.g) The guardian of the people, the watchful Agni, the very skillful, has been born for new-found prosperity. With his face anointed with ghee, he shines brilliantly and purely for the Bharatas, reaching up to the great heaven.
(4.4.4.2–3) O Agni, the Aṅgirases discovered you, who were hidden in secret, dwelling in every forest. You are born when being churned with great power; they call you, O Aṅgiras, the son of strength.

Men kindle Agni, the banner of the sacrifice, the first to be established, in his threefold seat. Riding in the same chariot with Indra and the gods, he sits upon the sacrificial grass as the Hotṛ priest of excellent wisdom for the performance of the sacrifice.
(4.4.4.3.k) O Agni, most rich in glorious fame, the people among the tribes invoke you—the one with flaming hair—most dear to many, so that you may carry their oblations.
(4.4.4.3ḷ) O friends, [bring] together for you a unified nourishment and a hymn of praise for Agni, the highest of the peoples, the son of strength, the powerful one.
(4.4.4.4ṃ) O bull-like Agni, you gather together all the riches of the enemy; kindled at the place of libation, bring us treasures.
With this [hymn], I invoke for you Agni, the Son of Strength, with reverence—the beloved, most wise steward of the sacrifice, the immortal messenger of all.

He, the ruddy one, is yoked by the all-nourishing [sacrifice]; let him, well-invoked, hasten hither. The sacrifice is accompanied by excellent prayers and well-performed rites; it is the divine gift of the Vasus for the people.
(4.4.4.5.p) The flame of this bounteous one has risen as he is being invoked; his ruddy smoke-clouds, touching the heavens, rise upward; the men kindle Agni.
O Agni, lord of wealth consisting of cattle, O son of strength, bestow upon us great renown, O Jātavedas!
Being kindled, the wise Agni, worthy of praise with our song, O you of many faces, shine forth wealth upon us.
O King Agni, by yourself, through the night and likewise at the break of dawn, you who possess sharp fangs, burn against the *rakṣas*!
(4.4.4.6ṭ) O Agni, we kindle you—the radiant, unaging god—so that this most wondrous fuel of yours may shine upon heaven; bring nourishment to those who praise you.

(4.4.4.6.u) To you, O Agni, with a *ṛc* verse, an oblation is offered at the heat of the bright light—O radiant one, wonder-worker, lord of the people, carrier of the oblations! It is offered unto you; bring nourishment to those who praise you!
O resplendent one, you mix both ladles of clarified butter in your mouth; therefore, fill us full as well. O Lord of Might, bring nourishment to the singers amidst our hymns of praise.
O Agni, may we today succeed for you with our hymns—as one would with a horse—with a thought that is auspicious and touches the heart, through our offerings.
(4.4.4.7.x) For indeed, O Agni, you have become the charioteer of auspicious will, of effective skill, and of the lofty cosmic order.
(4.4.4.7.y) Praising you today with these songs, O Agni, let us worship you; your vital powers thunder forth like those of heaven.
(4.4.4.7.z) Through these our hymns, O Agni, turn toward us; like the light of heaven, be well-disposed toward us with all your countenances.
I meditate upon Agni as the Hotṛ priest, the bountiful giver, the well-born son of strength, Jātavedas—the wise one, like Jātavedas himself.

(4.4.4.8.bb) The god whose sacrifice is well-performed, who with his upward-turned form faces the gods, follows the radiant glow of clarified butter—the bright-shining ghee being poured as an oblation.
O Agni, be our closest kinsman; be our protector, auspicious and providing a secure refuge.
We now entreat you for the welfare of our friends, O most radiant one, O shining one.
Agni is the Vasu, of good renown; come hither, most resplendent one, and grant us wealth.

(4.4.5.1.a) With Indra and Agni as my companion, I yoke you with a bond; with the two libations, with brilliance, with luster, with hymns, with praises, and with meters, for the increase of wealth and for preeminence among my kinsmen—with me as your companion, I yoke you with a bond.
(4.4.5.1.b) Ambā, Dulā, Nitatni, Abhrayantī, Meghayantī, Varṣayantī, Cupuṇīkā—such is your name. With Prajāpati and with all sacred thoughts, I place you down.
(4.4.5.1.c) The earth is a city with water, pervaded by food; men are its guardians, and Agni is stationed within it. To it I resort; may it be my refuge and my protection.

(4.4.5.2ḍ) The atmosphere is above the sky, pervaded by the sacred word (*brahman*); the Maruts are its guardians, and Vāyu is stationed within it. To it I resort; may it be my refuge and my protection.
(4.4.5.2.e) The sky is unconquered, pervaded by cosmic order (*ṛta*); the Ādityas are its guardians, and Sūrya is stationed within it. To it I resort; may it be my refuge and my protection.

(4.4.6.1.a) May Bṛhaspati settle you upon the back of the earth, full of light, for the sake of every out-breath and in-breath; bestow universal light! Agni is your overlord. (4.4.6.1.b) May Viśvakarman settle you upon the back of the intermediate space, full of light, for the sake of every out-breath and in-breath; bestow universal light! Vāyu is your overlord.
(4.4.6.1.c) May Prajāpati settle you upon the back of the sky, full of light, for the sake of every out-breath and in-breath; bestow universal light! Parameṣṭhin is your overlord.
(4.4.6.1ḍ) You are the winner of the east wind; you are the winner of the clouds; you are the winner of lightning. (4.4.6.2) You are the winner of thunder; you are the winner of rain.
(4.4.6.2.e) You are the *yānya* of Agni among the gods; you are the *yānya* of Agni.
(4.4.6.2.f) You are the *yānya* of Vāyu among the gods; you are the *yānya* of Vāyu.

(4.4.6.2.g) You are those belonging to the intermediate space; you are those belonging to the intermediate space of the gods. (4.4.6.2.h) You are the intermediate space; for the intermediate space, you!
(4.4.6.2.i) For the flood, you! For the *sarṇīka*, you! For the *satīka*, you! For the signal, you! For the wise one, you! For Vivasvat, you! For the light of heaven, you! For the Ādityas, you!

(4.4.6.2.k) For the *ṛc*, for radiance, for splendor, for brilliance, for light—(4.4.6.2ḷ) thee, the giver of glory, I settle in glory; thee, the giver of luster, in luster; thee, the giver of milk, in milk; thee, the giver of splendor, in splendor; thee, the giver of wealth, in wealth. With that seer, with that sacred formulation (*brahman*), with that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras.

(4.4.7.1.a) You are the maker of abundance; you are the maker of wide space; you are the eastern one; you are the upward one; you are the dweller in the intermediate region; sit in the intermediate region! (4.4.7.1.b) You are the dweller in the waters; you are the dweller in the hawk; you are the dweller in the vulture; you are the dweller in the eagle; you are the dweller in the firmament.

(4.4.7.1.c) I settle you in the wealth of the earth; I settle you in the wealth of the intermediate region; I settle you in the wealth of heaven; I settle you in the wealth of the quarters; I settle you, the giver of wealth, in wealth.
(4.4.7.1ḍ) Guard my out-breath; guard my in-breath; guard my diffused breath. (4.4.7.2) Guard my life; guard my all-encompassing life; guard my complete life.
(4.4.7.2.e) O Agni, that which is your supreme heart-name—come with that! Let us two clasp hands; be present among the five peoples, O Agni.
(4.4.7.2.f) Yāvan, Ayāvan, Evā, Ūma, Sabda, Sagara, Sumeka.
Through Agni he is the conqueror of all; through Sūrya he is the self-ruler; through Kratu he is the lord of power.
Through the bull, Tvaṣṭṛ [attained it];
through sacrifice, Maghavan; through the sacrificial fee, the heavenly world.
Through fury he is the slayer of Vṛtra; through benevolence he is the bestower of bodies;
through food he is the householder.
(4.4.8.1) He sat upon the earth;
(4.4.8.1) through the *ṛc*s, he became an eater of food;
(4.4.8.1) through the *vaṣaṭ*-call, he attained prosperity.
By means of the *sāman*, he is a protector of the body; by means of the *virāj*, he is possessed of light;
by means of the *brahman*, he is a drinker of soma.

With the cows he sustained the sacrifice; with his sovereign power, he sustained mankind; and with the horse and the chariot, the wielder of the thunderbolt, the Lord, [sustained all] through the seasons.
Encompassing with the year,
unassailable through austerity, being the sun by means of [his] bodies.
Prajāpati [presides] by means of the mind; Andha Acheta [presides] during the initiation; Dhātṛ [presides] during the consecration.
Savitṛ [is the deity] in the *bhṛtī* (the vessel for carrying the Soma);
Pūṣan [is the deity] in the *somakrayaṇī* (the cow used for purchasing the Soma);
Varuṇa [is the deity] when it is bound with a rope.
The Asura while being purchased; Mitra once purchased;
Śipiviṣṭa once seated.
When being carried forward, he is the one who dwells among men;
when arrived, he is the sovereign lord;
when being led forth, he is Prajāpati.
Agni [is present] in the Āgnīdhra shed; Bṛhaspati when being led forth from the Āgnīdhra; Indra in the Havirdhāna sheds.
Aditi is seated;
Viṣṇu is being brought down;
Atharvan has stepped near.
Yama is when it has been pressed;
Apūtapā is when it is being shaken;
Vāyu is when it is being purified.
(4.4.9.1) Mitra is the one whose glory is milk; (4.4.9.1) Manthin is the one whose glory is barley meal;
(4.4.9.1) the one drawn up for the Viśvedevas is the Unnīta.
Rudra has been invoked;
Vāyu has turned back;
Nṛcakṣas has looked upon us.
(4.4.9.1) The portion has arrived;
(4.4.9.1) it is for the ancestors, the *nārāśaṃsa*;
(4.4.9.1) it is taken by the Asuras.
The Sindhu has gone down to the purificatory bath;
the ocean has entered [it], the watery expanse has overflowed.
(4.4.9.1) He has gone to the zenith of heaven.

(4.4.10.1.a) The Kṛttikās are the lunar mansion; Agni is the deity. You are the splendor of Agni, the bestowal of Prajāpati, the Dhātṛ, and Soma. For the sake of the Ṛc, for splendor, for radiance, for light, and for luminosity, I take you.

(4.4.10.1.b) The constellation Rohiṇī has Prajāpati as its deity; the constellation Mṛgaśīrṣa has Soma as its deity; the constellation Ārdrā has Rudra as its deity; the constellation Punarvasū has Aditi as its deity; the constellation Tiṣya has Bṛhaspati as its deity; the constellation Āśleṣā has the Sarpas as its deity; the constellation Maghā has the Pitṛs as its deity; the constellation Phalgunī has Aryaman as its deity; the constellation [second] Phalgunī has Bhaga as its deity; the constellation Hasta has Savitṛ as its deity; the constellation Citrā...

The constellation Svātī has Indra as its deity; the constellation Viśākhā has Vāyu as its deity; the constellation Anūrādhā has Indra and Agni as its deity; the constellation Rohiṇī has Mitra as its deity; the constellation Vicṛtī has Indra as its deity; the constellation Āṣāḍhā has the Fathers as its deity; the constellation Āṣāḍhā has the Waters as its deity; the constellation Śroṇā has the Viśve Devas as its deity; the constellation Śraviṣṭhā has Viṣṇu as its deity; the constellation Śatabhiṣaj has the Vasus as its deity; the constellation [Śatabhiṣaj] has Indra as its deity.

The Proṣṭhapadas are the lunar mansion; Aja Ekapād is its deity. The Proṣṭhapadas are the lunar mansion; Ahir Budhnya is its deity. Revatī is the lunar mansion; Pūṣan is its deity. The two Aśvayujas are the lunar mansion; the Aśvins are its deity. The Apabharaṇīs are the lunar mansion; Yama is its deity—[that fullness which the gods placed for you behind].
Madhu and Mādhava are the two spring seasons;
Śukra and Śuci are the two summer seasons;
Nabhas and Nabhasya are the two rainy seasons.
Iṣa and Ūrja are the two autumnal seasons;
Sahas and Sahasya are the two winter seasons;
Tapa and Tapasya are the two dewy seasons.

(4.4.11.1.g) You are the internal bond of Agni. May Heaven and Earth be in harmony; may the waters and plants be in harmony; may the fires, being of one accord, be in harmony for my preeminence. (4.4.11.2) Those fires which are of one mind between heaven and earth, conforming to the two winter seasons, may they enter together as the gods enter Indra.
(4.4.11.2.i) *Samyak* and *Pracetās*, belonging to Agni, Soma, and Sūrya;
*Ugrā* and *Bhīmā*, belonging to the Pitṛs, Yama, and Indra.
(4.4.11.2.k) Dhruvā and Pṛthivī belong to the god Savitṛ and the Maruts, and to Varuṇa;
(4.4.11.2ḷ) Dhartrī and Dharitrī belong to Mitra and Varuṇa, and to Mitra the Ordainer; (4.4.11.2ṃ) Prācī and Prātīcī belong to the Vasus, the Rudras, and the Ādityas.
(4.4.11.3ṇ) They are your overlords; homage to them! May they be gracious to us. Him whom we hate and him who hates us, I place within your jaws.

(4.4.11.3.o) You are the measure of a thousand; you are the counterpart of a thousand; you are the span of a thousand; you are the height of a thousand; you are a thousandfold; for a thousand, I take you.

(4.4.11.3.p) O Agni, may these bricks of mine be milch-cows: one, and a hundred, and a thousand, and ten thousand; (4.4.11.4) a hundred thousand, a million, ten million, a hundred million, a billion, ten billion, a trillion, and a quadrillion. O Agni, may these bricks of mine be milch-cows—sixty, a thousand, ten thousand, inexhaustible, established in *ṛta*, increasing *ṛta*, dripping with ghee, dripping with honey, full of vigor, and possessing the power of *svadhā*. O Agni, may these bricks of mine be milch-cows named Virāj, yielding all desires in yonder world.

(4.4.12.1.a) The kindling-stick of the quarters, looking toward us, winning the light—heavenly Madhava shall protect us from this honeyed [season]. May the god Agni, invincible and difficult to overcome, guard this sovereignty and protect us.

May the Rathantara protect us with the Sāmans; may the Gāyatrī, the multiform among meters, protect us; may the Trivṛt Stoma with its structural arrangement, and the ocean and wind with the days, fulfill this power for us.

(4.4.12.1.c) The fierce one, the overcomer of the quarters, the bestower of vitality, pure on the bright day, full of power—may Indra, the sovereign lord, protect us from this with great [strength]. (4.4.12.2) May he maintain this dominion on every side.

The Bṛhat Sāman is the bearer of dominion, possessing increased virility; the Triṣṭubh is vigor, adorned with fierce heroes. O Indra, protect this center with the fifteenfold Stoma, together with Vāta and the ocean.

(4.4.12.2.e) The eastern direction among the directions is glorious and full of splendor; the All-Gods [rule] over the rainy season among the days, possessing the light of heaven. May this sovereign power be invincible, may it be unassailable force, thousandfold and victorious.

(4.4.12.2.f) In the Vairūpa Sāman, may we be able to do this here; with the Jagatī metre, we cause him to enter among the people. With the seventeenfold [Stoma], O All-Gods! (4.4.12.3) This is splendor, this is sovereignty, powerful, accompanied by the waters.

(4.4.12.3.g) The upholder of the quarters has established this sovereignty; may the strength of the regions be friendly. O Mitra and Varuṇa, you who are observant through the autumns and days, grant great protection to this kingdom!

Upon the Vairāja Sāman rests my inspired thought; through the Anuṣṭubh, heroic power and force have been gathered. This sovereignty, accompanied by friends and yielding gentle rain—O Mitra and Varuṇa, protect it with your lordships!

The sovereign of the quarters, powerful with might, may the winter season fulfill our desire through its fixed order. May the winds, seeking aid, and the great Śakvarī verses, dripping with ghee, protect this sacrifice of ours.

(4.4.12.4.k) May the divine goddess of the quarters, rich in light, easy to milk, full of milk, and dripping with clarity, protect us. O Bṛhaspati, you are our guardian both from the front and from behind; harness the voice for the southern direction.
May the upward direction be the delight of the quarters; may the year, Savitṛ of the days, and the Ṛc, the Sāman, the Atichandas, and the Chandojātaśatru—rich and pleasant—be gracious to us.

(4.4.12.4) O mistress of the world, in the thirty-three-fold hymn, O Vivasvat, O Vāta, favor us! (4.4.12.5) O Savitṛ, with your lordly powers, may there be for us a refreshing delight, full of clarity and rich in milk.

The fixed quarter of the directions, the wife of Viṣṇu, who is non-terrible, sovereign, and the mental inspirer of strength; may Bṛhaspati, Mātariśvan, and Vāyu, together with the purifying winds, sing our praises.
The support of heaven, the foundation of earth, mistress of this moving world, the consort of Viṣṇu, all-pervading, bestowing nourishment, auspicious and well-being—may Aditi be gracious in her lap.
May Vaiśvānara come to our aid;
he who is touched in heaven.
May Anumati favor us today.
(4.4.12.5ṣ) Follow indeed, O Anumati! (4.4.12.5ṭ) With what [favor] shall the wonderful one come to us?
(4.4.12.5.u) Who yokes [the horses] today?
Homage to your wrath, O Rudra, and homage to your arrow; let there be homage to your bow, and homage also to your two arms.
(4.5.1.1.b) That arrow of yours which is most auspicious, that bow of yours which has become auspicious, and that quiver of yours which is auspicious—with that, O Rudra, be gracious to us.
(4.5.1.1.c) O Rudra, that auspicious form of yours which is not terrible and does not appear evil—with that most peaceful form, O Lord of the Mountain, look upon us with favor.
O Lord of the Mountain, that arrow which you carry in your hand to discharge—O Protector of the Mountain, make it auspicious; do not harm the person or the living world.
(4.5.1.2.e) With auspicious speech we address you, O Mountain-Dweller, so that our entire world may be free from disease and well-disposed toward us.
The supreme advocate has spoken, the first divine physician; he crushes all serpents and all sorcerers.

(4.5.1.2.g) That one who is copper-colored, ruddy, and even brownish, the most auspicious; and those Rudras who are stationed here around the quarters by the thousands—of them all, we pray for the removal of their wrath.
(4.5.1.3) He who glides along, blue-necked and deep red—him the cowherds have seen, him the water-carriers have seen; him all beings have seen. Having been seen, may he be gracious to us.
Homage be to the blue-necked one, the thousand-eyed, the bountiful; and also to those who are his attendants—to them I have paid homage.
(4.5.1.3.k) Unstring the bowstring from both ends of your bow; and those arrows that are in your hand—O Blessed One, cast them away. (4.5.1.4)
(4.5.1.4ḷ) Having unstrung your bow, O thousand-eyed one, you who possess a hundred quivers; having blunted the points of your arrows, become auspicious and well-disposed toward us.
(4.5.1.4ṃ) The bow of the one with matted hair is strungless; his arrow-case is without arrows. His arrows have perished, and his quiver is empty.
O most bountiful one, that missile which is in your hand and that bow which you possess—with that, protect us on every side from all harm.
Homage be to your weapon, the unstrung one, the bold; homage also to both your arms, and to your bow.
(4.5.1.4.p) May the missile from your bow avoid us on every side; and whatever quiver you have, O Arai, place that far away from us.
(4.5.2.1.a) Homage to Hiraṇyabāhu, the leader of the army, and to the Lord of the quarters!
(4.5.2.1.b) Homage to the golden-haired trees, and to the Lord of cattle!
(4.5.2.1.c) Homage to the tawny, radiant one, and to the Lord of the paths!
(4.5.2.1ḍ) Homage to Babhluśa, the piercer; homage to the Lord of foods.
(4.5.2.1.e) Homage to Harikeśa, the one wearing the sacred thread; homage to the Lord of prosperity.
(4.5.2.1.f) Homage to the weapon of Bhava; homage to the Lord of moving beings.

(4.5.2.1.g) Homage to Rudra, the archer; homage to the Lord of the Fields! (4.5.2.1.h) Homage to the charioteer, the unslayable; homage to the Lord of the Forests! (4.5.2.1.i) Homage to Rohita, the carpenter; homage to the Lord of the Trees!

(4.5.2.2.k) Homage to Mantrin, to Vāṇija, to the lord of the armpits; homage! (4.5.2.2ḷ) Homage to Bhuvantya, to Vārivaskṛta, to the lord of the plants; homage! (4.5.2.2ṃ) Homage to Uccairghoṣa, to Ākrandayat, to the lord of the foot soldiers; homage!
Homage to him who is completely enveloped, who rushes forward; homage to the lord of living beings!
(4.5.3.1.a) Homage to the Conqueror, the Piercer, the Lord of those who pierce; homage!
(4.5.3.1.b) Homage to the Exalted One, the Quiver-bearer, the Lord of thieves; homage!
(4.5.3.1.c) Homage to the Quiver-bearer, the Arrow-case-holder, the Lord of robbers; homage!

(4.5.3.1ḍ) Homage to the deceiver, to the one who deceives from all sides; homage to the lord of thieves! (4.5.3.1.e) Homage to the prowler, to the one who haunts the outskirts; homage to the lord of the forests! (4.5.3.1.f) Homage to the armed raiders who seek to kill; homage to the lord of robbers!

(4.5.3.1.g) Homage to those who carry swords, who roam by night; homage to the Lord of the Carvers. (4.5.3.1.h) Homage to the turbaned one who roams the mountains; homage to the Lord of the Thieves. (4.5.3.1.i) Homage to those who carry arrows and to you who carry bows; homage! (4.5.3.2) Homage! Homage! Homage! Homage! Homage! Homage! Homage! Homage! Homage! Homage! Homage! Homage! Homage! (4.5.3.2.k) Homage to you who are stretching [the bowstrings] and to you who are fixing [the arrows], homage! (4.5.3.2ḷ) Homage to you who are drawing [the bow] and to you who are releasing [the arrows], homage! (4.5.3.2ṃ) Homage to you who are aiming and to you who are piercing, homage!

(4.5.4.1.a) Homage to you, the piercing ones and those who pierce through; homage to you! (4.5.4.1.b) Homage to you, the fierce throngs and those who crush; homage to you!

(4.5.4.2ṛ) Homage to the dogs and to the masters of the dogs; homage to you!
(4.5.5.1.a) Homage to Bhava and to Rudra; (4.5.5.1.b) homage to Śarva and to Paśupati;
(4.5.5.1.c) homage to the blue-necked one and to the white-throated one.
(4.5.5.1ḍ) Homage to the one with matted hair and to the one with shorn hair;
(4.5.5.1.e) homage to the thousand-eyed one and to the one with a hundred bows;
(4.5.5.1.f) homage to the mountain-dweller and to the one pervaded by rays.
(4.5.5.1.g) Homage to the most bountiful and to the one possessing arrows; (4.5.5.1.h) homage to the short and to the dwarf;
(4.5.5.1.i) homage to the great and to the more extensive.
Homage to the aged and to the one who causes growth.
Homage to the foremost and to the first; homage to the swift and to the fleet; homage to the rapid and to the hasty.
(4.5.5.2.o) Homage to the one of the waves and to the one of the shallow waters; (4.5.5.2.p) homage to the one of the streams and to the one of the islands.
(4.5.6.1.a) Homage to the eldest and to the youngest; (4.5.6.1.b) homage to the first-born and to the last-born;
(4.5.6.1.c) homage to the middlemost and to the unassuming.
Homage to the one who is last and to the one who is first;
homage to the one who belongs to the *sobha* tree and to the one who is used for counter-spells;
homage to the one who belongs to Yama and to the one who brings security.
(4.5.6.1.g) Homage to the field and to the threshing floor;
(4.5.6.1.h) homage to the singer of the *śloka* and to the dweller in the settlement;
(4.5.6.1.i) homage to the forest and to the thicket.
Homage to Śrava and to Pratiśrava.
(4.5.6.2ḷ) Homage to the one with the swift army and to the one with the swift chariot;
(4.5.6.2ṃ) homage to the hero and to the piercer; (4.5.6.2ṇ) homage to the one clad in armor and to the one who provides protection.
Homage to the one with the helmet and to the one with the armor;
homage to the one renowned and to the one whose army is renowned.
(4.5.7.1.a) Homage to the drum and to the striker;
(4.5.7.1.b) homage to the bold and to the one who reaches out;
(4.5.7.1.c) homage to the messenger and to the one sent forth.

(4.5.7.1.g) Homage to the one of the stream and to the one of the path;
(4.5.7.1.h) homage to the one of the ditch and to the one of the canal;
(4.5.7.1.i) homage to the one of the well and to the one of the lake.
Homage to Nādyā and to Vaiśanta!

(4.5.7.2.q) homage to the one who dwells in the homestead and to the protector of the homestead.
(4.5.8.1.a) Homage to Soma and to Rudra;
(4.5.8.1.b) homage to the tawny one and to the ruddy one; (4.5.8.1.c) homage to Śaṅgu and to Paśupati.
Homage to the fierce and to the terrible; homage to the one who strikes nearby and to the one who strikes from afar;
homage to the slayer and to the more deadly slayer.
(4.5.8.1.g) Homage to the trees with golden hair!
(4.5.8.1.h) Homage to Tāra! (4.5.8.1.i) Homage to Śambhu and to Mayobhu!
Homage to the one who brings peace and the one who brings bliss;
homage to the auspicious one and the one who is even more auspicious.

(4.5.8.2.o) homage to the one who carries across and to the one who carries over.
Homage to Ātārya and to Cālāṭya; homage to Śaṣpya and to Phenya;

Homage to Lopya and to Colopya!

(4.5.10.1.a) O Drāpi, lord of the soma-juice, you who are poor and blue-and-red: do not terrify these men, do not harm these cattle; let nothing whatsoever afflict them.
(4.5.10.1.b) That auspicious form of yours, O Rudra, which is auspicious and provides healing every day—the auspicious healing power of Rudra—with that, be gracious to us so that we may live.

(4.5.10.1.c) We offer this prayer to Rudra, the powerful one with braided hair, the lord of heroes, so that it may bring well-being to our bipeds and quadrupeds, and so that everything in this village may be nourished and free from disease. (4.5.10.2) Free from sickness.

(4.5.10.2ḍ) Be gracious to us, O Rudra, and grant us joy; we shall worship you with homage, you whose heroes dwell [in safety]. Whatever health and prosperity our father Manu attained through sacrifice, may we obtain that under your guidance, O Rudra.

(4.5.10.2.e) Do not harm our great ones, nor our small ones; do not harm our growing ones, nor those already grown. Do not slay our father, nor our mother; do not injure our dear bodies, O Rudra! (4.5.10.3) Do not cause us pain!

Do not harm us in our children or grandchildren, nor in our life-span; do not harm us in our cattle or our horses. O Rudra, do not slay our heroes in your wrath. Bearing oblations, we worship you with reverence.
Far be your bolt from us, O slayer of cattle and slayer of men; may your favor be with us, O lord of heroes. Protect us, O god, speak for us, and grant us shelter, you who are doubly mighty.

(4.5.10.3) Praise the famous one, who sits upon the chariot-seat, the youthful, fierce, and deadly hunter like a terrifying beast! O Rudra, being praised, be gracious to the singer; let your armies strike down someone other than us. (4.5.10.4) Praise the famous one, who sits upon the chariot-seat, the youthful, fierce, and deadly hunter like a terrifying beast! O Rudra, being praised, be gracious to the singer; let your armies strike down someone other than us.

May the missile of Rudra pass us by; may the ill-will of the impetuous, malevolent one avoid us. O bounteous one, relax your firm [bow] for the sake of our patrons; O dispenser of boons, be gracious to our children and descendants.

(4.5.10.4.k) O most bountiful one, most auspicious one, be gracious and well-disposed toward us! Having laid aside your weapon upon the highest tree, come hither wearing a skin and bearing your *pināka* bow. (4.5.10.5) Come, bearing [the bow].
(4.5.10.5ḷ) O scatterer, O bloodless one, homage be to you, O Blessed One! May those thousand missiles of yours strike down someone other than us.
(4.5.10.5ṃ) Thousands upon thousands are the missiles in your two arms; O Blessed One, as their master, turn their points away from us.
(4.5.11.1.a) Those thousands upon thousands of Rudras who are upon the earth—for them, we unstring our bows at a distance of a thousand leagues.
(4.5.11.1.b) You who dwell upon this great ocean, in the intermediate space;
(4.5.11.1.c) the blue-necked, white-throated Śarvas who roam below upon the earth.
The blue-necked, white-throated Rudras have taken refuge in heaven;
those who are tawny among the trees, blue-necked and crimson;
those who are lords of beings, hairless and wearing matted locks.
(4.5.11.1.g) Those who pierce through the foods while people are drinking from their vessels;
(4.5.11.1.h) those who are guardians of the paths, the increasers of the field, the strikers with the javelin;
(4.5.11.1.i) those who frequent the fords, armed with spears and carrying quivers.
(4.5.11.2.k) As many as these and even more Rudras who have spread throughout the quarters—to a distance of a thousand yojanas, we unstring their bows.

Homage to the Rudras who are on earth, who are in the intermediate space, and who are in heaven; whose food is wind, rain, and arrows—to them, ten [fingers] toward the east, ten toward the south, ten toward the west, ten toward the north, and ten upward: homage to them! May they be gracious to us. Whomsoever we hate, and whosoever hates us—him I place within your jaws.

(4.6.1.1.a) O Maruts, bestowing it upon us, grant us that food and strength which has been gathered from the stone, from the mountain, from the wind, from Parjanya, from the force of Varuṇa, and from the waters, the plants, and the trees.
(4.6.1.1.b) Let hunger seize thy stone; let thy heat reach him whom we hate. (4.6.1.1.c) O Agni, we envelop thee with the girdle of the ocean; be thou purifying and auspicious unto us.
(4.6.1.1ḍ) With the caul of the snow, O Agni, we envelop you; be purifying and auspicious for us.

(4.6.1.1.e) Upon the earth, upon the reed, most easily accessible among the rivers—O Agni, you are the bile of the waters. (4.6.1.2) Upon the earth, upon the reed, most easily accessible among the rivers—O Agni, you are the bile of the waters.
O Maṇḍūkī, come hither with them; make this sacrifice of ours pure-colored and auspicious.
The purifier, with his longing gaze, has shone upon the earth like the radiance of the dawn.
(4.6.1.2) Like one who overcomes on his course, like Etaśa in his joy—[he is] he who, like one parched by heat, is ageless.
O Agni, purifier, with your radiance and your pleasant tongue, O god, bring the gods hither and worship them.
(4.6.1.3.k) O purifying, radiant Agni, bring the gods here to us, to our sacrifice and our oblation.
(4.6.1.3ḷ) This is the gathering place of the waters, the dwelling of the ocean. May your missiles burn others than us; O Purifier, be auspicious toward us.
(4.6.1.3ṃ) Homage to your heat, to your flame; homage be to your radiance! Let your missiles consume others than us; O Purifier, be auspicious unto us!
To him who sits among men, vaṭ! To him who sits in the waters, vaṭ! To him who sits in the forest, vaṭ! To him who sits on the sacrificial grass, vaṭ! To him who has found the light of heaven, vaṭ!

(4.6.1.4.o) O gods who are worthy of sacrifice among the gods, who are worthy of sacrifice among those worthy of sacrifice, you who sit for your annual portion—though you do not eat the oblation, at this sacrifice of mine, offer yourselves of the honey and the clarified butter.

Those gods who attained godhead among the gods, who are the precursors of this Brahman, and without whom no domain whatsoever is purified—they are neither upon the ridges of heaven nor upon those of earth.

May your missiles burn another than us; O Purifier, be auspicious unto us! (4.6.1.5) Giver of breath, giver of out
May Agni with his sharp flame strike down every devouring demon; may Agni win wealth for us.

With this victorious army, may he be well-disposed toward us—the sacrificer who best worships the gods for our well-being. O Agni, shine forth with splendor and wealth, you who are the undeceived guardian and our protector from afar.
(4.6.2.1.a) That seer, our father, who sat down as the Hotṛ-priest offering up all these worlds—he, seeking wealth through his prayer, entered the highest, most excellent dwelling-place.

(4.6.2.1.b) When Viśvakarman, the far-reaching creator and ordainer, the supreme beholder, [acts] with his mind, their desires rejoice together in nourishment where they say there is one beyond the seven seers.

(4.6.2.1.c) He who is our father, our progenitor, he who is the ordainer; he who, being himself existent, has brought us forth from existence. (4.6.2.2) He alone is the one who bestows names upon the gods; toward him all other worlds go for counsel.

(4.6.2.2ḍ) The ancient seers, like singers in great number, offered up wealth for him; they who, unmanifested and yet manifested, in the measuring out of the mid-world, brought these beings into existence.

(4.6.2.2.e) You do not know him who generated this [world]; something else shall lie between you [and him]. Enveloped by mist and idle chatter, the reciters of hymns wander about, satisfied with the breath of life.
Beyond the sky, beyond this earth, beyond the gods and the Asuras, that which is hidden in the secret cave—what first embryo did the waters conceive, wherein all the gods came together?
(4.6.2.3.g) The waters first received that embryo wherein all the gods came together; it was placed upon the navel of the Unborn, in which this entire world is supported.

(4.6.2.3) For Viśvakarman was born as a god; then he became a Gandharva as the second; the third was the father who generated the plants. (4.6.2.4) He distributed the embryo of the waters in many places.
The Father of the eye, wise in his mind, generated these two bowing worlds as clarified butter; when their former boundaries were made firm, then indeed heaven and earth spread themselves out.
(4.6.2.4.k) With eyes on every side and faces on every side, with hands on every side and feet on every side, the one God, generating heaven and earth, stretches them out with his arms and wings.

(4.6.2.4ḷ) What was the foundation? What was the starting point? What indeed was it that existed? When Viśvakarman, creating the earth, spread out the sky with his majesty, he who is all-seeing. (4.6.2.5)
(4.6.2.5ṃ) What was the wood, and what was that tree, from which they fashioned heaven and earth? O wise ones, ask this with your mind: upon what did he stand while supporting the worlds?

(4.6.2.5ṇ) Those abodes of yours which are highest, those which are lowest, and those which are intermediate, O Viśvakarman—teach them to your friends at this oblation, O self-dependent one; worship yourself, taking pleasure in your own body.

(4.6.2.5.o) We invoke today for our aid Viśvakarman, the Lord of Speech, who is yoked by the mind, in this contest for booty. May he, the benefactor of all, whose deeds are righteous, take pleasure in our nearest invocations and grant us protection.
O Viśvakarman, strengthened by the oblation, sacrifice to yourself, taking pleasure in your own body; let other rivals around us be confounded, and here let the bountiful patron be ours.

(4.6.2.6.q) O Viśvakarman, by means of the strengthening oblation, you made Indra a protector who is invincible; to him the ancient tribes bowed down, so that he might be this formidable one, worthy of invocation.
(4.6.2.6ṛ) Homage to the ocean, the one who knows the way, the lord of the rivers! To Viśvakarman, the father of all rivers, offer the oblation day by day—the immortal oblation.
(4.6.3.1.a) Lead him upward, O Agni, offered with clarified butter; unite him with the increase of wealth, with progeny, and with riches.
(4.6.3.1.b) O Indra, make this man preeminent; let him be the controller of his kinsmen. Endow him with splendor; let him be a distributor of portions to the gods.
(4.6.3.1.c) O Agni, cause him to prosper in whose house we prepare the oblation; for him may the gods speak in favor, as well as this Brahmaṇaspati.
(4.6.3.1ḍ) May all the gods lift thee up, O Agni, with their thoughts. Be thou most auspicious to us, fair of aspect, rich in light.
(4.6.3.2.e) May the five divine quarters protect the sacrifice, O goddesses, driving away ignorance and ill-will, bestowing upon the lord of the sacrifice an abundance of wealth.

(4.6.3.2.f) The sacrifice has been established for the increase of wealth, magnified upon the kindled fire; winged with hymns, worthy of praise, and grasped, they offered the oblation, having taken hold of the heated *gharma*.

(4.6.3.2.g) When the gods, through vigor, completed the sacrifice for the divine sustainer who delights in it—the one honored by the gods, possessed of glory, and possessing a hundredfold strength—(4.6.3.3) the gods, having taken hold of the sacrifice, approached it.
(4.6.3.3) Savitar, with rays like the sun and golden hair, has raised up his eternal light from the east. Pūṣan, the divine guardian, follows his impulsion, beholding all beings.

The gods stood ready as priests for the gods; let the immolator prepare the victim for the immolator to sacrifice. Where the fourth sacrifice goes with the oblation, from there may the purifying blessings enjoy us.

(4.6.3.3.k) This celestial chariot sits in the midst of heaven, having filled the two worlds and the intermediate space. He looks upon all the butter-dripping [regions] between the eastern and the western sign.

The bull, the ocean, the ruddy one with beautiful wings, has entered the womb of the ancient father. Set in the midst of heaven as a speckled stone, he has strode forth; he guards the two ends of the region.
(4.6.3.4ṃ) All songs have magnified Indra, who is as expansive as the ocean, the best of charioteers among charioteers, the lord of spoils, the protector of the virtuous.
(4.6.3.4ṇ) May the sacrifice, invoking favor, bring the gods hither; may the god Agni perform the sacrifice and bring the gods hither.
(4.6.3.4.o) By the impulse of strength, with the upward-grasp, he has grasped me up; then Indra, by the downward-grasp, has made my rivals low.
The gods have increased the sacred word, both the uplifting and the pressing down; then may Indra and Agni scatter my rivals in all directions.
Swift, sharpening his weapons like a bull eager for combat, the striker, the shaker of the people, the loud-voiced, the unblinking, the sole hero—Indra has conquered a hundred armies at once.

With Indra—the one who thunders, the unblinking, the victorious, the one who stirs up battle, the one from whom the wicked cannot fall, the bold—conquer and prevail in the fight, O men, with that bull who holds arrows in his hand.

(4.6.4.1.c) He, with his bowmen and those bearing quivers, with his axe-wielding host, is Indra who mingles in battle; he is the conqueror in conflict, the drinker of Soma, strong of arm, with his bow uplifted, a shooter with well-aimed arrows.
(4.6.4.1ḍ) O Bṛhaspati, fly around with your chariot, slayer of demons, driving away our enemies; shattering the armies, crushing them in battle and conquering, be the protector of our chariots!

(4.6.4.2.e) Him who pierces the enclosure, the winner of cattle, whose arms are like thunderbolts, who conquers the racecourse and crushes with his might—O kinsmen, follow him in valor! O friends, rally behind Indra!

(4.6.4.2.f) O Indra, discoverer of strength, ancient one, pre-eminent hero, powerful, vigorous, victorious, fierce, superior hero, superior warrior, born of might, winner of cattle—ascend your victorious chariot!

(4.6.4.2.g) Penetrating the cow-pens with might, the irresistible hero Indra, whose wrath is a hundredfold, who is difficult to shake, the subduer of armies, and the invincible—may he protect our hosts in the battles.
(4.6.4.3) May Indra be their leader; may Bṛhaspati, the sacrificial fee, the sacrifice, and Soma go before them. Let the Maruts march at the head of the divine armies as they shatter and conquer.
The fierce roar of the gods has arisen—the host of Indra the bull, of King Varuṇa, of the Ādityas, and of the Maruts; the high-minded ones who cause the worlds to tremble, the victorious deities.
(4.6.4.3.k) May Indra be on our side when the banners meet; may those arrows which are ours be victorious! (4.6.4.4) May our heroes be superior; O gods, protect us in our invocations!
(4.6.4.4ḷ) Sharpen the weapons, O Maghavan; heighten the might of my warriors. O slayer of Vṛtra, raise up the vigor of the steeds; let the roar of the conquering chariots go forth.
(4.6.4.4ṃ) Come forward, conquer, O heroes! May your arms be firm; may Indra grant you protection so that you shall be invincible.
(4.6.4.4ṇ) Loosed, fly away, O arrow, sharpened by the sacred word (*brahman*). Go to the enemies; enter them! Let not one of them remain.
(4.6.4.5.o) I cover your vital organs with armor; may King Soma clothe you with immortality. May there be for you a wider space than the wide; may the gods rejoice after you as you conquer.
Where the arrows fly together like boys with shorn hair, there may Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, grant us protection for all days.

(4.6.5.1.a) Go forward along the eastern direction, O Agni, as one who knows; be here the foremost fire of Agni. Shining forth, illumine all the quarters; bestow strength upon our bipeds and quadrupeds.
(4.6.5.1.b) Step forward with Agni toward the vault of heaven, bearing the fire-pan in your hands; having gone to the ridge of heaven and to the light of the sun, join yourselves with the gods.

(4.6.5.1.c) From the earth I have ascended to the intermediate space; from the intermediate space I have ascended to heaven. From the back of the firmament of heaven, I have gone to the light of *suvar*. (4.6.5.2) I.
Going to the light of heaven, they look not back; they ascend to the sky, to the two worlds, those who, being well-knowing, have spread out the sacrifice that flows in every direction.

(4.6.5.2.e) O Agni, go forth as the first of those seeking the gods, the eye of both gods and mortals. May the sacrificers, desiring to sacrifice in harmony with the Bhr̥gus, go safely to the heavenly light.

Night and Dawn, of one mind yet different forms, meeting together suckle the single infant; between heaven and earth the golden disk shines forth; the gods, the givers of wealth, have maintained Agni.
(4.6.5.2.g) O Agni, thousand-eyed, hundred-headed! A hundred are your out-breaths, a thousand your in-breaths. You are the lord of thousandfold wealth; to you, for that strength, we pay homage—svāhā!

(4.6.5.3) You are the fair-winged Garuḍa; sit upon the earth! Sit upon the back of the earth! Fill the intermediate space with your luster! Prop up the sky with your light! Strengthen the quarters with your splendor!
(4.6.5.3.i) Being invoked, fair-faced Agni, sit upon your own womb in the east, O Sādhya; together with all the gods and the sacrificer, sit down in this higher common dwelling-place.
(4.6.5.4.k) O Agni, blaze forth, kindled before us with an unfailing beam, O youngest one! To you, all sacrificial strengths ever approach.

(4.6.5.4ḷ) We would worship you in your highest birth, O Agni; we would worship with hymns in your lower dwelling-place. From whatever womb you have arisen, I sacrifice to that; into you, when well-kindled, they have poured the oblations.
(4.6.5.4) Of that desirable Savitṛ, I choose the wondrous, all-beneficent favor, which Kaṇva milked from him—the swelling, thousand-streamed one. (4.6.5.5) [I choose] the great cow with her milk.

Seven are your fuel-sticks, O Agni, seven your tongues, seven the seers, and seven your beloved abodes; with seven priestly offices they worship you in seven ways—fill the seven wombs with clarified butter.
Such-like and other-like, this-like and counter-like, measured and commensurate, and bringing together;
bright-lighted and variegated-lighted, true-lighted and luminous, truthful, guardian of the Ṛta, and beyond distress.
(4.6.5.6.q) The troop consisting of Ṛtajit, Satyajit, Senajit, Suṣeṇa, Antyamitra, and Dūreamitra;
(4.6.5.6ṛ) Ṛta, Satya, Dhruva, Dharuṇa, Dhartṛ, Vidhartṛ, and Vidhārayas;
(4.6.5.6ṣ) such as you are, so like you are, come hither to us—ye who are alike and ye who are corresponding!
(4.6.5.6ṭ) May the measured ones and the well-measured ones, the Maruts who bring together [the spoils], be for our protection at this sacrifice.
(4.6.5.6.u) As the divine hosts, the Maruts, follow after Indra, so may the divine and human hosts follow after this sacrificer.

(4.6.6.1.a) Like the appearance of a rain-cloud is his countenance when the armored warrior goes into the lap of battle. With an uninjured body, may you be victorious; may the greatness of this armor protect you.

(4.6.6.1.b) With the bow may we win cattle; with the bow may we win the battle; with the bow may we conquer fierce adversaries. The bow brings about the retreat of the enemy; with the bow may we conquer all the quarters.

(4.6.6.1.c) As if about to speak, she comes close to the ear, embracing her dear friend; like a woman, she twangs from the stretched bowstring. (4.6.6.2) This is the bowstring, which carries one across in the encounter.

(4.6.6.2ḍ) Moving together like a young woman, may they bear [the arrow] in their lap like a mother her son; acting in concert, may these two bow-ends, quivering apart, pierce the enemies and the foes.

(4.6.6.2.e) The father of many, he has many sons; he makes a whizzing sound when he enters the fray. The quiver, fastened upon the back, conquers all encounters and all armies when it is set in motion.
(4.6.6.2.f) Standing on the chariot, the skillful charioteer leads the swift horses forward wherever he desires. Behold the greatness of the reins! The traces follow behind the mind.

(4.6.6.3.g) Making loud noises, the horses with strong hooves, striving for prize-winning speed together with the chariots, trampling the enemies with their forefeet, destroy the foes without retreating.
(4.6.6.3) The chariot-stand is his oblation by name, wherein his weapons and his armor are laid; there let us sit upon the strong chariot, always well-disposed in mind.

The Fathers who sit at the sweet draught, bestowers of vitality, dwelling in hardship, powerful, profound; possessing wondrous armies, strong with arrows, unfailing, truly heroic, vast, and conquerors of hosts.

(4.6.6.3.k) O Brāhmaṇas! (4.6.6.4) O Fathers worthy of Soma! May Heaven and Earth, the auspicious and faultless, be gracious to us. May Pūṣan protect us from misfortune, O increasers of Truth! Guard us; let no malevolent one have power over us.
She clothes herself in an eagle’s plumage; her tooth is a deer; bound with cow-hides, she flies forth when discharged. Where men run together and apart, there may the arrows grant us protection.
(4.6.6.4) O thou of straight course, spare us; let our body be as stone. May Soma speak for us, and may Aditi grant us protection. (4.6.6.5) May she extend her shelter over us.
(4.6.6.5ṇ) They strike their backs; they beat upon their haunches. O horse-whip, you who are full of wisdom, urge the horses on in the battles!
Like a serpent with its coils, it encircles the arm, warding off the strike of the bowstring; the hand-guard, knowing all the secret ways, as a man, shall protect the man from every side.
O Lord of the Forest, may you be firm-limbed, our friend, a furtherer, and a possessor of noble heroes; you are bound with cow-hides, so be strong—may your rider win all that is to be won.

(4.6.6.5.q) From heaven and from earth, strength has been uplifted; from the trees, power has been brought together. With an oblation, worship the chariot—the vigor of the waters, encompassed by cattle, the thunderbolt of Indra.
The thunderbolt of Indra, the vanguard of the Maruts, the offspring of Mitra, and the navel of Varuṇa—O divine chariot, enjoying this our offering of oblations, accept these gifts.

(4.6.6.6ṣ) Make the earth and the sky resound; let the world scattered in many places take heed of you. O drum, in harmony with Indra and the gods, drive the enemies far, even to the furthest distance! (4.6.6.7) Drive the enemies far, even to the furthest distance!
(4.6.6.7ṭ) Roar forth strength; bestow vigor upon us! Thunder, driving away misfortunes! O drum, blow away calamities from here! You are Indra’s fist; be firm!
(4.6.6.7.u) Drive those away and bring these back; the drum resounds with a signal. Our heroes, winged by horses, advance together; O Indra, may our chariot-warriors be victorious!
When you first neighed at birth, rising from the ocean or from the primordial waters, with the wings of a falcon and the forelegs of an antelope—O steed, your great birth is worthy of praise.
(4.6.7.1.b) Yama gave him; Trita harnessed him; Indra was the first to mount him. The Gandharva grasped his bridle; O Vasus, you fashioned the horse from the sun.
(4.6.7.1.c) You are Yama; you are Āditya, O steed; you are Trita by means of a secret vow. You are separated from Soma by an interval. (4.6.7.2) They say that you have three bonds in heaven.
(4.6.7.2ḍ) They say you have three bonds in heaven, three in the waters, and three within the ocean. O steed, you appear to me like Varuṇa himself, where they say is your highest place of birth.
(4.6.7.2.e) These, O steed, are your grooming-cloths; these are the places where the hooves of the winner are set down. Here I beheld your auspicious reins, which the guardians of *ṛta* protect.
(4.6.7.2.f) I recognized your self from afar with my mind, flying down from heaven like a winged bird. (4.6.7.3) I saw your head, the winged one, speeding along easy paths that are free of dust.

(4.6.7.3.g) Here I beheld your supreme form, striving to win nourishment at the station of the cow. When the mortal has attained his enjoyment from you, then, as the most voracious eater, you have awakened the plants.

(4.6.7.3) After thee, O steed, has come the chariot; after thee, the young bridegroom; after thee, the cattle; after thee, the fortune of maidens; after thee, the throngs have sought thy friendship; after thee, the gods have measured out their heroic power. (4.6.7.4) They...

(4.6.7.4.i) Golden-horned, his feet are iron; Indra was the swiftest in spirit among those who followed him. The gods themselves came to partake of the sacrificial food of him who was the first to mount the steed.
(4.6.7.4.k) With rounded flanks and slender waists, the divine coursers, like heroes, rush together; like swans they draw up in rows when the horses have reached the celestial racecourse.
(4.6.7.4ḷ) O steed, thy body is winged; thy mind is swift-gliding like the wind. Thy horns are spread abroad in many places; they move flickeringly in the forests.

(4.6.7.4) The steed, the prize-winner, has come forward to the command, meditating with a mind directed toward the gods. The goat, his kinship, is led before him; behind him follow the sages and the singers. (4.6.7.5) Upa... (4.6.7.5) The steed, the prize-winner, has come forward to the command, meditating with a mind directed toward the gods. The goat, his kinship
He has approached the highest dwelling place, hither toward his father and mother; for today he shall go to the gods as the most beloved, and then he prays for desirable boons for the donor.

(4.6.8.1.a) May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aryaman, Āyu, Indra, Ṛbhukṣan, and the Maruts not look with disfavor upon us, as we proclaim in the assembly the heroic deeds of the prize-winning steed, born of the gods.
When they lead before him the seized gift of the ram covered with woolly fleece and wealth, the bleating goat of all forms goes straight forward to the beloved path of Indra and Pūṣan.

(4.6.8.1.c) This goat, the portion of Pūṣan, belonging to all the gods, is led forward before the vigorous horse. When Tvaṣṭṛ [prepares] this beloved sacrificial cake for the steed, he quickens it for the sake of high renown.

(4.6.8.2ḍ) When men lead the horse three times around the path to the gods, which is fit for oblation and seasonal, then the first portion goes to Pūṣan—the goat, announcing the sacrifice to the gods.
(4.6.8.2.e) The Hotṛ, the Adhvaryu, the Āvayāj, the Agnimindha, the Grāvagrābha, and the wise Śaṃstṛ—with this well-prepared, well-offered sacrifice, fill full the bellies [of the gods].

May the approval of those who hew the sacrificial post, those who carry the post, those who carve the top-ring for the horse’s post, and those who prepare the cooking-vessel for the steed, likewise further us.

(4.6.8.3.g) He has come near; my prayer has been well-placed toward the regions of the gods, he whose back is smooth. The wise seers rejoice after him; for the prosperity of the gods, we have made him our good kinsman.
Whatever halter binds the prize-winning steed, whatever head-stall or rope belongs to him, or whatever grass has been placed in his mouth as fodder—may all those things of yours be among the gods.

Whatever of the horse’s raw flesh the fly has eaten, or whatever is smeared upon the sacrificial post or the axe, whatever is on the hands of the slaughterer or on his nails—may all that of yours be among the gods.

(4.6.8.4.k) Whatever undigested contents of the belly escape, whatever odor of raw flesh there is—let the immolators make that well-prepared, and let them cook the sacrificial meat until it is thoroughly cooked.

Whatever from your body, as it is being cooked by the fire, drips down when you have been impaled on the spit—let that not rest upon the earth, nor upon the grass; let it be offered to the longing gods.
(4.6.9.1.a) May the approval of those who look upon the horse as cooked, of those who say, "It smells good, take it out," and of those who wait for a portion of the steed's meat, further us.
The probe for the meat-cooking cauldron, the vessels for pouring the broth, the warming lids for the cooking pots, the hooks, and the carving-boards—all these attend upon the horse.
(4.6.9.1.c) Your stepping forth, your sitting down, your rolling over, and the foot-fetter of the steed; that which you drank and that which you ate as fodder—may all those of yours be with the gods.

(4.6.9.2ḍ) May the smoke-scented fire not make you crackle; may the glowing cauldron not break and consume you. The gods accept that horse which has been sacrificed, enjoyed, approved, and consecrated with the *vaṣaṭ* call.
The garment they spread beneath the horse, the upper-robe, the golden ornaments, the halter, the foot-rope, and the fetters—these dear things they offer among the gods.

Whatever of yours was pained by the heel or by the whip when you were spurred on with great force while galloping—just as one offers oblations with a ladle at the sacrifices, all those [pains] of yours I soothe with a sacred prayer (*brahman*).

(4.6.9.3.g) The axe meets the thirty-four ribs of the horse, the swift steed of the divine kin. Make the limbs free from flaw according to the sacred rules; having made a sound joint by joint, dissect [the body] along the joints.
(4.6.9.3) One is the dissector of Tvaṣṭṛ’s horse; two are the restrainers, and so is the season. Those of thy limbs which I prepare in due order, those I offer as balls of meat into the fire.

(4.6.9.3.i) May it not burn you; may your dear self not suffer as you enter [the fire]. May the axe not leave a mark upon your body. May the greedy, unskillful carver, passing over the joints, not mangle your limbs with the knife.

(4.6.9.4.k) Indeed, you do not die here, nor are you harmed; you go to the gods by easy paths. Your two bay horses and the two spotted mares have become your yoke-mates; the vigorous steed has taken its place at the pole of the donkey’s cart.

May the prize-winning steed grant us abundance in cattle, abundance in horses, heroic sons, and all-sustaining wealth; may Aditi grant us sinlessness, and may the horse, accompanied by our oblation, win for us sovereign power.
O Agni and Viṣṇu, being of one accord, may these songs increase you both; come hither with splendors and with strengths.

(4.7.1.1.b) And may for me *vāja* (strength), and *prasava* (procreation), and *prayati* (striving), and *prasiti* (extension), and *dhīti* (insight), and *kratu* (will), and *svara* (tone), and *śloka* (fame), and *śrāva* (hearing), and *śruti* (revelation), and *jyotis* (light), and *suva* (impulse), and *prāṇa* (out-breath), and *apāna* (in-breath), and *vyāna* (diffused breath), and *asu* (vitality), and *citta* (thought), and *ādhīta* (meditation), and *vāk* (speech), and *manas* (mind), and *cakṣus* (eye), and *śrotra* (ear), and *dakṣa* (skill), and *bala* (power), and *ojas* (vigor).
And my strength, and my life-span, and my old age, and my self, and my body, and my shelter, and my armor, and my limbs, and my bones, and my joints, and my members.

(4.7.2.1) Preeminence and my overlordship; my spirit of wrath and my brilliance; my luster and my water; my victory and my greatness; my breadth and my width; my height and my length; my growth and my increase; my truth and my faith; and my world. (4.7.2.2) My wealth and my power; my radiance and my play; my joy and my delight; my born and my yet to be born.

May my hymn be successful and my good deed be successful; may my wealth be successful and my object of knowledge be successful; may my past be successful and my future be successful; may my easy path be successful and my fair path be successful; may my prosperity be successful and my attainment be successful; may my mental resolve be successful and my benevolent intent be successful.

(4.7.3.1) May welfare be mine, and joy be mine, and what is dear be mine, and my desire be fulfilled, and may my wish be granted, and mental composure be mine, and prosperity be mine, and excellence be mine, and well-being be mine, and glory be mine, and fortune be mine, and wealth be mine; may the restrainer be mine, and the sustainer be mine, and security be mine, and steadfastness be mine, and the All be mine. (4.7.3.2) May greatness be mine, and consciousness be mine, and the power of discernment be mine, and procreation be mine, and prolificity be mine, and the plough be mine, and the furrow be mine, and cosmic order be mine, and immortality be mine.

And may there be freedom from consumption for me, and freedom from disease for me, and vitality for me, and long life for me, and absence of enemies for me, and fearlessness for me, and a good path for me, and a comfortable bed for me, and easy childbirth for me, and a fair day for me.

(4.7.4.1) May my vigor and my pleasant truth, my milk and my sap, my clarified butter and my honey, my feast and my banquet, my agriculture and my rain, my victory and my triumph, my wealth and my riches, my prosperity and my growth, my pervasiveness and my power, my muchness and my abundance, my fullness and my fuller measure, my imperishability and my grain-wealth, and my food be mine.

May hunger be mine, and rice be mine, and barley be mine, and beans be mine, and sesame be mine, and mung beans be mine, and lentils be mine, and wheat be mine, and peas be mine, and millet be mine, and fine grains be mine, and *śyāmāka* be mine, and wild rice be mine.

(4.7.5.1) May my stone and my clay, my hills and my mountains, my sands and my trees, my gold and my iron, my lead and my tin, my black metal and my copper, my fire and my waters, my creepers and my herbs, my grain ripening in cultivated fields and my grain ripening in uncultivated lands, and my domestic animals and my wild animals be perfected through sacrifice.

(4.7.5.2) May there be for me wealth and the acquisition of wealth; may there be for me what has been and prosperity; may there be for me riches and an abode; may there be for me action and power; may there be for me purpose and approach; may there be for me attainment and the goal.
(4.7.6.1) May Agni and Indra be mine;
(4.7.6.1) may Soma and Indra be mine;
(4.7.6.1) may Savitṛ and Indra be mine.
(4.7.6.1) May Sarasvatī and Indra be mine;
(4.7.6.1) may Pūṣan and Indra be mine;
(4.7.6.1) may Bṛhaspati and Indra be mine.
(4.7.6.1) And Mitra for me, and Indra for me; (4.7.6.1) and Varuṇa for me, and Indra for me;
(4.7.6.1–2) and Tvaṣṭṛ for me, and Indra for me.
May Dhātṛ and Indra be mine;
may Viṣṇu and Indra be mine;
may the Aśvins and Indra be mine.
(4.7.6.2) And the Maruts for me, and Indra for me; (4.7.6.2) and the Viśve Devas for me, and Indra for me; (4.7.6.2) and the Earth for me, and Indra for me.
(4.7.6.2) May the intermediate space and Indra be mine;
(4.7.6.2) may the sky and Indra be mine;
(4.7.6.2) may the quarters and Indra be mine.
May Mūrdhan and Indra be mine;
may Prajāpati and Indra be mine.

(4.7.7.1) And my Aṃśu, and my Raśmi, and my Adābhya, and my Adhipati, and my Upāṃśu, and my Antaryāma, and my Aindravāyava, and my Maitrāvaruṇa, and my Āśvina, and my Pratiprasthāna, and my Śukra, and my Manthin, and my Āgrayaṇa, and my Vaiśvadeva, and my Dhruva, and my Vaiśvānara, and my Ṛtugrahas, and my Atigrāhyas, and my Aindrāgna, and my Vaiśvadeva.

And may the Marutvatīya be mine, and the Mahendra be mine, and the Āditya be mine, and the Sāvitra be mine, and the Sārasvata be mine, and the Pauṣṇa be mine, and the Pātnīvata be mine, and the Hāriyojana be mine.

(4.7.8.1) My fuel and my sacrificial grass and my altar and my hearths and my offering-ladles and my cups and my pressing-stones and my sacrificial posts and my sounding-holes and my two pressing-boards and my wooden trough and my Vāyu-cups and my *pūtabhṛt* vessel and my *ādhavanīya* vessel and my *āgnīdhra* shed and my oblation-holder and my houses and my assembly hall and my sacrificial cakes and my cooks and my purificatory bath and my cry of "Svaga!"—may these be mine.

(4.7.9.1) May my Agni and my Gharma, my Arka and my Sūrya, my Prāṇa and my Aśvamedha, my Pṛthivī and my Aditi, my Diti and my Dyau, and my fingers—the Śakvarīs—and the quarters be perfected through the sacrifice.
(4.7.9.1) May my Ṛc and my Sāman, my Stoma and my Yajus, my Dīkṣā and my Tapas, my Ṛtu and my Vrata, and my Bṛhat and Rathantara through the rain of day and night be perfected through the sacrifice.
(4.7.10.1) My embryos and my calves; (4.7.10.1) my three-year-old male goat and my three-year-old female goat; (4.7.10.1) my two-year-old bull and my two-year-old cow.
(4.7.10.1) And my five-year-old bull, and my five-year-old cow; (4.7.10.1) and my three-year-old bull, and my three-year-old cow;
(4.7.10.1) and my four-year-old draught-ox, and my four-year-old draught-cow.
(4.7.10.1) And my four-year-old bull and my four-year-old cow;
(4.7.10.1) and my ox and my barren cow; (4.7.10.1) and my bull and (4.7.10.2) my heifer, and my draft-ox and my milch-cow.
(4.7.10.2) May life be perfected through sacrifice; (4.7.10.2) may the out-breath be perfected through sacrifice; (4.7.10.2) may the in-breath be perfected through sacrifice.
May the pervasive breath (vyāna) be perfected through the sacrifice; may the eye be perfected through the sacrifice;
may the ear be perfected through the sacrifice.
(4.7.10.2) May the mind be perfected through sacrifice;
(4.7.10.2) may speech be perfected through sacrifice; (4.7.10.2) may the self be perfected through sacrifice.
May the sacrifice be perfected by the sacrifice.

(4.7.11.1.a) One for me, and three for me, and five for me, and seven for me, and nine for me, and eleven for me, and thirteen for me, and fifteen for me, and seventeen for me, and nineteen for me, and twenty-one for me, and twenty-three for me, and twenty-five for me, and twenty-seven for me, and twenty-nine for me, and thirty-one for me, and thirty-three for me. (4.7.11.2) For me.
(4.7.11.2.b) Four and eight and twelve and sixteen and twenty and twenty-four and twenty-eight and thirty-two and thirty-six and forty and forty-four and forty-eight and my [forty-eight].
(4.7.11.2.c) Vāja and Prasava and Āpija and Kratu and Suva and Mūrdhan and Vyaśniya and Antyāyana and Antya and Bhauvana and Bhuvana and Adhipati.
May Vāja protect us from the seven directions or from the four distant realms; may Vāja, together with all the gods, protect us here in the winning of wealth.
(4.7.12.1.b) May all the Maruts come today with every aid; may all the fires be well-kindled. May all the gods come to us with protection; may all wealth and strength be ours.
O gods, come with your golden chariots to the impulse of strength—to drink the Soma—Agni, Indra, Bṛhaspati, and the Maruts.

(4.7.12.1ḍ) O ye who possess the prize, protect us in every contest for booty! (4.7.12.2) O wise, immortal ones, knowers of the Eternal Order, drink of this honeyed mead and rejoice; being satisfied, go by the paths traveled by the gods.
May *vāja* be before us and in our midst; may *vāja* arrange the gods according to the seasons. For the impulse of *vāja* bends everything down; may I become a lord of *vāja* in all directions.
Milk is on the earth, milk is in the plants, milk is in heaven, and milk is established in the intermediate space. May the quarters of the sky be full of milk for me.
(4.7.12.2.g) I unite myself with milk and ghee; I unite myself with the waters and the plants. As such, O Agni, may I win strength.
Night and Dawn, of one mind yet different forms, moving together, suckle the single infant. Between heaven and earth the golden disk shines; the gods, bestowers of wealth, have sustained Agni.

(4.7.12.3.i) You are the ocean, possessing mist, bestowing moisture; you are the source of well-being, the source of bliss—bear toward me [the oblation], svāhā! You are the Marut, the host of the Maruts; you are the source of well-being, the source of bliss—bear toward me [the oblation], svāhā! You are the seeker of aid, the recipient of worship; you are the source of well-being, the source of bliss—bear toward me [the oblation], svāhā!
(4.7.13.1.a) I yoke Agni with power and with ghee—the celestial, well-winged one, great in vigor. With him may we fly to the realm of the sun, ascending to heaven upon the highest firmament.

(4.7.13.1.b) These two wings of yours, O Agni, are unaging and feathered, with which you strike away the demons. With them may we fly to the world of the doers of good deeds, where the seers are who were first-born in ancient times.

(4.7.13.1.c) You are consciousness; you have the ocean as your source; you are the drop, the skillful one, the falcon, the observer of cosmic order; you are the golden-winged bird, the swift mover, the great one, firm in your station. (4.7.13.2) You are seated here.
Homage be to you; do not harm me. You stand supported upon the head of the universe. Your heart is within the ocean, your life-span is in heaven and earth, placed among all beings.

(4.7.13.2.e) Give us water; split open the ocean! From the sky, from Parjanya, from the intermediate space, and from the earth—therefrom favor us with rain. You are the head of heaven, the navel of the earth, the strength of the waters and of the plants. You are all-encompassing life, a far-reaching refuge; homage to the path!

(4.7.13.2.f) With that sacrificial session which the seers performed through austerity, kindling the fire while bringing forth the light of heaven—into that vault of heaven I place this fire, which men call the one for whom the sacred grass is strewn.

(4.7.13.3.g) O gods, may we follow him with our wives, with sons, with brothers, or even with gold; grasping the firmament in the world of good deeds, upon the third ridge in the luminous realm of heaven.

(4.7.13.3) The restless one has ascended to the midst of speech; this Agni, the lord of the virtuous, is far-seeing. Established upon the back of the earth, he flashes brilliantly and casts those who would attack him beneath his feet. (4.7.13.4) Those who seek to fight against us...

(4.7.13.4.i) May this Agni, the most heroic, the bestower of vigor, shining with a thousandfold brilliance and never flagging, blaze forth; resplendent in the midst of the flood, he shall approach the celestial abodes.
(4.7.13.4.k) Move forward together; follow along, proceed! O Agni, prepare the paths that lead to the gods. In this highest common dwelling-place, may all the gods and the sacrificer sit down.
O Agni, by that [path] by which you carry a thousand, by which you carry all wealth—by that path, carry this sacrifice of ours, which is the highest, leading to the gods.

(4.7.13.5ṃ) Wake up, O Agni; be watchful for him. Unite this man with the merit of his sacrifices and pious works. Making you a youthful father once again, he has followed after and taken up this thread within you.
This is your seasonal birthplace, from which, once born, you shone forth; knowing it, O Agni, ascend it, and then increase our wealth.

(4.7.14.1.a) O Agni, may splendor be mine in our invocations; kindling thee, may we nourish our bodies. May the four quarters bow down to me; with thee as our overseer, may we conquer the hostile armies.
(4.7.14.1.b) May all the gods be present at my invocation—Indra’s followers, the Maruts, Viṣṇu, and Agni. May the wide mid-region be my protector; may Vāta blow for me in this desire.

(4.7.14.1.c) May the gods bestow wealth upon me; may the blessing be mine, and mine the invocation of the gods. May the two divine Hotṛ-priests grant us gain, so that we, with our bodies, may be well-provided with heroes through the sacrifices performed yesterday.
(4.7.14.2ḍ) Let them sacrifice for me; let my oblations be mine. May the intention of my mind be true. May I not fall into any sin whatsoever. O All-Gods, speak in my favor!

O divine six wide ones, grant us wide space; O all you gods, display your heroism here! May we not be abandoned by our offspring nor by our bodies; may we not fall into the power of the enemy, O King Soma.
May Agni, repelling fury from the front, protect us on every side as an undeceivable guardian. Let the secret plotters turn back again; let their consciousness perish when they awaken.

May Dhātṛ, the ordainer of ordainers, who is the lord of the world, and the god Savitṛ, the overcomer of adversaries; may both Aśvins and Bṛhaspati—may these gods protect this sacrifice and the sacrificer from misfortune.

(4.7.14.3) May the wide-striding buffalo, invoked by many, grant us protection in this call, abounding in food. O Indra, Lord of the bay horses, be gracious to our progeny; do not harm us, nor deliver us over to destruction. (4.7.14.4) Do not injure us, do not abandon us.

(4.7.14.4.i) May those who are our rivals be driven away; with Indra and Agni we repel them. The Vasus, Rudras, and Ādityas have made me one who touches the heights, a formidable observer, and a sovereign ruler.

(4.7.14.4.k) We invoke Indra from afar, him who wins cattle, who wins wealth, and who wins horses; may he take pleasure in this our sacrifice at this invocation. O Lord of Bay Steeds, we make you our ally in this.
(4.7.15.1.a) I meditate upon Agni, the first, the wise one, whom many kindle as the leader of the five peoples; having entered into every clan, we implore him: may he deliver us from distress.

(4.7.15.1.b) He whose this breathing, whose blinking, and whose moving is all alone, and whose born and being born [is his]—I praise Agni; seeking protection, I call upon him repeatedly: may he deliver us from distress.

(4.7.15.1.c) I meditate upon Indra, the first, the wise slayer of Vṛtra; his hymns of praise have come unto me—he who comes to the call of the donor who performs good deeds. May he deliver us from distress. (4.7.15.2) May he deliver us from distress.

(4.7.15.2ḍ) He who leads the battle, who brings the weapons together for combat, and who unites the three prosperities—I, seeking protection, call aloud upon that Indra; may he deliver us from distress.

I think of you both, O Mitra and Varuṇa; take note of that, O you whose power is truth, whom you drive away with your firm support. You who, as fierce ones, go forth on the same chariot to [punish] the king—deliver us from sin.

(4.7.15.2.f) Your chariot, with its straight reins and true laws, which approaches and destroys the one who acts deceitfully—I praise it. (4.7.15.3) Seeking protection, I invoke Mitra and Varuṇa; may those two release us from sin.

We meditate upon the ordinances of Vāyu and Savitṛ, those two who support that which possesses a self and who guard it; those two who have become the encompassers of the universe—may they both release us from sin.
(4.7.15.3) May our most excellent blessings rest upon the ordinance of the two gods. I praise Vāyu and Savitṛ; seeking protection, I call upon them repeatedly. May those two release us from sin.
